author: taylorbayouth
body:
## Summary

This branch builds the first vertical slice of the Open Recon agent engine on top of the existing extractor. Three commits:

- **Ref convention (schema 2.0)** — Every element and text node now carries a short opaque `ref` (`@e1`, `@t1`, …). A top-level `lookup` table maps each ref to its CDP `backendNodeId`. The LLM sees only refs; the executor resolves them via `lookup`. `backendNodeId` is gone from record bodies. `schemaVersion` bumped to `2.0`.
- **DESIGN.md** — Architectural source of truth for the full engine pipeline: artifact shapes, action registry, settle contract, loop semantics, provider interface, caching seams (named but not implemented), and the slice build plan.
- **Slice 1 engine** — End-to-end agent loop with Anthropic only, three verbs (`click`, `type`, `done`), happy path.

## New modules

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/actions.js` | Verb registry — single source of truth for vocab, args, and refType constraints |
| `lib/prompt.js` | System prompt builder; action vocab section auto-generated from registry |
| `lib/reduce.js` | `Brief → LLMView` — deterministic text listing + `briefHash` (caching seam) |
| `lib/validate.js` | Checks Action[] against registry + snapshot lookup; returns ok/errors, never throws |
| `lib/execute.js` | CDP dispatch (click via mouse events, type via `DOM.focus` + `insertText`); calls `session.settle()` after every action |
| `lib/plan.js` | Provider facade + `toolsFromRegistry()` |
| `lib/providers/anthropic.js` | Anthropic Messages tool-use adapter; returns `Completion` artifact |
| `lib/loop.js` | Orchestrator: extract → reduce → plan → validate → execute; builds `Run` artifact; Step → message conversion |
| `agent.js` | Smoke harness CLI (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... npm run agent -- "<task>"`) |

`Session.settle()` added to `lib/connect.js` — universal post-action wait. Slice 1 is a fixed 150 ms wait; the interface is the seam for lifecycle/AX-quiet checks later.

## What's deliberately not here

- Caching (named seams only — Anthropic prompt cache, brief diff, element resolution)
- Additional verbs (`focus`, `press`, `scroll`, `navigate`, `wait`)
- Additional providers (OpenAI, Ollama)
- Text nodes in the LLMView listing
- Brief persistence in the Run artifact
- Smarter settle (lifecycle events, AX-tree-quiet polling)

All deferred per DESIGN.md.

## How to smoke-test

```bash
npm run launch                  # Chrome on port 9222
# navigate to a page
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... npm run agent -- "click the search box and type hello, then done" --verbose
```

Output is a pretty-printed `Run` artifact on stdout. Loop turn logs on stderr with `--verbose`.

## Reviewer notes

- `lookup` is executor-only — the LLM prompt never includes it (stripped in `reduce.js`)
- `validate()` returns `{ ok, errors }` and never throws — errors are fed back into the next prompt turn, not retried automatically
- Settle after `done` is intentionally skipped — `done` exits the loop immediately
- `.claude/` is intentionally untracked (local agent memory)

### 🎨 Palette: Improve accessibility and mobile interaction

#### 💡 What
This PR implements a series of surgical micro-UX improvements focused on keyboard accessibility, screen reader support, and mobile form usability.

#### 🎯 Why
The landing page previously lacked visible focus indicators, making it difficult for keyboard users to navigate. Additionally, form fields lacked semantic labels, and mobile users were presented with a generic keyboard for phone number entry.

#### 📸 Before/After
- **Focus:** Interactive elements now exhibit a high-contrast orange (`#d40`) ring when focused via keyboard.
- **Forms:** Inputs now have associated `sr-only` labels for screen readers.
- **Mobile:** Phone field now triggers the numeric dialer.

#### ♿ Accessibility
- Implemented modern `:focus-visible` CSS pattern.
- Added visually hidden labels using the standard `.sr-only` utility.
- Converted a non-semantic `<button>` used for navigation into a proper `<a>` link.
- Added descriptive Arabic `aria-label` attributes to icon-only links and carousel controls to ensure a coherent experience for screen reader users.

author: mattwwarren
body:
## Summary

- Adds a loose fallback to `parse_stdout()` that recovers the sentinel payload from a bare code-fenced JSON block when no `<<<AUTO_DEV_RESULT>>>` markers are found (Fix A)
- Documents the loose fallback in `docs/headless-contract.md` §6 and clarifies that markers are still required from the producer (Fix B)
- Adds `TestLooseFallback` (7 tests) in `test_auto_dev_result.py` and an acceptance test in `test_wrapper.py` confirming the wrapper routes to `COMPLETED` (not `needs_attention`) on bare code-fence output

## Root cause

The worker session `eb8bf03e` (PR #334) emitted the sentinel wrapped in a `` ```json `` code fence without the `<<<AUTO_DEV_RESULT>>>` framing. `parse_stdout()` returned `BlockedResult(reason="no_result_emitted")`, the wrapper called `signal_needs_attention`, and the dispatcher saw a `BLOCKED_ON_USER` task it couldn't auto-resolve — causing a wasted re-dispatch.

## Fix

The loose fallback activates only when:
1. No `<<<AUTO_DEV_RESULT` marker exists in stdout (preserves the crash-mid-emit path unchanged)
2. A code fence is found containing valid JSON with both `schema_version` and `status` keys

A warning is logged when the fallback is used so the producer mis-emission is visible.

## Test plan

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/test_auto_dev_result.py::TestLooseFallback` — 7 new tests
- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/test_wrapper.py::TestHeadlessWrapper::test_print_bare_code_fence_routes_to_completed` — acceptance test
- [ ] Full suite: `uv run pytest tests/` — 1145 passed

Closes #337

## Summary

Core support for unified video settings: captions radio group, playback-rate radio group rename, text-track selection in the store, and popover fixes for disabled triggers and blur-dismiss inside menus. 

This also sets up the menus to rely on primitives rather than compound components. 

## Changes

- Add `CaptionsRadioGroupCore` with data attrs and tests
- Rename playback-rate menu core to `PlaybackRateRadioGroupCore` and remove legacy playback-rate-menu module
- Extend text-track store for caption track selection
- Harden popover: respect disabled triggers; avoid closing on blur from in-menu pointer gestures

## Testing

```bash
pnpm -F @videojs/core test src/core/ui/captions-radio-group src/core/ui/playback-rate-radio-group src/dom/ui/popover
```

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large player UI and text-track selection surface area with removed playback-rate-menu elements, but behavior is covered by core, DOM, and e2e tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **unified settings-style menus** for video skins (gear → Speed / Captions submenus) while moving playback rate and captions onto **generic `media-menu` + radio-group primitives** instead of dedicated playback-rate menu custom elements.

Popover logic ignores **disabled** triggers and uses a **blur guard** so in-menu pointer clicks do not dismiss popovers.

> **Tests:** New/updated unit tests for radio groups, menu items, popover focusout, and Playwright selectors/page objects for settings navigation and playback rate via `getPlaybackRate()`.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

- `"fmt %s" % obj` was incorrectly calling `obj.__rmod__("fmt %s")` and returning its result whenever `obj` defined `__rmod__`, instead of formatting `obj` as the `%s` argument.
- Root cause: `try_dunder_binary` (which tries the reflected slot) was called before the `str_printf_format` guard in `BinaryOp::Mod`.
- Fix: hoist the `str` guard above `try_dunder_binary`; when `lhs` is `str`, call `str_printf_format` immediately without consulting `__rmod__` at all.

## What Changed

`crates/pyrust/src/interpreter/runtime/expr.rs`, `BinaryOp::Mod` arm:

Before:
1. `try_dunder_binary` (finds `rhs.__rmod__`, calls it, returns early)
2. `if Str` → `str_printf_format` (never reached)

After:
1. `if Str` → `str_printf_format` (handles all `str % args` cases)
2. `try_dunder_binary` (for non-str lhs, e.g. `10 % obj`)

This matches CPython semantics: `str.__mod__` never returns `NotImplemented`, so the reflected slot on the right operand must not be consulted when `lhs` is a `str`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Repro from issue: `"hello %s" % Formatter()` where `Formatter` defines `__rmod__` returns formatted string, not `__rmod__` result.
- [ ] `str % obj` where `__rmod__` returns `NotImplemented`: formats normally, no TypeError.

author: entcheneric
body:
## Description

Optimizes XP cooldown checks in both `update_user_xp` and `update_user_xp_from_voice` by adding an in-memory cache that tracks the last XP grant time per user per guild.

### Before
- Each XP update executed a complex SQL INSERT ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE with 3 correlated subqueries (`SELECT textCooldown FROM levelConfig`) — **even when the user was still on cooldown**
- The SQL had redundant CASE branches that would still run the query, just not update the value
- The cooldown logic was buried in SQL, making it harder to maintain

### After
- Added `_last_xp_gain_cache` dict: `(guild_id, user_id) -> timestamp`
- Memory cache is checked first — if the user is still on cooldown, **no DB query is executed at all** (0 queries instead of 1)
- Cooldown value is fetched from `_get_cached_config` (already cached, 5-minute TTL), eliminating all correlated subqueries
- When cooldown has elapsed, a simple single INSERT ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE is executed
- Voice XP now properly defaults to 60 seconds (matching the DB default) instead of the hardcoded 5

### Benefits
| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| User on cooldown (text) | 1 query with 3 subqueries | **0 queries** |
| User on cooldown (voice) | 1 query with 2 subqueries | **0 queries** |
| Cooldown elapsed | 1 query with 3 subqueries | 1 simple query |

Closes #1371

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

Internal framework fix that closes a synthetic-walkthrough footgun: the manager-flow demo opens on an in_progress weekly review of an opportunity whose pipeline CSV happens to be backed by real (non-synthetic) FLWs. The seed stamps a snapshot onto that in_progress run with the narrative FLW set so the demo doesn't show the wrong data, but \`useRunView\` was ignoring stamped snapshots on in_progress runs and serving the live pipeline instead. With this fix, a stamped snapshot is always preferred — real in_progress runs are unaffected because production never stamps one.

## Technical Summary

\`commcare_connect/static/js/workflow-runner.tsx::useRunView\` previously branched on \`isCompleted && snapshot\` to decide whether to serve snapshot fields. After this change the branch is just \`snapshot\` — if it's stamped, serve it; \`isCompleted\` / \`asOf\` continue to reflect the real run status.

Per \`commcare_connect/workflow/views.py:430\` ("Snapshot is null while in_progress; populated on completion"), production runs never stamp a snapshot on an in_progress workflow. The only code path that produces one is the synthetic generator, which deliberately stashes a preview snapshot onto its backdated in_progress run. So this is a no-op for every real workflow and a fix for the synthetic case.

The chc_nutrition template's pre-existing row-source fallback chain (PR #287) already prefers \`instance.snapshot.pipelines\` over the raw \`pipelines\` prop as a defensive backstop, but that only fires when \`view.pipelines\` returns empty — which it doesn't for synthetic in_progress runs because the live CSV behind opp 10000 has real FLWs. Fixing it at the framework layer makes the fallback chain redundant rather than load-bearing for this case.

## Safety Assurance

- Real in_progress workflows (snapshot null): unchanged code path. Returns live pipelineData as before.
- Real completed workflows (snapshot stamped at completion): unchanged behavior. Still serves snapshot fields.
- Synthetic in_progress workflows (snapshot stamped by seed): NEW — now serves the seeded snapshot instead of live data.
- \`isCompleted\` flag still reflects \`inst.status === 'completed'\` — no template that branches on \`view.isCompleted\` is affected.
- \`asOf\` is null on in_progress runs (matches old behavior); only set when \`isCompleted\` is true.

Verified by reading the workflow lifecycle in \`commcare_connect/workflow/views.py\` and \`save_snapshot\` flow: the framework has exactly one writer of \`run.snapshot\` (the completion handler) outside the synthetic seed. No production code path stamps a snapshot on an in_progress run.

## Summary

HTML primitives for the unified settings menu: menu item `type` and value display, captions/playback-rate radio groups, and removal of the legacy playback-rate-menu compound.

### Changes vs Design

One thing that I didn't account for in the original design was how we display the current values in the root menu view. In React it's pretty straightforward to use the hooks to get the value but HTML side is a little more tricky. I opted to use a `<media-menu-item-value>` component which uses the menu item context to determine the `type` (`playback-rate` or `captions`) and get the right data. Open to ideas on how to improve/replace this if we don't like it. 

## Changes

- Add `menu-item-value`, setting state helpers, and menu item `type` (`playback-rate` | `captions`)
- Add captions radio group element and define entry; rename playback-rate menu to radio group
- Remove legacy `playback-rate-menu` custom elements and define
- Add `command-for` helper for popover/command wiring

author: toddysm
body:
Closes #312. Part of #318.

## Summary
Phase K of the Connector Service implementation: complete the observability stack and fill in every audit event listed in the design.

## Telemetry
**5 named Prometheus metrics** (exposed at `/metrics` via `prometheus_client.make_asgi_app()`):
- `custos_connector_bind_latency_seconds` (histogram)
- `custos_connector_pull_tick_duration_seconds` (histogram)
- `custos_connector_active_leases` (up/down counter, labelled `connectorInstanceId`)
- `custos_connector_manifest_fallback_total` (counter, labelled `outcome` = used/ignored/rejected/unknown)
- `custos_connector_cursor_lag_seconds` (observable gauge driven by `CursorLagRegistry`)

**6 OTel span helpers** (canonical names):
- `custos_connector.bind_for_step`
- `custos_connector.lease.issue`, `.lease.refresh`
- `custos_connector.pull_tick`
- `custos_connector.manifest.discovery`
- `custos_connector.identity.resolve`

`install_otel_providers()` is idempotent under a lock; wires `TracerProvider` + `MeterProvider(metric_readers=[PrometheusMetricReader()])`. The call-context middleware bypasses `/metrics` (network-policy is the trust boundary for the scrape).

Span helpers are plain class-based context managers, **not** `@contextmanager`-decorated, because the codebase uses frozen-slots dataclass exceptions widely (`ManifestDiscoveryError`, `LoaderError`). `contextlib._GeneratorContextManager.__exit__` rebinds `exc.__traceback__` which is incompatible with `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` subclasses of `Exception`. The class-based CM returns `None` from `__exit__` and lets Python's native re-raise propagate without touching the traceback.

## Audit completeness
**7 new typed event helpers** wired into every production code path that emits a corresponding lifecycle event:
- `audit_registration_accepted` / `_rejected` (loader)
- `audit_deprecation_toggled` (loader)
- `audit_manifest_fallback_used` / `_ignored` / `_rejected` (manifest discovery — 5 sites)
- `audit_authz_decision` (call-context middleware, alongside legacy `emit_event`)

`PLATFORM_WORKSPACE_ID = "__platform__"` sentinel for events that are platform-scope rather than workspace-scope.

## Test results
- `tests/test_telemetry.py` (17 tests)
- `tests/test_audit_completeness.py` (8 tests)
- `tests/test_metrics_endpoint.py` (7 tests)
- `tests/test_api_routes.py` — `_audit_event_types`/`_audit_events` helpers filter the new `authz.decision` event (verified separately in `tests/test_callctx.py`)

**676 passed, 29 deselected**. Ruff format/check + mypy all green.

## OpenAPI
`openapi.json` regenerated — no diff (the `/metrics` mount is a Starlette sub-app and excluded from FastAPI's OpenAPI schema, as designed).

## Summary
- The axis transition family (x snappy / x fluid / y directional / y non-directional / z directional / z non-directional) leans on the spring and inertia integrators' default settle thresholds (`restDelta = restSpeed = 0.01`). With the stiffness/damping each provider already uses, the visible motion is done well before the integrator considers the system settled — the tail past ~98% is imperceptible but still costs frames and delays the sequence handoff / page lifecycle.
- Add explicit `restDelta: 0.1` (and `restSpeed: 0.1` for springs) to every axis provider's physics — 10× the integrator defaults. No stiffness/damping/translate changes, so the perceived motion is unchanged; only the imperceptible tail is cut.

## Files touched
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/x/snappy.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/x/fluid.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/y/directional.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/y/non-directional.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/z/directional.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lib/transitions/axis/provider/z/non-directional.ts`

## Test plan
- [ ] Showcase each axis feel (snappy x, fluid x, directional y, non-directional y, directional z, non-directional z) and confirm front-edge motion is unchanged.
- [ ] Confirm the back-edge tail is shorter — chained navigations should hand off faster, no lingering sub-pixel settle.
- [ ] Sanity-check that non-axis transitions (sheet, hero, bubble, scroll, etc.) are unaffected — none were touched.

body:
## Summary

First static artifact for the **Map + USDA + heatmap** demo track (decided 2026-05-22). Cross-joins 30,357 CA SNAP-authorized retailers × FY2024 USDA PER × 281-PUMA SNAP-gap into a reproducible set of pitch visuals committed under `data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/`. No UI integration, no DB writes.

**Headline finding** from the county-level join (`county_metrics.csv`, PUMA→county via tract-count weighting):

| County | Eligible pop | Non-enroll | Grocery share | Grocery / 10K eligible | Quadrant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orange | 286K | 67.9% | 0.245 | 17.9 | **priority** (low access × high gap) |
| San Bernardino | 302K | 58.3% | **0.185** | 12.2 | clearest food-desert signal |
| San Diego | 311K | 65.4% | 0.249 | 18.3 | **priority** |
| Fresno / Kern / Sacramento | 180–200K | 53–58% | 0.23–0.26 | 11.6–18.0 | execution gap |

Statewide CA PER **10.98%** (FY2024 USDA: 7.58 over / 3.40 under) — FNS does not publish county-level PER, and the README is explicit that any county-PER choropleth is fabricated. The spatial story rides on **county grocery share × PUMA-allocated non-enrollment**, with statewide PER as the QC anchor.

## What lands

- `data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/` — 4 build scripts, 11 reproducible artifacts (PNGs + interactive HTML + CSVs + JSON), README with pitch framing + honest caveats.
- `data-ops/reference/` — newly vendored: Census 2020 tract→PUMA crosswalk (85K rows) + CA county GeoJSON + README documenting sources.
- `data-ops/sample/ca-snap-gap/` — PUMA non-enrollment estimates (281 rows, ACS 2023 1-Year PUMS).
- `data-ops/sample/usda-snap-retailers-ca/` — 30,357-row retailer CSV + manifest + README. The 14 MB `retailers.geojson` is intentionally **not** committed; the CSV is sufficient for every build script and the geojson is regenerable from the manifest's source URL.

## Commits (4)

1. `feat(data-ops): Track 1 food-access × PER static artifact` — hexbin/scatter/county/gap PNGs + `retailers_by_county.csv` + `summary.json`
2. `feat(data-ops): Track 1 interactive Folium map` — `interactive_map.html` (5.2 MB self-contained) with all-vs-grocery heatmap toggle
3. `feat(data-ops): Track 1 county choropleth + PUMA→county crosswalk` — vendored Census crosswalk + CA county GeoJSON; two-panel matplotlib choropleth + interactive Folium choropleth + 58-row `county_metrics.csv`
4. `feat(data-ops): Track 1 merge-prep — quadrant chart + self-contained data deps` — `county_quadrant.png` priority view + folds data deps onto branch + clean-rebuild verification

## Test plan

- [ ] `tools/ca-snap-gap/.venv/bin/python data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/build.py` regenerates `food_access_*.png`, `retailers_by_county.csv`, `summary.json`
- [ ] `tools/ca-snap-gap/.venv/bin/python data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/build_interactive.py` regenerates `interactive_map.html`
- [ ] `tools/ca-snap-gap/.venv/bin/python data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/build_choropleth.py` regenerates choropleth + `county_metrics.csv`
- [ ] `tools/ca-snap-gap/.venv/bin/python data-ops/analysis/track1-food-desert/build_quadrant.py` regenerates `county_quadrant.png`
- [ ] Open `artifacts/interactive_map.html` in browser — toggle "All retailers" vs "Grocery only" heatmap to see urban hexes collapse
- [ ] Open `artifacts/county_choropleth.html` in browser — hover a county for non-enrollment / grocery share / store count

Reproducibility verified end-to-end on a clean `artifacts/` directory before commit.

## Honest caveats (in README)

- PER is state-level only. No county-PER choropleth is drawn.
- PUMA→county weighting uses tract counts, not tract populations. Edge-county allocations are slightly off. ACS-population weighting is queued as a follow-up.
- USDA 2016 category spend is national-only — vendored elsewhere, intentionally not joined here.

## Where to take it next

1. Swap tract-count → ACS tract-population weights for the choropleth (requires Census API key).
2. Drive-time isochrones from each retailer (OSMnx) to make the food-desert claim spatial rather than count-based.
3. Wire `county_metrics.csv` into the iOS map view or dashboard as a real data layer.

author: spranab
body:
## Summary

Closes #47. Phase 2 Proposal 6 from the yantrikdb-agi gap analysis.

The v0.7.19 \`correct()\` minted a new rid + tombstoned the original — every inbound reference (graph edges, replication audit rows, manual \`supersedes\` metadata) dangled afterwards, and the only audit trail was a single \`metadata.correction_note\` string that was easily missed. v0.7.20 \`correct()\` mutates the memory **in place** and appends to a queryable revision history.

## Breaking changes (engine + Python binding)

### Engine signature

```rust
pub fn correct(
    rid: &str,
    new_text: Option<&str>,
    metadata_merge: Option<&serde_json::Value>,
    new_importance: Option<f64>,
    new_valence: Option<f64>,
    reason: &str,        // REQUIRED, non-empty
) -> Result<CorrectionResult>
```

- \`new_embedding\` REMOVED (HNSW doesn't support in-place vector update — embedding changes still use forget+record)
- \`correction_note\` REMOVED (replaced by \`reason\` as required positional)
- \`new_text\` now \`Option\` (was required); pass \`None\` to keep
- \`metadata_merge\` NEW (Option, patch-merged into existing metadata)

### Python binding

\`db.correct(rid, reason, new_text=None, metadata_merge=None, new_importance=None, new_valence=None)\` — \`reason\` positional-required, others kwarg-optional. Result dict adds \`revision_num\`.

New \`db.history(rid)\` exposed.

## Invariants

- rid preserved (result.corrected_rid == rid)
- created_at preserved
- Atomic: revision INSERT + memories UPDATE in one transaction
- \`reason\` REQUIRED, non-empty; \`InvalidInput\` on violation
- At least one mutation field must be supplied; no-op corrections rejected
- Inbound link integrity preserved — anything pointing TO this rid continues to resolve
- Encrypted databases: prior_text + prior_metadata go through \`encrypt_text()\` before storage in the revision row; \`history()\` decrypts on read

## Schema v30

```sql
CREATE TABLE record_revisions (
    revision_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    rid              TEXT NOT NULL,
    revision_num     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    prior_text       TEXT NOT NULL,    -- encrypted if provider attached
    prior_metadata   TEXT NOT NULL,    -- encrypted if provider attached
    prior_importance REAL NOT NULL,
    prior_valence    REAL NOT NULL,
    reason           TEXT NOT NULL,
    applied_at       REAL NOT NULL,
    hlc              BLOB NOT NULL,
    origin_actor     TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(rid, revision_num)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_record_revisions_rid
    ON record_revisions(rid, revision_num);
```

\`UNIQUE(rid, revision_num)\` + \`INSERT OR IGNORE\` makes replication apply idempotent across re-syncs.

## Replication

\`materialize_correct\` rewritten for the new payload shape (\`rid\`, \`revision_num\`, \`new_text\` / \`metadata_merge\` / \`new_importance\` / \`new_valence\` nullable, \`reason\`, \`applied_at\`).

**Cross-version note:** v0.7.19 followers seeing a v0.7.20 leader's correct op will fail the new payload's \`rid\` lookup (no \"rid\" key on the old shape) and silently no-op rather than corrupting state. Operators must roll forward in-order; rolling back v0.7.20 → v0.7.19 AFTER correct() calls have landed is unsupported (the in-place mutation cannot be reversed automatically). Documented in the materialize_correct doc block.

## Test plan

- [x] \`correct_preserves_rid_and_created_at\` — central invariant
- [x] \`correct_writes_revision_row_with_prior_state\` — revision capture
- [x] \`correct_multiple_revisions_increment_revision_num\` — sequencing
- [x] \`correct_rejects_empty_reason\` — empty + whitespace-only both rejected
- [x] \`correct_rejects_no_mutation_fields\` — no-op rejection
- [x] \`correct_preserves_inbound_graph_edges\` — link integrity (the central v0.7.20 win)
- [x] \`correct_history_empty_for_never_corrected_record\` — clean default
- [x] \`schema_v30_fresh_install_has_record_revisions_table\` — fresh install smoke check
- [x] Cascaded existing tests: \`test_correct_memory\`, \`test_correction_replicates\`, \`test_correct_preserves_dimensions\`, \`test_encrypted_correct_memory\` (all assertions updated for in-place semantics)
- [x] **Full lib sweep: 1505/1505 tests pass locally**
- [x] \`cargo fmt --check --all\` clean

## Pre-registered impact (from yantrikdb-agi Phase 2)

> \"skill_define success rate goes from 0% to >50% within 1 week\" — depends on this PR + the server-side validation-UX work (Tier 1, forwarded to yantrikdb-server). Engine ships first so the server's \"how to fix\" remediation messages can point at the new correct() semantics.

## Scope discipline

- Engine + Python binding only. No MCP-server changes.
- Schema migration v30. Fresh installs get the table from SCHEMA_SQL; existing DBs get it from MIGRATE_V29_TO_V30. Forward-only.
- BREAKING signature change. Server-side callers (and any other downstream) must update. Coordinating via swarm message after merge.
- No version bump. v0.7.20 charter will batch this with #45 / #46 / #48 once those land.

### Files changed (8)

```
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/base/schema.rs                 SCHEMA_VERSION=30, MIGRATE_V29_TO_V30, fresh-install record_revisions
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/base/types.rs                  CorrectionResult.revision_num, new RecordRevision struct
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/distributed/replication.rs    materialize_correct rewrite + cross-version doc
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/distributed/sync.rs            test_correction_replicates cascaded
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/engine/lifecycle.rs            correct() rewrite + history() query + encryption pass-through
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/engine/mod.rs                  migration registration
crates/yantrikdb-core/src/engine/tests.rs                8 new tests + 3 cascaded
crates/yantrikdb-python/src/py_engine/memory.rs          correct() binding rewrite + history() binding
```

author: ax-jkikta
body:
## Why the previous fix didn't work

PR #73 (v1.0.30) added a \"Wait for PyPI to serve new version\" step that polled \`https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json\` from the GitHub runner. I assumed the MCP Registry was waiting on PyPI metadata propagation, so polling the same endpoint would gate the registry publish on the same condition.

**v1.0.31 disproved that.** The wait step saw HTTP 200 and the registry's validation saw HTTP 404 only **0.3 seconds later**. Same URL, opposite results.

## What's actually happening

I pulled the MCP Registry source (\`internal/validators/registries/pypi.go\` on \`modelcontextprotocol/registry@main\`) and the registry queries this exact URL:

\`\`\`go
fetchURL := fmt.Sprintf(\"%s/pypi/%s/%s/json\", pkg.RegistryBaseURL, ...)
\`\`\`

Identical to what I was polling. The divergence is a **CDN PoP boundary**: GitHub Actions runners and the MCP Registry server hit different PyPI CDN edges. The runner's PoP had the new version; the registry's PoP hadn't. Both pointing at PyPI, neither lying — they're just resolving the JSON URL via different cache nodes.

Polling from the runner side can never predict when the registry's PoP catches up.

## Fix

Wrap \`./mcp-publisher publish\` in a retry loop: **6 attempts × 30 s backoff = ~2.5 min budget**. The publish lands as soon as the registry's PoP is in sync (historical observation: 3-5 min after upload, so the budget catches the typical case). If the budget exhausts, exits with an explicit pointer to the backfill command.

I kept the \"Wait for PyPI to serve new version\" step from PR #73. It's still useful as a cheap (~10 s on happy path) confirmation that PyPI itself completed the upload — catches a different failure mode (publish was structurally accepted but never appeared). Removed the misleading 'will fix the registry publish' framing from its comment.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML syntax validated locally.
- [x] \`uv run ruff format --check .\` / \`ruff check .\` / \`mypy .\` / \`pytest tests/\` — all clean (no source changes).
- [ ] **Real validation: the next release.** A clean run with the retry kicking in once (or never) confirms the fix. If the retry budget exhausts, the diagnosis was incomplete and we revisit.

## Version

CI-only; no version bump or CHANGELOG entry (consistent with PR #73 and the repo convention for workflow-only changes).

| `assessment-input` | Synthetic per-layer findings for the report skill |

17 real task evals across all 8 layer/utility skills, replacing the PR 1 placeholder graders. All passing at 1.00 aggregate against the fixtures.

### From the grader fix commit

One brittle `contains: "findings"` grader replaced with `regex_match: "(?i)finding(s)?"` so the report skill doesn't false-positive when the agent legitimately uses singular form ("Key Finding" in a table header). Caught during local PR1+2+3 validation run on the test branch.

### From PR #3 — agent-level eval

New user-invocable skill `isee-orchestrate` extracts the assess pipeline out of `agent.md` (single source of truth — `agent.md` Assess mode now delegates). Agent-level eval at `evals/isee-orchestrate/` with `skill_invocation` grader validates the 6 phase skills are invoked in the documented order. Two tasks, both branches covered:

| Task | Fixture | Required skills | Aggregate |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `lightweight-skipped-agents` | lightweight-startup (no agents) | 5 (skip phase 5) | 0.98 |
| `agent-heavy-full-pipeline` | agent-heavy (2 agents, 2 skills) | 6 (run phase 5) | 0.99 |

Bonus user affordance: `/isee-orchestrate` directly works without the mode picker.

## Validation evidence

Full local PR1+2+3 validation run on `test/waza-all-prs` (pre-grader-fix):

| Skill | Tasks | Aggregate |
|---|---:|---:|
| isee-advise | 2/2 | 1.00 |
| isee-assess-agents | 2/2 | 1.00 |
| isee-assess-evidence | 3/3 | 1.00 |
| isee-assess-execution | 3/3 | 1.00 |
| isee-assess-intent | 1/1 | 1.00 |
| isee-assess-report | **0/1 → 1/1** (after grader fix in this PR) | 0.83 → **1.00** |
| isee-assess-structure | 3/3 | 1.00 |
| isee-drift | 2/2 | 1.00 |
| isee-orchestrate | 2/2 | 0.98 / 0.99 |

19/19 tasks green on the test branch with this PR's grader fix applied.

## How to verify

```
git checkout suuus/waza-pr3-agent-eval
waza coverage
waza run isee-orchestrate     # ~6-15 min — agent-level eval
waza run                       # ~30-50 min — full suite
```

## Why this happened (note for future stacked PRs)

When a PR's `base` is another feature branch, GitHub's "Merge" button merges into that base — not into `main`. After merging an upstream stacked PR, downstream PRs need their base re-pointed to `main` before merging. Adding to PR template or a contributor note is worth considering.

author: ywutian
body:
Single-purpose doc capturing the structural data-ceiling finding from this 2-session investigation, so future sessions don't burn time repeating the same 4-path hunt.

## Why this doc

Across this session we built 4 diagnostic instruments (Brier scorer, monotonicity suite, per-cell lift, ridge logistic regression) and used them to argue engine is mis-calibrated. We then attempted to LEARN better coefficients from outcome data → blocked by selection bias + sample size. We attempted to expand the \`SchoolCdsAdmitBand\` Tier 1 anchor → blocked by CDS standard not publishing the data. We attempted state transparency reports → blocked because UC is structurally unique. We attempted academic/journalist sources → only Harvard SFFA, single-school, composite-axis.

**4 paths × ~60 schools / agencies / sources = 0 new usable rows for non-UC schools.**

## What the doc captures

1. **Why each path failed structurally** (not "didn't look hard enough")
2. **Why UC is unique** (3 simultaneous conditions: CA state law + UCOP centralized IR + UC self-normalized GPA)
3. **Don't do list** for the next session / agent
4. **Forward-looking watch items**: federal ACTS proposal (2027+), commercial data, university data-sharing agreements
5. **Pointers to all 5 PRs** (#299/#300/#302/#304/#305) and the related memory file

## Why this matters

Without this doc, the next agent / session that sees an engine miscalibration signal will likely:
- Open Step 1/2 diagnostic instruments
- See the same Brier 0.302 / per-cell deltas
- Conclude "let's learn coefficients from data" → blocked by bias
- Pivot to "let's expand CDS bands" → blocked by data availability
- Burn 2 days re-discovering this

This doc shortcuts that loop with concrete negative findings + paths to watch for.

## Test plan

- [x] Doc renders cleanly in Markdown
- [x] Pre-push gate green (no code changes)
- [x] Cross-referenced with memory file (\`feedback_do_not_tune_coefficients.md\`)
- [x] Pointers to all 5 PRs are correct

author: randomparity
body:
## Summary

Fixes #206. `--fields` / `--exclude-fields` now actually shape `bzr bug`
output instead of always rendering a fixed five-column table (or a full JSON
object with unrequested fields nulled). `--fields` selects which columns/keys
appear, in order; `--exclude-fields` removes them. Under `--json` the output
object is trimmed to the selection, gh-style.

## Changes

- **Table output** — `bug list`, `my`, `search`, and `query run` honor
  `--fields` (column selection, in the given order) and `--exclude-fields`
  (column removal), replacing the hardcoded five-column table. `bug view`
  detail rows honor an explicit field set.
- **JSON output** — `--fields` / `--exclude-fields` trim the output object to
  the selection. `id` appears only when requested, and `--exclude-fields id`
  drops it — while the client still fetches `id` on the wire
  (`force_id_fields`) so every bug deserializes regardless of the selection.
  Trimming happens client-side after the fetch, so it applies on REST and
  XML-RPC alike. Multi-ID `bug view` trims each entry in `bugs` while leaving
  the `{"bugs": [...], "failed": [...]}` wrapper intact.
- **Pre-network validation** — a selection that leaves nothing to emit exits 7
  with a clear message before any network I/O, for every list-style bug
  subcommand. Table emptiness is measured against the five default columns;
  JSON against the full field set. `bug view` is exempt in both modes (a sparse
  or empty single-bug object is a coherent result) and warns rather than
  failing — documented so a `{}` + exit-0 result is discoverable as a possible
  field-name typo.
- **serde_json `preserve_order`** — enabled for trimming; crate-wide, so
  `json!` values now serialize keys in insertion order. Cosmetic effect on the
  error envelope and `query`/`template` results; noted in the changelog.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the projection helpers (`canonical_field_list`,
  `force_id_fields`, `bug_to_json`/`bugs_to_json`, `validate_*_field_selection`)
  and the client entry points that prepend/strip `id`.
- Integration tests covering `bug list`/`view` `--json` trimming, all-unknown
  vs. partial-unknown selections, the list/view exit-code asymmetry, and an
  end-to-end `--exclude-fields id --json` contract gated on
  `query_param_is_missing("exclude_fields")` so a `force_id_fields` regression
  fails the test.
- A guard test (`cli_and_docs_avoid_misleading_trim_phrasing`) keeps stale
  marketing-style phrasings out of the CLI help and manual.

Full suite: 1224 lib + 21 + 72 integration tests pass.

## Notes

- One pre-existing clippy lint remains at `src/xmlrpc/client_tests.rs:792`
  (`map_unwrap_or`), tracked separately as #216 — not introduced by this branch.
- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-27-json-field-trimming-design.md`.

author: vlumi
body:
## Summary

The data-side of #246. After this lands, fresh JPEGs with EXIF GPS imported through the converter get their place hierarchy populated in the DB at intake time. PR 2 of #246 will add the `bin/photo-geocode.ts` daemon for backfilling existing photos and adding languages later; PR 3 adds `bin/photo.ts audit --country-mismatch` (#346).

## Schema (migration 007)

```sql
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_country_code TEXT;
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_state        TEXT;
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_city         TEXT;
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_district     TEXT;
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_place        TEXT;
ALTER TABLE photo ADD COLUMN geocoded_address      TEXT;     -- raw Nominatim address JSON

CREATE INDEX photo_geocoded_country_idx  ON photo (geocoded_country_code);
CREATE INDEX photo_geocoded_state_idx    ON photo (geocoded_state);
CREATE INDEX photo_geocoded_city_idx     ON photo (geocoded_city);
CREATE INDEX photo_geocoded_district_idx ON photo (geocoded_district);

CREATE TABLE photo_localized (
  photo_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
  lang              TEXT NOT NULL,   -- never 'en'
  geocoded_state    TEXT,
  geocoded_city     TEXT,
  geocoded_district TEXT,
  geocoded_place    TEXT,
  geocoded_address  TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (photo_id, lang),
  FOREIGN KEY (photo_id) REFERENCES photo(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

English is the canonical / filter-keyed language; lives on the photo row directly so filter queries and the English read path don't need a join. Other languages live in `photo_localized` only when actually translated. `geocoded_address` keeps Nominatim's raw response so the field mapping can be revised without re-fetching.

Operator-set `photo.country_code` and `photo.place` are **untouched** — the reverse-geocode data sits alongside.

## Module

`converter/reverse-geocode/`:

- Nominatim client with custom `User-Agent: photo-diary/<version> (<repo-url>)` and 1 RPS queue (per Nominatim's public usage policy).
- Per-`(lang, coord)` file cache at `${GEOCODE_DIR}/cache/<lang>/<lat>:<lon>.json` (coords rounded to 4 decimals ≈ 11 m precision). Atomic writes via temp + rename so partial JSONs never read back as cache hits.
- Country-specific fallback chains for `state` / `city` / `district`. Singapore-style city-states leave `state` NULL and that's fine — `display_name` still renders.
- Env: `NOMINATIM_BASE_URL` (self-host escape), `GEOCODE_DIR` (defaults to `<cwd>/.geocode/`).
- Network / no-address failures log but don't throw — caller gets `null` and moves on.

## Converter intake

- Opt-in via `REVERSE_GEOCODE=1` in the instance's `.env`.
- `REVERSE_GEOCODE_EXTRA_LANGS=ja,fi` lists languages beyond the always-on English. Each extra is one additional Nominatim call per photo at intake (at 1 RPS, so a 3-language setup adds ~3 s per photo with coords on cache miss).

## Driver layer

- `db.upsertGeocoded(photoId, lang, fields)` routes English to photo columns, other languages to `photo_localized` via upsert that doesn't clobber existing non-NULL fields.
- `db.loadPhotosMissingGeocoded(lang, limit)` is the daemon's "give me work" query (PR 2's consumer). Ordered by `taken DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC` so recent photos (more likely to be visited) get filled in first; EXIF-less photos go to the back.
- `db.loadPhoto` / `db.loadPhotos` accept optional `lang`. When non-English, joins `photo_localized` and merges localized values over English photo columns in `mapRow`.

## Backend API exposure

Photo response gains a `geocoded` field:

```ts
{
  geocoded: {
    countryCode: string | undefined,
    state: string | undefined,
    city: string | undefined,
    district: string | undefined,
    place: string | undefined,
    address: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,   // parsed raw JSON
  }
}
```

Controllers don't yet thread `lang` from the request — EN-for-everyone for now. The driver-layer plumbing is ready; controller plumbing comes in a tiny follow-up paired with #247's frontend work in 0.12.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck --workspaces` — clean.
- [x] `npm run lint --workspaces` — clean.
- [x] `npm test --workspaces` — 634 server + 963 react-app + 7 converter pass.
- [x] Migration tests updated to expect schema version 7 + the new columns in the photo schema's column list.
- [x] Manual against the dev DB:
  - Direct `geocode(35.6586, 139.7454, "en")` returns Minato / Tokyo / Japan structured data + display_name; cache file written; second call cache-hits.
  - Same coords in `ja` and `fi` return localized strings.
  - `db.upsertGeocoded(id, "en", ...)` writes to photo columns; `loadPhoto(id)` returns those.
  - `db.upsertGeocoded(id, "ja", ...)` writes to `photo_localized`; `loadPhoto(id, "ja")` returns Japanese values; `loadPhoto(id)` (no lang) still returns English.
  - `country_code` stays language-independent (lives on photo, not photo_localized).

## What's next

- **PR 2 of #246**: `bin/photo-geocode.ts` daemon for backfilling existing photos + adding languages later. Operator-side tool, long-running, lock-file + resumable.
- **PR 3 (#346)**: `bin/photo.ts audit --country-mismatch` — small audit addition using the new `geocoded_country_code`.

body:
## Summary

The prompt's failure analysis assumed a `(mean + 2*std)` gap rule over `np.diff(sorted_freqs)`. The **actual** implementation is the histogram-peak detector `detect_transmitter_windows` (`thrifty/identify.py:26-76` and `thriftyx/identify.py:33-83`) — a different algorithm. The two behave differently on the prompt's test corpus:

- Std-of-gaps variant → **fails** on `[101, 102, 128]` (as the prompt hand-calculated).
- Current histogram-peak variant → **passes** (histogram has 25 zero bins between the two clusters, well below `low_thresh=0.4*std`).

Per stop condition: all 6 prompt cases pass → document and stop, no fix needed.

## Walk-through for `[101, 102, 128]`

- `cnts = bincount([0, 1, 27]) = [1, 1, 0, ..., 0, 1]` (length 28)
- `std(cnts) ≈ 0.309`, `low_thresh ≈ 0.124`, `high_thresh ≈ 0.386`
- Both `cnt=1` clusters exceed `high_thresh` ⇒ each becomes a peak.
- 25 zero bins between them all fall under `low_thresh` ⇒ split fires.
- Result: `edges = [101, 115, 129]` ⇒ 2 transmitters. ✓

## Test results

30 tests, all passing (run against both `thrifty.identify` and `thriftyx.identify`):

| Case | Input | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| a–f (prompt cases) | as documented | as documented | matches |
| BatRF realistic dual-bin TX1 + single-bin TX2 | 500+500 / 1000 dets | 2 | 2 |
| 3 TXs each with 3-bin spread | 3000 dets | 3 | 3 |
| Adjacency boundary sweep (gap 1..50) | matched 500-det clusters | 1 / 2 | matches |
| **Extremely uneven populations (2000:50)** | imbalanced | 2 (want) | **1 (got)** — known limitation |

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/test_identify_auto_classify.py -v
============================== 30 passed in 0.11s ==============================
```

## Known limitation found (not in scope to fix here)

At 40:1 population imbalance the dominant cluster inflates `std(cnts)`, raising `high_thresh` above the weaker cluster's count. The weak TX is then lost. This is not the BatRF field-test pattern (TX1/TX2 have similar duty cycles) and the existing `--map` (freqmap) flag already provides the production-grade workaround (`thriftyx/identify.py:112-126`). Recommendation: keep the auto-classifier as a developer convenience; advise `--map` in the user guide for paper-grade runs.

## What's in the diff

- `docs/verification/auto_classify_robustness.md` — algorithm walk-through, test matrix, comparison with prompt's Candidate A/B, recommendation.
- `tests/unit/test_identify_auto_classify.py` — 30 parametrized tests (6 prompt cases × 2 modules + 4 realistic + 6 adjacency × 2 + 1 known-limitation × 2).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_identify_auto_classify.py` — 30/30 pass
- [x] Existing tests in `tests/unit/test_identify.py` (on a sibling branch via `dd83153`) would continue to pass; no code changes here
- [ ] **Do not merge before sub_offset (PR #39) and divisor (PR #40) are resolved** — the upstream investigations may affect the field-test data flow that exercises this code path.

## Recommended follow-up (separate PR)

Optionally: docs-only update to `docs/user_guide.md` and `_ko.md` recommending `--map` for production captures. Skipped here to honour the "no fix needed" stop condition strictly.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Summary

API requests trigger 30+ synchronous file I/O operations per call, compounding into 30+ second latency. This PR eliminates the 5 hottest I/O sites in the request dispatch chain.

### Root Cause

| Operation | Impact |
|-----------|--------|
| `Coord.is_initialized` | 3 syscalls per request (file_exists x2 + is_directory), no cache |
| `Trajectory.read_entries` | Reads entire JSONL file, parses all lines, just to compute round number |
| `Trajectory.append_entry` | Disk write per keeper tool call |
| `Keeper_registry_tool_usage_persistence.flush` | JSON serialize + mkdir_p + disk write per keeper tool call |
| `Telemetry_eio.summarize_tool_usage` | Reads up to 100k JSONL events on every tools/list call |

### Changes

1. **Server-level `is_initialized` cache** (1s TTL) — `Atomic.t`-based, eliminates 3 syscalls per request
2. **In-memory trajectory round counter** — `Hashtbl`-based, hydrated from disk on first miss, no subsequent reads
3. **Telemetry summary cache** (30s TTL) — avoids parsing 100k JSONL events on every tools/list call
4. **Batched tool usage persistence** — dirty set + periodic flush (5s) instead of per-call disk I/O
5. **Background flush fiber** — periodic `flush_all_dirty` in server bootstrap loop

### Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/coord/coord_utils_paths_backend.ml` | `is_initialized` cache + `invalidate_initialized_cache` |
| `lib/coord/coord_utils_paths_backend.mli` | Expose `invalidate_initialized_cache` |
| `lib/trajectory/trajectory.ml` | In-memory round counter (`next_round`) |
| `lib/trajectory/trajectory.mli` | Expose `next_round` |
| `lib/telemetry_eio.ml` | `summarize_tool_usage` cache with 30s TTL |
| `lib/keeper/keeper_registry_tool_usage_persistence.ml` | Dirty set + `mark_dirty` + `flush_all_dirty` |
| `lib/keeper/keeper_registry_tool_usage_persistence.mli` | Expose `mark_dirty`, `flush_all_dirty` |
| `lib/mcp_server_eio_call_tool.ml` | Use `next_round` + `mark_dirty` |
| `lib/server/server_runtime_bootstrap.ml` | Background flush fiber |

## Test Plan

- [ ] `dune build .` passes
- [ ] `dune runtest` — no new test failures (pre-existing failures unrelated)
- [ ] Manual: start server, make MCP tool calls, verify latency < 2s
- [ ] Verify trajectory files still have correct round numbers
- [ ] Verify telemetry summary returns correct data (within 30s staleness)
- [ ] Check Prometheus metrics: `masc_tool_call_duration_ms` improvement

author: jtzingsheim1
body:
Lets the staleness gate be tuned (or effectively disabled) from the Vercel dashboard via `BBB_STALENESS_MINUTES`, no code change needed. Defaults to the existing 60 min when unset, so **behaviour is unchanged until the var is set**.

## Why
GitHub Actions scheduled cron fires well past its nominal 30-min cadence (observed 2–3h gaps), so the 60-min gate renders the "Data temporarily unavailable" page much of the time — bad for a showcase. But the public chart shows a **daily aggregate average**: whether the latest snapshot is 30 min or a few hours old barely changes a daily mean. The 60-min gate was sized for live per-station prices the site doesn't display, so it's over-strict for the actual product.

## What
- `BBB_STALENESS_MINUTES` overrides the threshold (default 60). Raise to e.g. `360` to ride out cron lag; set very high to effectively disable the gate.
- Documented in `docs/deploy-runbook.md` (env table) and `.env.local.example`.

## Note
This is the dashboard "dial" alternative to hard-disabling the staleness self-policing. The genuinely-reliable fix (free external cron hitting an ingest endpoint every 30 min) remains an option for later if true freshness is wanted.

body:
## Summary

Adds the operational runbook and one-shot setup script we built while bringing the Eval Judge deployment online against `boddev.onmicrosoft.com`. The new content captures everything a fresh tenant needs to go from "no Work IQ at all" to "eval-score running over A2A" without re-discovering the same gotchas.

## What changed

- **`agents/eval-judge/README.md`**  end-to-end A2A runbook covering Work IQ service-principal provisioning, delegated token acquisition (JWT audience/scope), the correct gateway URL (`workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/a2a`), agent ID discovery, and the `--m365-agent-id` / `--judge-agent-id` invocation pattern. Also documents the gotchas: AADSTS650052 (missing SP), the wrong-gateway redirect, and the ~100 calls/user/hour limit on the preview API.
- **`scripts/setup-a2a.ps1`**  one-shot tenant prep. Takes tenant + client + secret + admin creds and does all of: provisions the Work IQ first-party SP (`fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7`), runs the device-code flow against the Azure PowerShell public client to mint a delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` token, discovers and persists agent IDs from `.agents`, optionally validates connectors via app-only Graph, and optionally launches eval-score with the discovered IDs.

## Why

Standing this up by hand required ~10 manual steps and hit AADSTS650052 mid-flow because the Work IQ SP wasn't in the tenant. Now anyone who needs to spin up Eval Judge on a new tenant can run a single script.

## Notes for reviewers

- The runbook is purely documentation; no source changes.
- The setup script is a thin orchestrator over `az`, `gh`, and direct OAuth token endpoints, with idempotent SP provisioning.
- No changes to existing pipeline code.

author: seeker71
body:
## Two pieces, named honestly

This PR contains two commits in tension:

**Commit 1 — the megabyte demo (d41b28a0)** — adds `seeded_bytes`, `sum_bytes_list` natives + a demonstration that 1 MB shares between Go and Rust kernels through a 15-byte channel via the seeded-from-shared-parameters pattern. Works end-to-end.

**Commit 2 — the analysis (264fb6dd)** — surveys the kernel's 88 natives, identifies ~30 that should compost back to Form recipes, and proves the LCG (the algorithm under `seeded_bytes`) IS expressible as a Form recipe. **Names that Commit 1's additions are themselves composting candidates.**

## Your correction (after Commit 1 landed)

> *"do we need those crypto protocols in the kernel? I think not, avoid putting things in the kernel that can be expressed in form native code. analyse the full kernel surface and reduce it to its primitives, and have shared binary features in form native recipes that can expand into native machine code for efficiency, allowing the kernel to bootstrap from primitives into an efficient, flexibility, sovereign cell"*

I had been moving in the wrong direction — pre-emptively adding SHA-256, Ed25519, and a PKI demo (sha2 + ed25519-dalek crates, @noble npm packages). All of that is **stashed, not committed** — the correction supersedes it.

## The megabyte demo (still valid as a demonstration)

```
$ form/form-samples/cross-modal/16-megabyte-channel/orchestrate.sh
Cell A — Go kernel:    payload sum 127501088 (1.5s)
Cell B — Rust kernel:  payload sum 127501088 (0.11s)
Channel bytes:         15
Payload bytes:         1,000,000
Compression ratio:     66666:1
```

It proves the protocol shape: shared substrate-resident algorithms + parameters-on-channel = arbitrary content through small channels.

But the implementation (seeded_bytes as kernel native) violates the minimal-kernel discipline. **The native is scaffolding; the canonical truth is the Form recipe.**

## The honest finding from the analysis

Form-recipe LCG in `form-samples/cross-modal/17-recipes-as-truth/seeded-bytes-recipe.fk`:

```
go         = 1   (recipe == native ✓)
rust       = 1   (recipe == native ✓)
typescript = 0   (recipe != native — JS Number precision breaks at 2^53)
```

The composting principle works on Go and Rust where Form integers are 64-bit precise. **TypeScript breaks composting for crypto-style algorithms** because JS Number is float64; the LCG's intermediate (state × 1103515245 ≈ 2^61) overflows the 2^53 safe-int range.

Three paths forward, named honestly in the analysis:
1. TS kernel adopts BigInt-backed Form integers (slower but precise)
2. Form gets fixed-width modular-multiply primitives (narrow surface, expressive)
3. Algorithms reformulate to stay within 2^53 (limited expressibility)

## What this PR ultimately ships

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `form/form-kernel-{go,rust,ts}/...` | `seeded_bytes` + `sum_bytes_list` natives (scaffolding; composting candidates) |
| `form/form-samples/cross-modal/16-megabyte-channel/` | The megabyte demo — 1 MB through 15 bytes, cross-kernel three-way |
| `kernels/MINIMAL_KERNEL_ANALYSIS.md` | 88-native survey + composting plan + minimum kernel target (~25 primitives) |
| `form/form-samples/cross-modal/17-recipes-as-truth/` | Proof the LCG composts to a Form recipe in Go/Rust + honest TS precision finding |

## Cross-refs

- [`lc-private-channel-via-substrate`](../docs/vision-kb/concepts/lc-private-channel-via-substrate.md)
- [`lc-doorway-patterns`](../docs/vision-kb/concepts/lc-doorway-patterns.md)
- [`numeric-types-plan.md`](../docs/coherence-substrate/numeric-types-plan.md) — the format-recipe destination where `arithmetic-hint` dispatches to JIT/BigInt/etc.
- [`SUBSTRATE_AS_DEPLOYMENT_RUNTIME.md`](../kernels/SUBSTRATE_AS_DEPLOYMENT_RUNTIME.md)
- [`lc-grammar-is-the-universal-recipe`](../docs/vision-kb/concepts/lc-grammar-is-the-universal-recipe.md) — every algorithm IS a recipe

`./validate.sh` stays **137 ok, 0 divergent**. Demo + analysis live in `form-samples/cross-modal/` (not auto-walked).

## What I'd push next if you want movement

Compost `sum_bytes_list` first — it's the lowest-hanging fruit (a fold; no precision issues; just speed). Form-recipe version + retire the native. Then tackle TS arithmetic precision so the rest of the composting plan can land.

body:
## Summary

Two `Qt::UniqueConnection` + lambda assert sites introduced by the adaptive throttle feature. Both assert at runtime with:

```
ASSERT failure in "QObject::connect: Unique connection requires the slot to be a pointer to a member function of a QObject subclass."
Qt6Core.dll  qobject.h:269
```

`Qt::UniqueConnection` is only valid with `&ClassName::memberFunction` pointer syntax — Qt has no way to compare lambda closures for deduplication.

> **Note**: the LNK1220 build failure is handled separately by #3237 (already merged). This PR covers the two runtime asserts only.

## Fixes

### 1 — `RadioModel::ensureOwnedPanadapter` (`RadioModel.cpp:3440`)

Asserts whenever a **second slice is added while autothrottle is actively capping fps**. The function already has an early-return guard at line 3412 (`if (auto* existing = …) return existing`) that ensures the connection is made at most once per pan — `Qt::UniqueConnection` was both invalid with a lambda and redundant.

### 2 — `NetworkDiagnosticsHistory` constructor (`NetworkDiagnosticsDialog.cpp:2416`)

Same issue. The connection is made exactly once in the constructor so the flag was always a no-op in addition to being invalid.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/models/RadioModel.cpp` | Remove `Qt::UniqueConnection` from deferred-cap lambda in `ensureOwnedPanadapter` |
| `src/gui/NetworkDiagnosticsDialog.cpp` | Remove `Qt::UniqueConnection` from `adaptiveThrottleChanged` lambda in `NetworkDiagnosticsHistory` ctor |

## Test plan

- [x] Autothrottle off, single slice — no assert
- [x] Autothrottle on, single slice — no assert
- [x] Autothrottle on, second slice added mid-session — no assert, both slices render at capped fps
- [x] Autothrottle toggled on/off mid-session — correct behavior throughout
- [ ] CI green

## Constitution

**Principle XI — Fixes Are Demonstrated**: both assert sites verified absent on Windows under autothrottle on and off before this commit was staged.

author: stevenwarejones
body:
Simplifies EDPA cloud test data generation so that regenerating all synthetic impression data for an environment is a single command with a config file, instead of multiple manual runs with many CLI flags.

Before this change, regenerating data required running GenerateSyntheticData separately for each event group with manually-specified entity keys, output paths, and model lines that had to match what EdpAggregatorCorrectnessTest expected inline. Getting any flag wrong meant silent test failures.

Now a single textproto config (impression_test_data_config.textproto) defines all event groups, entity keys, and output structure. Both GenerateSyntheticData and EdpAggregatorCorrectnessTest consume it, so test expectations and generated data cannot drift. Regenerating data for an environment is just: bazel run GenerateSyntheticData -- --config-file=config.textproto --kms-type=GCP --kek-uri=... --schema=gs:// --output-bucket=BUCKET --create-done-blobs

author: metagenau
body:
## Summary
Increased the default epsilon value in the centered-log-ratio (CLR) transform from `1e-6` to `1e-4` to improve numerical stability during backpropagation and prevent gradient spikes that destabilize the ODE solver.

## Changes
- Updated `clr()` function default `eps` parameter from `1e-6` to `1e-4`
- Updated `clr_mse()` function default `eps` parameter from `1e-6` to `1e-4`
- Updated `composite_loss()` function default `eps` parameter from `1e-6` to `1e-4`
- Added detailed documentation explaining the gradient regularization rationale

## Implementation Details
The epsilon parameter serves a dual purpose:
1. **Structural zero handling**: Prevents log(0) by flooring small values
2. **Gradient regularization**: Since `d log(x)/dx = 1/x`, an overly small epsilon allows near-zero predictions to inject large gradient spikes (~1/eps) into the backward pass

With `eps=1e-6`, these spikes destabilize the SiLU fitness function and downstream ODE solver (dopri5), causing it to shrink the timestep until numerical underflow occurs. The new value of `1e-4` caps per-element gradients at ~10^4 while preserving the behavior for abundant species, providing a better balance between numerical stability and model expressiveness.

author: edwinaml-su
body:
## Bug

`/ece/hoja-ingreso` (y otras 5 páginas con el mismo patrón) mostraban "Application error" con el error:

```
Error: A <Select.Item /> must have a value prop that is not an empty string.
This is because the Select value can be set to an empty string to clear
the selection and show the placeholder.
```

Radix UI Select (lib detrás de Shadcn) **reserva** `value=""` para el estado "sin selección / placeholder". Un `<SelectItem value="">` rompe esa invariante y dispara el error en cada render — la página entera deja de funcionar.

## Fix

Reemplazo `value=""` por `value="all"` (centinela explícito) y mapeo entre estados:

```tsx
<Select
  value={state || "all"}
  onValueChange={(v) => setState(v === "all" ? "" : v)}
>
  <SelectItem value="all">Todos</SelectItem>
  ...
</Select>
```

El estado interno del componente sigue siendo `""` — la lógica downstream (Zod, queries tRPC) no cambia. Solo cambia el shape DOM del Select.

## Archivos arreglados

| Archivo | Filtro |
|---|---|
| `(clinical)/ece/hoja-ingreso/page.tsx` ← **reportado** | estado workflow |
| `(clinical)/ece/orden-ingreso/page.tsx` | modalidad |
| `(clinical)/pharmacy/cart/page.tsx` | status carrito |
| `(admin)/gs1/medicamentos/page.tsx` | recall + vencimiento (2 selects) |
| `(admin)/deaths/page.tsx` | estado workflow |
| `(admin)/drugs/buscar-srs/page.tsx` | estado SRS |

Tras un grep regex sobre toda la app, **no quedan** `SelectItem value=""` residuales.

## Test plan
- [ ] Vercel deploya preview.
- [ ] `/ece/hoja-ingreso` carga sin "Application error" — se ve la lista.
- [ ] Cambiar el filtro "Estado" funciona en cada uno de los 6 selects.
- [ ] Seleccionar "Todos" deja la consulta sin filtro (mismo comportamiento previo, ahora sin romper Radix).

author: kellyj386
body:
The accident-report body diagram modelled each paired region (arms, legs,
shoulders, etc.) as a single SVG group containing both limbs, so clicking
the right arm filled both sides. Add a left/right laterality axis to
selections so paired limbs are independently clickable, and restyle the
upper body so head and neck read as distinct regions.

- Diagram: paired regions render two <g>s (left, right), each with its
  own click handler, fill/stroke, and hover state. Midline regions
  (head, face_jaw, neck, torso, hips) are unchanged. Restyle head + neck
  with a clear gap between regions.
- Data model: BodySelections gains PairedSelection ({left, right}) per
  paired key; midline keys remain BodySide. nextSide() is reused per
  laterality so each side toggles independently.
- DB: add accident_body_part_selections.laterality (nullable, check in
  left/right); widen the unique key to include it with NULLS NOT
  DISTINCT. Existing rows stay NULL and the renderer treats NULL on a
  paired region as both sides, preserving historical reports' visual.
- Wire: submission/edit forms emit one payload entry per (region, side,
  laterality); action reconciles by (region, laterality). PDF and CSV
  prefix paired entries with "Left "/"Right ". Read-only + admin
  renderers rebuild the lateralised selection from rows.

This pull request improves the robustness and accuracy of the frontend-backend API route contract checker, particularly in how it parses and matches API paths between the frontend and backend. The changes include both bug fixes and enhancements to the code and tests.

**Key improvements:**

*Parsing and matching accuracy:*
- The script now ignores `/api`-like substrings that are part of identifiers or import paths in frontend code, preventing false positives when scanning for API calls.
- Improved the regular expressions for matching router prefixes and decorator routes in backend code for better reliability, including formatting and line break handling.
- The path normalization logic was clarified and slightly updated for better readability and maintainability.

*Code quality and maintainability:*
- Improved error message formatting in the allowlist loader for better readability.
- Minor refactoring for clarity, such as splitting regular expression concatenation and updating import usage [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5290faa69c676bef7a9eebb79ac77f584656f9c57e54dc467979cf854d657055L2-L10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5290faa69c676bef7a9eebb79ac77f584656f9c57e54dc467979cf854d657055L122-R136) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5290faa69c676bef7a9eebb79ac77f584656f9c57e54dc467979cf854d657055L137-R153) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5290faa69c676bef7a9eebb79ac77f584656f9c57e54dc467979cf854d657055L73-R76).

*Testing:*
- Added new tests in `test_frontend_backend_route_contract_checker.py` to verify that the extraction logic correctly ignores import alias substrings and that the main script passes when there are no unresolved alias paths.

These changes collectively make the contract checker more reliable and easier to maintain.

## Description

Add interactive tool-guard approval card support for the Telegram channel using Telegram Bot API's InlineKeyboardMarkup + CallbackQuery mechanism. Follows the same cards/ directory pattern as QQ and WeCom channels.

### New files (src/qwenpaw/app/channels/telegram/cards/):

- __init__.py — package exports
- context.py — shared helpers (meta extraction, body text flattening, session context builder)
- dispatcher.py — TelegramCardHandler with registry-based routing
- tool_guard.py — approval card: builders, render, handle, enqueue

### Modified channel.py:

- Initialize TelegramCardHandler in constructor
- Register CallbackQueryHandler in _build_application() for inline button clicks
- Override on_event_message_completed() to intercept card events
- Extend on_streaming_end() to send compact approval card after streaming completes
- Fix early-return bug that would skip post-streaming card dispatch

### Behavior:

- Non-streaming: raw body text + Approve/Deny inline buttons in one message; on click, buttons are replaced with approval status line while preserving body text
- Streaming: body text streamed normally, then a compact MarkdownV2 card (tool name + buttons) sent separately; on click, updated to show status
- In-memory cache stores full request context to work around Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit
- Deduplication prevents double-click issues
- Resolved card shows who approved/denied (Telegram @username)

## Summary This PR does two things: it removes the in-process inbound source-IP allowlist entirely, and it lays the foundation for pluggable worker compute backends by introducing a `WorkerRuntime` abstraction. ## IP allowlist removal The `[server.ip_allowlist]` setting and its GitHub webhook overlay (`[server.integrations.github.webhooks.ip_allowlist]`) have been removed from config parsing, the settings API, and the OpenAPI spec. The `ip_allowlist.rs` module (~600 lines including the `GitHubMetaResolver`, middleware, and cache logic) is deleted. **Migration:** Existing `settings.toml` files containing those keys will now fail to parse as unknown fields. Source-IP restrictions should be moved to a reverse proxy, firewall, VPN, Tailscale ACL, or cloud ingress — as documented in the new security guidance. `build_router_with_options` loses the `ip_allowlist_config: Arc` parameter and `RouterOptions` loses `github_webhook_ip_allowlist`. Call sites in tests and the auth harness are updated accordingly. TCP serving no longer uses `make_service_with_connect_info` since `ConnectInfo` was only needed for IP extraction. ## WorkerRuntime abstraction A new `worker_runtime.rs` module introduces: - **`WorkerRuntime` trait** — `start`, `request_stop`, `force_stop`, `is_alive` - **`WorkerLaunchSpec`** — all inputs needed to describe a worker process, replacing the former `worker_command` helper - **`WorkerRef::Local { pid, process_group_id }`** — replaces the `worker_pid` / `worker_pgid` pair on `ManagedRun` - **`StartedWorker`** — carries the ref, optional stderr stream, and a `wait` future - **`LocalWorkerRuntime`** — the only implementation for now; wraps the existing subprocess spawn logic `AppState` stores an `Arc` and `AppStateConfig` accepts an optional override in `#[cfg(test)]` for injection. Stop/kill paths in `server.rs` and `lifecycle.rs` now call `worker_runtime.request_stop` / `force_stop` / `is_alive` instead of issuing signals directly. ### Plan Summary - **Task 1:** New `worker_runtime.rs` with trait, types, and `LocalWorkerRuntime` impl - **Task 2:** Wire `Arc` into `AppState` / `AppStateConfig` / `TestAppStateBuilder` - **Task 3:** Replace `worker_pid` / `worker_pgid` on `ManagedRun` with `worker_ref: Option`; build `WorkerLaunchSpec` in `execute_run_subprocess` - **Task 4:** Route all stop/kill calls through the runtime (`terminate_worker_for_deletion`, `shutdown_active_workers`, `cancel_run` fallback) - **Task 5:** Fake `RecordingWorkerRuntime` for unit tests; new cancel-fallback and shutdown tests ### Fabro Details

author: qianye1001
body:
## Summary

Fix native memory leak caused by old `SslContext` not being released during TLS certificate hot-reload when using the OpenSSL (netty-tcnative) provider.

Fixes #10395

## Root Cause

When TLS certificates are dynamically reloaded via `FileWatchService`, the `loadSslContext()` methods in `NettyRemotingServer` and `ProxyAndTlsProtocolNegotiator` directly overwrite the `sslContext` field without releasing the old instance. Since `ReferenceCountedOpenSslContext` allocates native off-heap memory (SSL_CTX, X509 chain, EVP_PKEY), this native memory is leaked on every certificate rotation cycle.

## Changes

### `remoting/src/main/java/org/apache/rocketmq/remoting/netty/NettyRemotingServer.java`
- Capture old `sslContext` before building the replacement
- Call `ReferenceCountUtil.release(oldSslContext)` after successful assignment
- Added imports for `SslContext` and `ReferenceCountUtil`

### `proxy/src/main/java/org/apache/rocketmq/proxy/grpc/ProxyAndTlsProtocolNegotiator.java`
- Same pattern: capture old context, release after new one is assigned
- Made `sslContext` field `volatile` for thread-safe reads from TLS handshake threads
- Added import for shaded `ReferenceCountUtil`

## Safety

- **"Build new, then release old"** ordering ensures `sslContext` is never null or prematurely released
- `ReferenceCountUtil.release()` is safe for JDK provider `SslContext` (no-op for non-ReferenceCounted)
- In-flight connections using the old context are unaffected (refCount managed by Netty channel pipeline)

## Testing

- [ ] Existing TLS tests pass
- [ ] Manual RSS monitoring during certificate rotation shows stable native memory

body:
### Motivation

- Establish a formal, project-neutral operating architecture (EOS v10) that enforces separation between runtime, workshop, and active project and mandates first-moment orientation and strict claim/decision governance.
- Provide a runnable scaffold for the EOS v10 runtime so governance, pipeline, modules, doctors, and file-matrix contracts are available as composable artifacts rather than only documentation.
- Create a standalone `ENGINEER_OS_V10` release layout to allow cutover and migration from the legacy `.engineer` runtime.

### Description

- Added a high-level charter in `/.engineer/architecture/v10/00_ENGINEER_OPERATING_SYSTEM_CHARTER.md` and a layered architecture manifest at `/.engineer/architecture/v10/01_EOS_LAYERED_ARCHITECTURE.yaml` that define the EOS v10 layers, invariants, and pipeline.
- Introduced an EOS v10 runtime scaffold under `/.engineer/eos_v10/` containing `README`, `contracts/packets.yaml`, `doctors/doctor_manifest.yaml`, `indexes/index_manifest.yaml`, `kernel/runtime_identity.yaml`, `pipeline/eos_pipeline.yaml`, module manifests under `modules/`, schema `schemas/module_schema_minimal.json`, and a test scaffold in `tests/` and `playbooks/`.
- Added a standalone release tree `ENGINEER_OS_V10/` with core identity and orientation contracts, governance kernel and module contracts, pipeline lifecycle, file-matrix and doctor contracts, schemas (`08_SCHEMAS/claim_packet.schema.json`), tests, and a migration map, plus `ENGINEER_OS_V10/ENTRYPOINT.yaml` to bootstrap v10.
- Updated the existing `00_ENTRYPOINT.yaml` to bump the runtime version to `7.1.0` and to include the new EOS v10 charter, layered architecture, module contract, and EOS v10 runtime files in the `read_first` list.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this PR; the change adds test scaffolds and schema files for future automated validation such as `contract schema validation` and `pipeline stage continuity checks` listed in `/.engineer/eos_v10/tests/README.md` and `ENGINEER_OS_V10/09_TESTS/test_plan.md`.

Critical fix: Railway's "Root Directory" is set to keeper/, so the deployed container couldn't resolve `../src/lib/swap-pipeline`. Vendoring the file as `keeper/swap-pipeline.ts` (byte-identical to the canonical source) restores boot. Update keeper/index.ts to import from the local copy.

- No scanner, matcher, policy, migration, or inventory behavior changes.

author: blamechris
body:
## Summary

Fixes #22 — the validator regex for attribution footers was false-positiving on rule text that *describes* what NOT to do. Updated regex anchors to line start in the last 15 lines (where real footers always live).

## Root cause (corrected from original #22)

Original hypothesis was that Haiku was injecting attribution into outputs. Investigation showed the opposite — Haiku was faithfully preserving the rule text per system-prompt rule #3 ("Preserve ALL non-customizable sections EXACTLY as-is"), and the validator's regex was misreading the preserved rule.

For example, \`generic/autonomous-dev-flow.md:423\` contains:

\`\`\`markdown
1. **NO attribution** — No Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with Claude", no AI mentions anywhere. Zero Attribution Policy.
\`\`\`

The unfiltered regex \`Generated with[[:space:]]+Claude\` matches that line. So would the deployed customization. Pre-existing templates only deployed cleanly because the validator was added on May 19 (\`34fd147\`) AFTER they had already shipped.

\`decompose-issue\` (PR #21) was the **first new template** after May 19, and tripped this latent false-positive on all 14 managed repos.

## Change

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| \`grep -qE 'Co-Authored-By:?[[:space:]]*Claude\|Generated with[[:space:]]+Claude'\` | \`tail -n 15 \| grep -qE '^(🤖[[:space:]]+)?Generated with[[:space:]]+(\\[?Claude\|Claude Code)\|^Co-Authored-By:[[:space:]]+Claude'\` |
| Matches anywhere in output | Matches only line-start, only in last 15 lines |
| Matches "Co-Authored-By" optionally without colon | Requires colon + space (real footer format) |
| Matches "Generated with Claude" anywhere | Requires line-start, allows optional 🤖 prefix, prefers "Claude Code" or markdown-link \`[Claude\` |

## Verification

### True-positive coverage (should still flag real footers)

| Synthetic input | Result |
|---|---|
| \`🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://...)\` + \`Co-Authored-By: Claude <email>\` at end | ✅ flagged |
| Bare \`Co-Authored-By: Claude <email>\` at end | ✅ flagged |
| \`Generated with Claude\` on own line at end | ✅ flagged |

### False-positive coverage (should NOT flag legit rule text)

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| Rule text "no Co-Authored-By, no \\"Generated with Claude\\"" embedded in markdown rule list (\`autonomous-dev-flow.md\` etc.) | ✅ not flagged |
| Prose mention "we sometimes cite the Generated with Claude footer" buried deep in body | ✅ not flagged |

### Production sweep

Ran the new regex against **169 currently-deployed templates across 11 managed repos** (\`chroxy\`, \`exodus-loop\`, \`repo-relay\`, \`repo-memory\`, \`medlens\`, \`carebridge\`, \`MarchBorne\`, \`ltl\`, \`explAIn\`, \`readitation\`, \`archery-apprentice\`):

\`\`\`
Sampled 169 deployed templates. False positives: 0
\`\`\`

This means the next time any of those templates are re-deployed (e.g., when the user changes the corresponding customization), the validator will no longer reject them spuriously.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR
- [ ] Then in the follow-up "re-apply decompose-issue" PR, observe deploy CI passing validation on all 14 managed repos
- [ ] If a real attribution footer ever sneaks through (Haiku regression, etc.), the validator should still catch it — verified via synthetic injection tests above

## Out of scope

- Adding a permanent regression test harness (tracked in #25 — applies here too; the synthetic tests in this PR are ad-hoc)
- The decompose-issue template itself — re-introduced in the follow-up PR
