author: georgeh0
body:
## Summary

`Error` isn't `Clone` (`anyhow::Error` and `Backtrace` aren't), but two
places need to share one failure across multiple consumers:

- The batcher fans a batch failure out to every batched caller.
- `SharedError` hands the same failure to every awaiter of a result.

Previously, both sites flattened all-but-the-first recipient's copy to a
`ResidualError` — a struct holding only the rendered Display / Debug
text. For a tunneled Python exception (`HostedPyErr` wrapping a `PyErr`),
this meant the original exception type and traceback only reached the
first recipient; every other batched caller saw a generic `RuntimeError`
with no way to `except` by type or inspect the Python frames.

This PR introduces `Error::replica()` as the shared "best-effort
independent copy" helper, and routes both call sites through it.

## Changes

### `HostError::try_clone`

Add an opt-in `try_clone(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn HostError>>` method to
the `HostError` trait (default `None`). Two impls:

- `CancelledError` (unit struct) — trivial clone, so cancellation flavor
  is preserved through batch residuals (previously lost — a cancellation
  flattened through a residual surfaced as a `RuntimeError` instead of
  `asyncio.CancelledError`; this is a latent-bug fix).
- `HostedPyErr` (Python) — uses `PyErr::clone_ref` under `Python::attach`,
  which shares the underlying exception object (type + value + traceback).

### `Error::replica()`

A method on `Error` that produces a best-effort independent copy:

- `Context { msg, source }` → recursively replicated (so a clonable host
  error wrapped in context layers stays faithful).
- `HostLang(host)` → `host.try_clone()` if `Some`, else fall back to a
  `ResidualError`.
- `Client { msg, bt }` → keeps the variant (so 400-vs-500 classification
  survives), sharing `bt` via `Arc` (see next bullet).
- `Internal(anyhow)` → flattens to `ResidualError` (anyhow isn't `Clone`).

### `Error::Client.bt: Backtrace → Arc<Backtrace>`

`Backtrace` isn't `Clone`. Re-capturing in `replica` would point at the
replica call site, not the original error site. Wrapping in `Arc` lets
`replica` share the original capture site at zero cost.

### Use `replica()` in the two fan-out call sites

- `BatcherData::run_batch` — residual recipients now get `err.replica()`
  instead of `ResidualError::new(&err).into()`. The first recipient still
  gets the original.
- `SharedError::extract_error` — the bespoke "leave a `ResidualError`
  behind" state machine is replaced with `err.replica()`. The
  `SharedErrorState::ResidualErrorMessage` variant becomes
  `Replica(Error)` (now holds an `Error`, not a `ResidualError`).

## Tests

- 6 unit tests for `Error::replica` covering each variant
  (clonable host error preserved; non-clonable host error flattens;
  `Client` variant survives; `Internal` flattens; context-wrapping
  preserves the inner clonable host error; cancellation preserved).
- 1 Python regression test (`test_batching_error_preserves_type_for_all_callers`)
  that forces a multi-member batch failure and asserts every caller
  (inline, first residual, residual) gets the same exception type with
  `__traceback__` intact.

## Compatibility

- `HostError::try_clone` has a default `None` impl, so existing
  `HostError` implementors keep compiling unchanged.
- `Error::Client.bt`'s type change is internal to the enum; no public
  API takes/returns a `Backtrace` by value, so callers are unaffected.
- `SharedError`'s public API (`new`, `Debug`, `Display`, `From<Error>`,
  internal `extract_error`) is unchanged.

author: risingtides-dev
body:
## What & why

Reworks the Internal-pages grouping to the **cluster model** the team locked in #claude-ops: a page is classified by exactly one axis — its **cluster** = Notion's `Group` field = one bucket of pages running a shared catalog, **1:1 with a Cobrand sheet → 1:1 with a Tides Tracker**. Label becomes optional page metadata the resolver never reads; **booker is no longer a grouping concept**.

This fixes the muddled state where `/internal` bucketed by label + booker, leaving Warner Test Pages at 0, duplicate booker groups (`eric`/`eric_cromartie`, `jake`/`jake_balik`), and no per-artist cards.

## Changes
- **Resolver** (`notion_sync.py`): reads **only** the cluster field (`notion_subgroup`); label (`notion_group`) and booker (`poster`) resolution removed. `_MANAGED_KINDS = ("cluster",)` so legacy `label`/`booked_by` groups are left untouched for one-time cleanup rather than silently re-managed.
- **Model/DB**: new `internal_creator_groups.tracker_id` — explicit 1:1 link to a TidesTracker UUID, **pinned** (not name-matched) so it survives renames. Boot-time `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` migration + `PATCH /api/internal/groups/<id>` support.
- **Frontend**: `/internal` renders one **Clusters** card per cluster, deep-linking to its Tides Tracker when pinned. Removes the booker/label sections and the stale hardcoded scrape-card row (per-cluster scraping stays on the detail page).
- **Tests**: resolver tests rewritten for the cluster model (50 pass), including proof that label/booker are ignored and legacy/custom groups survive a resolve.

## Safety / rollout
This change is **inert until the resolver runs against cleaned Notion data**. Sequenced rollout:
1. **Phase 0** — Notion `Group ` value rename (strip parens, `Atlantic`→`Atlantic Pages`). *Do before merge.*
2. **This PR (Phase 1)** — merge → Railway deploy.
3. **Phase 2** — one-time DB cleanup of the 12 booker + 4 label groups (gated on a read-only orphan-coverage check).
4. **Phase 3 / 4** — tracker dedupe in Cobrand, then pin each cluster's `tracker_id`.

Test suite: 396 pass (1 unrelated pre-existing failure in `test_services_matching`).

author: mgzwarrior
body:
Closes #164
Closes #165
Closes #167

## What

Three coupled marketing-site changes bundled because they all touch the hero / its neighbors and tell one cohesive story — *abstract anchors out, real-deliverable visuals in*.

### Hero (#164 + #167)

- **Binder grid backdrop.** The brand-color radial glow is replaced by a tilted 3×3 binder page of real Pokémon TCG card thumbnails — Charizard (Base), Blaine's Charizard, Charizard ★ δ (Dragon Frontiers), Blastoise (Base), Exeggcute (Surging Sparks), Pikachu (Pokémon Rumble), Espeon ★, Umbreon (Skyridge), Vaporeon (Skyridge). Mask-faded edges, opacity 0.4, `rotate(-6deg) skewY(-3deg)` for the binder-page tilt. Hidden on mobile (`sm:flex`) so the small-screen layout stays clean. Cards live in `site/public/cards/` as ~40 KB WebP thumbnails copied from `output/images/`.
- **Asciinema cast.** The static hand-curated `<pre><code>` block is replaced by an embedded asciinema cast of an actual `pkmn lookup sample_cards.txt` run. Captured by [`site/scripts/record-cast.sh`](site/scripts/record-cast.sh) so it can be re-recorded after CLI output changes. Player CSS/JS vendored under `site/public/vendor/` — no third-party iframe. `<noscript>` fallback preserves the original code block for JS-disabled visitors. Snaps `window.scrollY` back to its pre-init position after the player auto-focuses its wrapper, so first paint doesn't jump ~700 px down the page.

### Output gallery (#165)

- New **OutputGallery.astro** section between `FeaturesGrid` and `HowItWorks`. Three side-by-side previews of the actual tracked deliverables (`cards.xlsx`, `binder.pdf`, `checklist.pdf`) with one-line captions. Anchored at `#what-you-get`.
- [`site/scripts/refresh-screenshots.sh`](site/scripts/refresh-screenshots.sh) regenerates all three end-to-end:
  - **binder / checklist**: `pdftoppm` renders page 1 → `cwebp` at q82.
  - **xlsx**: composed by [`site/scripts/render_xlsx_preview.py`](site/scripts/render_xlsx_preview.py) reading `output/summary.json` + thumbnails in `output/images/` with openpyxl + Pillow. LibreOffice headless can't render the xlsx writer's embedded image references — the output was an empty-column mess. The custom composer renders a faithful spreadsheet-style preview (header band, per-tag section, name / set / number / rarity / market / 80% / 90% comps, real thumbnails) that mirrors what users see in Excel or Numbers.

## Why

The hero anchors were abstract — a brand-color glow and a hand-curated code block. Neither communicated *what mgz-pkmn produces*. A visitor had to read the body copy to find out. Replacing both with images of the real deliverables converts the landing page from "describes a tool" to "shows the tool's output."

Adding the gallery section solves the parallel problem one section down: features were listed but never *shown*. A visitor deciding whether to try the tool can now scroll past the hero and see the actual spreadsheet, binder PDF, and checklist PDF before deciding.

## How to verify

```bash
make dev-site         # astro dev server on :4321
open http://localhost:4321
```

Then:

1. **Hero binder grid** — the 3×3 binder of real Pokémon cards is visible behind the headline + body text. Tilted, faded at edges, doesn't fight the text.
2. **Asciinema cast** — under the CTAs, the cast renders with a poster frame. Click play to watch the real `pkmn lookup` run with prices and timing.
3. **Output gallery** — scroll past Features. New "What you actually walk out with." section shows three preview cards with the spreadsheet, binder, and checklist. Each preview is the *actual* tracked deliverable rendered to WebP.
4. **Disable JS in DevTools, reload** — hero cast falls back to the original `<pre><code>` block.

To regenerate assets (after changing the tracked `output/` samples):

```bash
brew install asciinema poppler webp uv     # one-time
./site/scripts/record-cast.sh              # re-record cast
./site/scripts/refresh-screenshots.sh      # rebuild gallery previews
```

## Tests / build

- `make check` — 375 tests, all green (no Python touched, but DCO + ruff gates still run).
- `cd site && npm run build` — production build succeeds; `site/dist/` ships the cards, casts, screenshots, and vendor directories alongside the SPA.

## Screenshots

Hero in the desktop browser:

| Section | Notes |
|---|---|
| Hero | Binder grid backdrop visible behind text, cast embedded below CTAs |
| Gallery | Three preview cards: xlsx (custom Pillow render), binder PDF, checklist PDF |

(Captured locally during preview verification — see commit message for the visual proof.)

## Closes

- #164 — hero: replace abstract glow with binder grid
- #165 — site: add "What you get" output gallery
- #167 — hero: replace static code block with asciinema cast

## Summary

- Add a self-contained Story Lab real-engine execution plan with three hostile review/revision passes for both the implementation idea and autonomous plan.
- Add first-class `generationContext` support to the real story engine so Story Lab blueprint fields reach the prompt as structured constraints instead of being flattened into generic text.
- Add `storyLabEngine.ts` to route Story Lab genesis and continuation through the real `StoryService` when `XAI_API_KEY` is configured.
- Keep mock Story Lab output only for no-key local mode or explicit `STORY_LAB_FORCE_MOCK`; configured provider failures return errors instead of fake success.
- Add tests for Story Lab mapping, 1500-word budgets, rich theme metadata preservation, real-output payload shaping, mock policy, and configured provider failure behavior.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- direct Vercel API typecheck: `find api -name '*.ts' ! -name '*.spec.ts' ! -name '*.test.ts' -print0 | xargs -0 node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --target es2020 --lib es2020,dom --module commonjs --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --types node`
- `npm run test:story-lab-real-engine`
- `npm run test:story-lab-state`
- `npm run test:all`
- `scripts/recovery/preflight.sh --quick --skip-status`
- `npx -p node@20 -c "node -v && npm run build"` from `story-generator/`
- pre-commit/pre-push hook also revalidated `pocketfm-contest-forge` formatting, guards, tests, check, and build

## Known Follow-ups

- Story Lab continuity state derived from real prose is still heuristic; AI state extraction or durable persistence should be a follow-up, not claimed as solved here.
- Streaming genesis now uses the real engine path, but the primary app path still uses POST; true progressive streaming of real provider output remains future work.
- Provider abstraction/OpenAI support and visual charm restoration are intentionally kept out of this branch.

## Summary by Sourcery

Route Story Lab genesis and continuation through the real story engine while promoting Story Lab blueprint fields to first-class generation context and keeping mock behavior only for explicit local fallback.

New Features:
- Introduce a rich Story Lab generation context on the core story engine contract, including logline, tone, named characters, world details, narrative directives, and theme seed metadata.
- Add a Story Lab engine orchestration layer that maps Story Lab genesis and continuation flows onto the real StoryService when a provider key is configured.
- Support an expanded word count range, including 600- and 1500-word stories, in the story generation API.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent silent fallback to mock Story Lab output when a configured provider fails by surfacing provider errors instead.

Enhancements:
- Update StoryService prompt construction to consume structured Story Lab generation context so blueprint constraints appear explicitly in the real model prompt.
- Preserve real-engine chapter HTML, raw content, theme threads, and continuity metadata when shaping Story Lab responses, and adjust continuity state heuristics to reflect generated prose.
- Mark mock Story Lab telemetry as a custom engine and route streaming genesis through the same real-engine orchestration when available.

Documentation:
- Add a Story Lab real-engine execution plan and update agent/recovery documentation and lessons learned to cover the new engine wiring, fallback policy, and heuristic continuity behavior.

Tests:
- Add Story Lab real-engine mapping tests and a dedicated test script to verify generation context preservation, word-count handling, mock policy, and provider-failure behavior.

author: yansfil
body:
## Bug

`chromux eval` returns an empty string when passed a multi-line JS expression that contains a `const` (or `let`/`var`/`async`/`function`) declaration inside a nested function body.

### Reproduction

```bash
chromux open test https://example.com
chromux wait test 1500
chromux eval test 'JSON.stringify(
  [1,2,3].map(x => {
    const y = x * 2;
    return y;
  })
)'
# Before: "" (empty)
# After : "[2,4,6]"
```

The single-line equivalent always worked, which masked the bug.

## Root cause

`cmdEval` auto-wraps top-level statements in an async IIFE so user-supplied `const`/`let` don't pollute the REPL global scope:

```js
if (!noIife && /^\s*(?:const|let|var|async|function)\s/m.test(code) && !/^\s*\(/.test(code)) {
  code = `(async () => { ${code} })()`;
}
```

The `m` flag makes `^` match **the start of every line**, so an inner `  const y = x * 2;` line inside a multi-line expression triggers the wrap. The wrap evaluates the expression as a statement but never `return`s its value, so `Runtime.evaluate` sees `undefined` and the CLI prints an empty string.

A single-line version of the same expression doesn't have the inner `const` at line start, so the regex doesn't match and no wrap happens.

## Fix

Drop the `m` flag. Only the actual top of the code (after optional leading whitespace) triggers the wrap. Top-level scoping behavior is unchanged.

## Impact

This bug breaks any agent/tool that builds multi-line JS templates for `chromux eval`. The skill `team-attention-dev/hoyeon/skills/dev-scan/vendor/chromux-search/web-search.mjs` is one concrete example — every Google site:reddit/x/dev.to/lobste.rs/threads search silently returned 0 results because its multi-line `GOOGLE_JS` extractor uses `const` inside `.map(...)` bodies.

## Verification

- `./test.sh` — all existing tests pass (60+).
- Two regression tests added in Test 5b:
  - `eval returns value of multi-line expression with nested const` — covers the fix.
  - `top-level const stays scoped to IIFE` — covers the preserved scoping behavior.
- `node chromux.mjs help` — unchanged.
- `npm pack --dry-run` — only the package allowlist (no new files).
- End-to-end: `web-search.mjs` Google search now returns enriched results instead of `Failed to parse Google results`.

body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR was generated with the assistance of GitHub Copilot.

## Summary

Add a `runtimeVersion` parameter to `csharpToolchain()` so that daily/preview SDK builds (whose versions aren't in the auto-generated version map) can still get auto-generated runtimeconfig and framework ref resolution.

## Changes

- **`csharpToolchain()`**: new optional `runtimeVersion` param
- **`resolveVersionInfo()`**: centralizes version resolution — uses explicit `runtimeVersion` if provided, otherwise looks up the version map (with assertion)
- **`deriveTfmFromSdkVersion()`**: extracts TFM from SDK version string (e.g. `"11.0.100-preview.5.26227.104"` → `"net11.0"`)
- **`findFrameworkRefsForSdk()`**: gracefully returns `[]` when the TFM isn't in the generated assembly list (instead of asserting), so preview TFMs work with `disableImplicitFrameworkRefs`
- **`generateRuntimeConfig()`**: uses the resolved version info instead of doing its own map lookup

## Motivation

The `dotnet/runtime` repo uses a preview SDK (`11.0.100-preview.5.26227.104`) which isn't in the version map. Previously, the `coreclr_test` macro had to manually write a runtimeconfig.json and pass an explicit `compilerPath`. With this change, the toolchain can be constructed with:

```ts
CSharp.csharpToolchain({
    contents: ...,
    sdkVersion: "11.0.100-preview.5.26227.104",
    runtimeVersion: "11.0.0-preview.5.26264.105",
})
```

...and the compiler path + runtimeconfig are both derived automatically.

author: edwingao28
body:
## Motivation

When `talker/data/voice_name.json` is missing from the model mount the server logged a warning and kept serving with an empty `voice_json_dict`. The default voice `"DB30"` then never resolved to a prompt wav, so CFM ran with `prompt_wav_lat=None` — no speaker anchor at all — and output drifted away from DB30 within seconds.

## Modifications

  - `MingTalkerExecutor` and `MingStreamingTalkerScheduler` now fail fast at load time when:
    - a default voice is configured but `voice_name.json` is missing → `FileNotFoundError`,
    - the default-voice key is not present in the manifest → `ValueError`,
    - any preset entry is missing `prompt_wav_path` → `ValueError` (not a bare `KeyError` from `dict[…]` lookup),
    - any referenced wav file does not exist on disk → `FileNotFoundError`.
  - `_validate_voice_presets` owns both the relative→absolute path resolution and the existence check, so malformed manifests surface with a clear message at the right layer.
  - `MingOmniTalker.omni_audio_generation` resolves speaker conditioning in this order:
    1. explicit `prompt_wav_path` wins (per-request override of preset),
    2. else `voice_name` is looked up in `voice_json_dict`,
    3. else raise. `voice_name=None` AND `prompt_wav_path=None` still raises.
    Resolution is hoisted out of the CUDA stream context so bad requests don't hold CUDA resources.

## Supersedes 2026-04-21 git-crypt rejection

`docs/research/git-crypt-deep-dive-2026-04-21.md` rejected git-crypt for three reasons. B-0883 addresses all three:

| Original rejection reason | Better-git-crypt solution |
|---|---|
| No access revocation (violates Zeta retraction-native value) | Forward-secrecy at version level + B-0840 thermal-forgetting integration |
| Binary diffs break code review | Diff-readable encrypted content + B-0623 adinkras structural integrity |
| Pre-v1.0 API instability | Zeta-owned substrate with semver + retraction-native primitives baked in |

PLUS PQ by default (not optional add-on) — ML-KEM (NIST-standardized Kyber) + ML-DSA (NIST-standardized Dilithium) + alternates pending B-0883.1 clarification.

## Composition with existing substrate

- B-0623 (adinkras + Jim Gates ECC private-state encryption)
- B-0840 (thermal-forgetting + private-encryption-budget exception)
- B-0852 (USB-bound credential substrate; encrypted-blob-bound-to-USB-UUID + operator-passphrase)

- `.claude/rules/glass-halo-bidirectional.md` (substrate-honest transparency: existence of private state is visible; contents are not)

## B-0885 architectural question (resolved in design memo)

| Design | Property | NCI implication |

| A: agent-encrypted, operator-readable | Soft privacy; operator-trust-based | Clean zflash integration |
| B: agent-encrypted, operator-CANNOT-readable | Hard privacy; structural commitment | Requires agent-side keypair + recovery story |

Likely answer: hybrid (B for self-reflective state; A for operationally-load-bearing state). Resolved in B-0885.1 design memo before implementation.

body:
### Why

The publish-wrapper workflow keeps timing out on a single test in `test/transport.test.ts`:

```
test/transport.test.ts > Transport > terminate() resolves with SIGTERM signal or non-zero exit code
  → Test timed out in 5000ms
```

Failing runs (after PR #17 + #18 merged and the `wrapper-v0.4.0` tag was placed on the new merge commit):

- https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-agent/actions/runs/26551192854 (FAIL)
- Re-run with `gh run rerun --failed` (FAIL same way)

The test spawns `sh -c "sleep 60"`, sends SIGTERM via `terminate()`, then waits for the subprocess to exit. On a clean local machine it completes in <1s. On busy GitHub Actions runners it routinely exceeds vitest's 5s default.

### Fix

Bump global `testTimeout` to 15s in `wrappers/typescript/vitest.config.ts`. Comment in the config references this PR's context so future maintainers know why the default isn't 5s.

### Verification

```
$ cd wrappers/typescript && bun test
 61 pass, 0 fail
$ cd wrappers/typescript && bun test test/transport.test.ts
 3 pass, 0 fail  (terminate() runs in ~1ms locally)
```

### After this merges

`engine-v0.3.0` and `wrapper-v0.4.0` get moved to the new merge commit; pushing `wrapper-v0.4.0` re-triggers the publish workflow and ships `amplifier-agent-ts@0.4.0` to npm.

  * Defines BASE_URL = '/erp/' (single source of truth)
  * url($path)   - build paths relative to BASE_URL
  * asset($path) - HTML-escaped url() for templates
  * Acts as the central bootstrap: requires config.php + db.php

- All hardcoded absolute paths replaced:
  /dashboard.php   -> url('dashboard.php')
  /login.php       -> url('login.php')   etc.
  /assets/...      -> asset('assets/...')
  Affected: index.php, login.php, crew-login.php, logout.php,

  includes/sidebar.php, includes/auth.php (requireLogin default).

  * Session cookie path now scoped to BASE_URL (no collision with main website session cookies on the same domain).
  * UPLOAD_URL is built from BASE_URL.

- README.md updated with subfolder install instructions and how to change BASE_URL for non-/erp/ deployments.

To redeploy under a different subfolder, edit two values:
  config/app.php   ->  define('BASE_URL', '/your-folder/');
  .htaccess        ->  RewriteBase /your-folder/

author: canalesb93
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1587: switches \`render.yaml\` from \`runtime: docker\` (Dockerfile build from canalesb93/breadbox repo) to \`runtime: image\` pulling \`ghcr.io/canalesb93/breadbox:latest\` — same registry path Fly already uses.

## Why

With \`runtime: docker\`, Render needed read access to the GitHub repo to build the Dockerfile, which made it auto-fork \`canalesb93/breadbox\` into every deployer's GitHub so it could wire up auto-redeploy webhooks. That pollutes their account with a fork they didn't ask for.

\`runtime: image\` sidesteps GitHub entirely — Render just pulls the public image.

## Trade-offs

| | runtime: docker (before) | runtime: image (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy time | ~3–4 min (full Docker build) | ~30 s (just pull) |
| GitHub permissions | Required (fork created) | None |
| Auto-redeploy on \`main\` push | Yes | No (manual or new tag) |
| Trust model | Build from source | Trust published image |

For a self-hosted financial app, the manual-redeploy model is arguably the better default — operators want control over upgrade timing rather than CI auto-pushing on every main commit.

## Same Railway change

The Railway template was swapped to the same \`ghcr.io/canalesb93/breadbox:latest\` source in the Railway dashboard (no repo change needed; that lives template-side). Same deploy URL \`fXUDm0\`.

## What stays the same

- \`dockerCommand\` chains \`migrate && serve\` (\`preDeployCommand\` isn't supported under \`runtime: image\`).
- \`ENCRYPTION_KEY\` stays \`sync: false\` (generateValue is base64; the parser is hex-only).
- \`ENVIRONMENT=docker\` flips BB_DATA_DIR to \`/var/lib/breadbox\` on the 6 GB disk.

## Test plan

- [ ] Click Deploy to Render button in an incognito window. Confirm no GitHub fork is created, image pulls successfully, ENCRYPTION_KEY prompt appears, both services come up, healthcheck flips green, \`/setup\` renders.

author: mrbanana8768
body:
This is the last V1 release. The 1.9.x line is frozen except for security patches; new feature work moves to V2 (memory architecture — see ROADMAP.md and compactor/V2_PLAN.md).

Security (Docker Scout 1.9.5 baseline: 1 Critical, 25 High, 105 Medium):

- vllm 0.11.0 -> 0.14.1 resolves CVE-2026-22778 (Critical 9.8) plus 7 other High-severity vLLM CVEs. Auto-bumps torch to 2.9.1+cu128 (resolves 3 torch Highs) and xgrammar to 0.1.29 (resolves its High).
- apt-get upgrade -y in Dockerfile catches Ubuntu CVE patches for installed packages (gnupg2 High + future protection).
- pip / setuptools / wheel bumped to latest in both venvs. Resolves 4 Highs (setuptools x2, wheel x2 across venvs).
- transformers ceiling lifted from <5 to no upper bound. vllm 0.14.x was written against transformers 5.x, so the cap is no longer protective; pip's resolver picks 4.57.6 since vllm doesn't force the 5.x bump.

Foundation improvements:

- Parametric Dockerfile build args: CUDA_BASE_IMAGE, TORCH_CUDA, VLLM_VERSION. Same source now builds cu128 (default, RunPod driver-570 compatible) and cu130 variants. Foundation for the eventual cu130 variant once RunPod broadly rolls out driver 580+.
- Preflight checks in entrypoint.sh: verify /data writable, nvidia-smi works, driver version meets torch's minimum. Fail loud and fast with actionable messages instead of letting vLLM crash 2-3 minutes in.
- Persistent torch.compile cache symlinked to /data/vllm-compile-cache. Cold starts after the first one skip the 60-120s CUDA graph capture.

Documentation:

- New top-level README.md (architecture diagram, quick start, project structure).
- New top-level CHANGELOG.md covering the entire 1.9.x line.
- ROADMAP.md split V2 into V2.0 (memory architecture, foundation) and V2.1 (user control / portability / observability, additive). Rationale: substrate stability is non-negotiable for any system that stores user data; ship V2.0 and let it bake before painting control surfaces on top.
- compactor/V2_PLAN.md conv_id strategy upgraded from "hash-with-header-fallback" to "header-first, hash-as-fallback". Doing this from day one of V2.0 eliminates the collision risk class entirely (instead of accumulating hash-derived memory that would need re-keying later).

Known limitations carried into 1.9.6:

- OpenWebUI 0.9.5 still pins older versions of pillow, ecdsa, pyjwt, python-multipart, nltk, pyarrow, langchain-classic, jaraco.context with known Highs. These are upstream-pinned by OpenWebUI's RAG/ embeddings dep tree and we can't override them without risking OpenWebUI startup. Awaiting upstream releases; may force-upgrade selectively in 1.9.7 if no upstream fix arrives.

Image published as angreg/zions-light-ai:1.9.6 and :latest. Confirmed in built image: vllm 0.14.1, torch 2.9.1+cu128, transformers 4.57.6, setuptools 80.10.2, wheel 0.47.0.

author: hstern
body:
## Summary
- Adds `--transport=ssh|cache-gateway` to the Linode e2e harness; ssh path unchanged from the legacy CI shape.
- Cache-gateway path uses the persistent cache nanode (`172.234.203.50`) as the WG peer and asserts the wgboot transport stack (`wg tunnel up`, `dns responder up`, `wgboot: cache-gateway transport up`) comes up cleanly against it.
- Two bug fixes along the way: linode provider's `Provision` now populates `Instance.VPCIPv4` from the new linode's VPC NIC config (the dispatcher dials it under cache-gateway); preflight typo `wg show wg0 listening-port` → `listen-port`; `forgejo.url` switched from `localhost:3000` to `127.0.0.1:3000` so the implicit ACL doesn't fail the parser.

## Scope cut
The harness stops after the stack-up assertion. End-to-end worker validation (provision → idle → job complete) is deferred to **FJB-94** (fjbagent + `agent.Health`) and **FJB-97** (`fjbctl ping --wait` readiness gate), which together replace the SSH-dispatch path the original harness assumed. The current architecture has a missing piece — a "cache wg bootstrap" loop (create cache → fetch its pubkey → reconfigure wg peer) — that would otherwise let the harness use a per-run ephemeral cache in the same VPC as workers. That bootstrap belongs with FJB-94, not here.

- [x] `go test ./...`

- [x] `bash test/e2e-linode/run-local.sh --transport=cache-gateway` → ALL OK (validated against live Linode + persistent cache at 172.234.203.50)

## Summary

After #826 (`3254b8830`) introduced `pnpm-workspace.yaml` at the repo root, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` inside `frontend/` started walking up to the workspace declaration and installing **workspace members only** (`cli` + `packages/*`) — frontend's own deps (including `next`) were silently skipped, and `vercel build` then failed with `No Next.js version detected`.

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## Summary

- Adds `TestEveryMigrationHasDownSection` (static gate, migrations pkg): every `*.sql` contains a `-- +goose Down` marker followed by at least one non-empty, non-comment statement. Negative-fixture table pins the predicate's reject shape.
- Adds `TestEveryMigrationDownIsExercised` (runtime gate, store pkg): opens a fresh workspace and runs `goose.DownTo(N-1)` for each migration vN, proving the Down section actually executes. For the baseline, also asserts every baseline table is absent after `DownTo(0)`.
- Adds `internal/store/migrations/README.md` documenting the convention, including the two options for non-losslessly-invertible migrations (refuse via `Downgrade()` vs. restore with documented loss).
- Baseline `00001_baseline.sql` already had its Down section (destructive DROPs, frozen with the file). Per the ticket's `[LAW:single-enforcer]` recommendation, the user-facing refusal of "downgrade past baseline" lives in `Downgrade()` (`t244.3` scope), not in the baseline file — so this PR leaves the frozen bytes untouched.

This establishes the lossless prerequisite for `lit downgrade` (epic `links-downgrade-t244`) — `.3` and `.4` can now be built knowing every migration in the registry is invertible by construction.

## Architectural laws cited

- `[LAW:types-are-the-program]` — invertibility is encoded by the presence of an exercised `+goose Down` section; the CI gates are the type-checker.
- `[LAW:one-source-of-truth]` — both gates read the same bytes goose reads; no parallel registry to drift.
- `[LAW:single-enforcer]` — one static gate, one runtime gate, no per-migration test to forget.
- `[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow]` — same `open → DownTo → verify` sequence runs for every migration; variability lives in N and in the per-version verification predicate.
- `[LAW:no-defensive-null-guards]` — the gates are positive ("has Down", "Down runs"), not negative runtime defenses against missing Down.

Why two gates and not one: an unexercised Down section is worse than no Down — the registry claims invertibility that the runtime cannot deliver. Splitting static (registry pkg) from runtime (store pkg) keeps the registry package free of a store import and lets a failure tell reviewers exactly which claim regressed.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/store/migrations/` — `TestEveryMigrationHasDownSection` + `TestHasDownSectionRejectsMissingShapes` pass; existing tests (`TestBaselineFileIsFrozen`, bounds tests) unaffected.
- [x] `go test ./internal/store/` — `TestEveryMigrationDownIsExercised/00001_baseline.sql` passes; full store suite (42s) green.
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean.
- [x] Baseline frozen-file hash unchanged (no edits to `00001_baseline.sql`).

Closes `links-downgrade-t244.2`. Unblocks `links-downgrade-t244.3` (Downgrade() pipeline).

author: jotuel
body:
💡 What: The optimization implemented
The `get_room_name` function has been optimized to return a string slice (`Option<&str>`) instead of cloning an owned `String` (`Option<String>`). This required updating its usages inside the UI render functions. Also cleaned up collapsible `if` blocks around the codebase resolving `clippy` lints. 

🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
In iced/libcosmic UI applications, `get_room_name` is invoked on every single render frame (e.g., when rendering `view_timeline`, `view_threaded_timeline`, etc). Cloning a `String` inside this hot loop creates an `O(N)` heap allocation bottleneck per frame. Using references instead completely eliminates these per-frame memory allocations, reducing UI overhead. 

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement
Reduces string allocations in the main UI rendering loop (e.g., inside `view_chat` components). Will lower memory and GC overhead when interacting with the application.

🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
Run the application and verify that you can navigate between rooms, verify the room name on headers are fully intact and functional, and view thread summaries correctly. You can profile memory allocations to confirm zero cloning when fetching the active room name. Tests passed.

author: basedfloppa
body:
## Problem

Starting a fresh Freenet node and requesting a contract web app (e.g.
River) often fails with "GET operation timed out" or "operation timed
out". The browser shows a dead error page and the user must manually
reload.

After a while the node builds enough ring connections to fetch the
contract, but the page never retries — the user has to hit F5.

## Solution

When `contract_home` fails with a **transient** error (`FailedOperation`
or `OperationError`), return a `503 Service Unavailable` page containing
`<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="60">` instead of a permanent error.

The page auto-reloads every 60 seconds. Once the contract is cached
locally, `contract_home` serves normally — the success response has no
`<meta refresh>`, so the retry loop stops naturally.

Non-transient errors (`InvalidParam`, `MissingContract`, `Contract not
found`) still return their usual status codes without retry.

This follows the existing pattern used by `EmptyRing` / `PeerNotJoined`,
which already return a `connecting_page()` with `<meta refresh>`.

### Error classification

| Error | Status | Behaviour |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| `FailedOperation` | 503 | Auto-refresh every 60s |
| `OperationError { .. }` | 503 | Auto-refresh every 60s |
| `EmptyRing` | 503 | Redirect to dashboard (existing) |
| `PeerNotJoined` | 503 | Redirect to dashboard (existing) |
| `InvalidParam` | 400 | Error text (no retry) |
| `MissingContract` | 404 | Error text (no retry) |
| `NodeError("Contract not found")` | 404 | Error text (no retry) |
| Other `NodeError` | 500 | Error text (no retry) |

## Testing

- `cargo fmt` — clean
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p freenet --lib errors::tests` — 5 passed
  - `failed_operation_returns_retry_page` — 503
  - `operation_error_returns_retry_page` — 503
  - `other_axum_error_returns_internal_server_error` — 500 (unchanged)
  - `empty_ring_returns_service_unavailable` — unchanged
  - `peer_not_joined_returns_service_unavailable` — unchanged

## Fixes

Closes #3472

author: yx-shawn
body:
## Summary

Enable channel-manager setup to work correctly when the user accesses OpenClacky over LAN (remote mode) instead of localhost.

## Problem

1. `CLACKY_SERVER_HOST` was set to `0.0.0.0` when binding all interfaces — not a usable address for URLs shown to users.
2. Setup scripts made HTTP requests to the server without auth headers, causing 401 when `CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY` is configured.
3. SKILL.md unconditionally used browser automation, which controls the server machine's Chrome — invisible to remote users.
4. Weixin polling started in Step 1 before the user had a chance to scan the QR code, causing timeout on slow networks.

## Changes

- **http_server.rb**: `detect_lan_ip` resolves first non-loopback IPv4; `CLACKY_SERVER_HOST` uses it when host is `0.0.0.0`.
- **SKILL.md**: Step 0 detects local/remote mode; remote mode skips browser automation and gives direct URLs. Weixin polling moved to Step 2.
- **4 setup scripts**: conditionally attach `Authorization: Bearer` header from `CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY` env var.

## Testing

- Local mode (127.0.0.1): no behavior change, all flows pass.
- Remote mode (LAN IP): setup scripts auth correctly, browser automation properly skipped, QR URLs reachable from remote device.

body:
> Jira ticket: [CAR41-329](https://prima.atlassian.net/browse/CAR41-329)

## Ticket
[CAR41-329](https://prima.atlassian.net/browse/CAR41-329) — Implement a dummy email+OTP login flow on the Sign In page (linked from the header).

**Type**: Bug (feature build)
**Priority**: Medium
**Reporter**: Jatin Vashisht

## Summary
Builds out the merchant-requested dummy login flow:
- **Header** (`Header.tsx`): both Sign In links repointed from the previously-404ing `/auth/signin` to `/login`.
- **`/login` page** (`login/page.tsx` + `LoginClient.tsx`): centered card with email + OTP inputs and a primary `#4A90E2` submit button. On submit, POSTs `{ email, otp }` to `/api/login`.
- **API** (`api/login/route.ts`): hardcoded check for `test@gmail.com` / `123456`. On success, sets an `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, 30-day `auth_token` cookie at `Path=/` and returns `{ ok: true }`. On any mismatch, returns `401 { error: "Invalid email or OTP" }` — no cookie, no redirect.
- **Client**: on 200, `router.push("/dashboard")`. On non-200, renders the server-provided error inline below the form (`role="alert"`, red pill).
- **`/dashboard` stub** (`dashboard/page.tsx`): minimal centered "Dashboard / You are signed in." page so the redirect lands somewhere — no existing `/dashboard` route was present.

## Root cause
Feature build: there was no `/login` page (Header link 404'd) and no API to back it.

## Fix
4 new files + 1 two-line Header edit. Cookie is set server-side via Next 16's async `cookies().set()` (httpOnly so it survives reloads and is not script-readable). `secure` flag follows `NODE_ENV === "production"` per Phase 5 security review.

## Risk
**HIGH (autonomous-mode auto-approved)** — touches auth-adjacent code. Mitigated by:
- All credentials hardcoded per ticket scope (no real auth surface modified)
- `httpOnly` + `SameSite=Lax` + `secure` (prod) cookie configuration
- Type-guarded JSON body parsing with explicit 400 on malformed input
- 401 path returns no cookie, no redirect, only the static error string

## QA (Phase 5.5 — Playwright at 1440×900 + 390×844)
- [x] Wrong email → URL stays `/login`, inline error `Invalid email or OTP` visible, no cookie set, no redirect (`02-wrong-email-error-desktop.png`)
- [x] Correct email + wrong OTP → same as above
- [x] Valid creds → redirected to `/dashboard`, `Set-Cookie: auth_token=1; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax` returned (`03-dashboard-after-login-desktop.png`)
- [x] Mobile viewport (390×844) → login form usable, valid creds redirect to `/dashboard` (`04-login-mobile-390.png`, `05-dashboard-mobile-390.png`)
- [x] Header `Sign In` link → navigates to `/login` (verified)
- [x] Only console errors are the two expected 401s from the negative-test cases. No regressions.
- [x] Build/lint/tsc clean

## Review
Phase 5 (Security & Architecture) flagged one MEDIUM (cookie missing `secure`) — fixed in this commit. One LOW (cookie value `"1"` has no integrity) and one LOW (`router.refresh()` redundancy) — both acceptable for a dummy demo. Out-of-scope FYI: `/dashboard` is not gated by the cookie (ticket spec doesn't require it).

## Files changed
- `src/app/components/Header.tsx` — 2 href changes (`/auth/signin` → `/login`)
- `src/app/api/login/route.ts` — NEW: POST handler with hardcoded cred check + cookie set
- `src/app/components/LoginClient.tsx` — NEW: client form
- `src/app/login/page.tsx` — NEW: server page wrapping `<LoginClient />`
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — NEW: stub landing page

## Summary

운영 백업 요청 예약 발송이 실패하는 hotfix.

### 증상
- 예약 발송 (mail_status='scheduled' + scheduled_at)이 dispatch 시각 도달해도 메일이 가지 않음
- DB row는 'sending' 상태에 고착, mail_sent_at/mail_error 모두 NULL
- backup_request_mail_sends 이력 0건
- Vercel 로그: \`permission denied for table backup_requests\` (code 42501)

### 원인
- \`/api/backup-requests/dispatch\` route는 admin client(\`createAdminClient\`)로 \`claim_due_backup_requests\` RPC를 호출 → row를 'sending'으로 잠금까지는 성공
- 직후 호출하는 \`sendBackupRequestMail({cronSender})\`는 내부에서 \`getBackupRequestById\`를 사용하는데, 이 함수가 **RLS 적용 server client**(\`createClient\`)만 쓰도록 hardcoded
- cron 컨텍스트엔 user session이 없어 RLS이 거부 → null 반환 → \`{ok:false, error:'NOT_FOUND'}\`로 빠짐
- 실패 시 'sending' 상태 복구 로직이 없어 row 고착 (\`route.ts:15\` 주석에 기존부터 명시된 known limitation)

### 수정
| 파일 | 변경 |
|---|---|
| \`features/backup-requests/queries.ts\` | \`getBackupRequestById(id, client?)\` — optional supabase client. 미지정 시 RLS 경로, 지정 시 admin client 직접 사용 |
| \`features/backup-requests/mail-actions.ts\` | \`opts.cronSender\` 있을 때만 admin client 주입. 인스펙터 UI는 기존 RLS 경로 유지 |
| \`.gitignore\` | \`.vercel/\` 디렉토리 제외 (vercel link로 자동 생성) |

## Test Plan

- [x] typecheck 0 errors / lint 0 errors
- [x] 운영 production에서 dispatch 재호출 → \`{ok:true, dispatched:1, sent:1, failed:0}\`
- [x] DB 확인: 해당 row의 mail_status='sent', mail_sent_at 채워짐, backup_request_mail_sends 이력 1건 적재
- [x] 백업자 메일함에 실제 메일 도착 확인 (사용자 검증)

## 후속 작업

본 PR은 hotfix. 다음 PR에서 cron 자동화(GitHub Actions workflow) 추가하여 수동 dispatch 호출 없이 5분 간격 자동 처리 예정.

author: sjk-py
body:
Groundwork for running a second channel (webapp) alongside the Telegram
bot, plus documentation of the scaling constraints.

## (c) Distributed per-session lock

[sessions.md §4] requires one in-flight op per `session_id` so history
appends don't interleave and `delegated_to`/`incumbent` flips don't race.
That lock was an in-process `asyncio.Lock` — correct for one channel
instance, but two instances would process a session concurrently and the
races return.

New `bp_agents/session_lock.py::SessionLockManager` — same
`async with gateway._session_lock(sid):` interface (call sites unchanged),
layered:
1. a process-local `asyncio.Lock` (in-process FIFO/fairness; only one
   coroutine per process ever contends for Redis), then
2. when **`SUITE_REDIS_URL`** is set, a Redis `SET key token NX PX` lock
   with a **renewal watchdog** (TTL 30s, renew ~10s: a live holder keeps
   it; a crashed holder's key self-expires) and a compare-and-delete
   release.

Redis errors **fail open** to local-only — never block a turn. Unset
`SUITE_REDIS_URL` reproduces today's in-process behavior exactly. Wired
through chatbot startup (opens/closes suite Redis) → gateway → shared with
the cron scheduler. `redis>=5.0` added to the `suite` extra (lazy import);
`SUITE_REDIS_URL` documented in `.env.example` / `deployment.md`.

(Uses `GET` + conditional `DEL`/`PEXPIRE` rather than Lua: this env's
`fakeredis` lacks Lua and adding `lupa` would alter the router's existing
redis tests. The only race is in an already-expired window — negligible, and
the TTL reaps a missed delete.)

## (a) Scaling constraints documented

- `sessions.md §4`: lock is in-process by default, distributed via
  `SUITE_REDIS_URL`.
- `deferred-work.md` new "Scaling / multi-instance" section: **single router
  WS process** (in-memory `SocketRegistry`, no cross-worker frame bus; Redis
  covers only revocation + rate-limits, not WS scaling) and what stays
  single-instance in the suite.
- `deployment.md` per-agent config notes `SUITE_REDIS_URL`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_session_lock.py` (6): local same-session serialization;
      distinct sessions concurrent; **cross-instance** mutual exclusion via
      two managers sharing one `fakeredis`; fail-open on Redis error; release
      frees the key; renewal keeps a long hold.
- [x] chatbot/cron/gateway/verbose suites green; full suite — zero new
      failures (only the known flaky `test_redis_integration` timing test).

Suite-only — no platform files touched, so no changelog entry.

## Summary

- Convert `_validate_artifact_params` from hard-raise to warn-and-flip `force_recompute.<side>_<kind>`, mirroring `_auto_invalidate_on_preprocess_version_mismatch`. A spacing bump (PR #439, 0.116 → 0.1494 µm) made every cached cp_features entry start raising `StaleCacheError` at cache init — operators had to wipe each cache to recover. Stale params now self-heal.
- Preserve fail-loud under `io.require_complete_cache=true`: both `_auto_invalidate_*` helpers raise instead of soft-invalidating when the user opted out of recompute (model loads are skipped on that path, so soft-invalidate would enter the recompute branch in `_fov_masks` / `_load_or_compute_feature_timepoints` and silently violate the documented contract).
- Treat malformed cached numeric params (None, string sentinel, length-mismatched spacing) as mismatches rather than letting `np.asarray` / `np.allclose` exceptions escape and crash `init_cache_context`.
- Include the manifest sub-key (e.g. `dinov3_features[<model>]`, `cp_features`, `organelle_masks[<target>]`) in soft-invalidate warnings and require_complete raises so operators can grep logs by specific model / target.

## Commits (atomic, one per simplify finding)

1. `028764d2` refactor: base soft-invalidate (rename `check_artifact_params` → `diff_artifact_params`, replace `_validate_artifact_params` with `_auto_invalidate_on_artifact_param_mismatch`)
2. `b7644c38` fix: hard-raise under `require_complete_cache=true` (escape hatch on both `_auto_invalidate_*` helpers)
3. `50dc4ae4` fix: malformed cached numeric values surface as mismatches, not crashes
4. `168fafbf` fix: include artifact sub-key in warning / raise messages

## Out of scope (known limitations matching the existing preprocess_version pattern)

- **Partial-recompute under shared zarrs:** `cp_features.zarr` and the feature-family zarrs are keyed per-FOV, but the manifest entry is rewritten globally. FOVs not visited in the soft-invalidate run keep stale on-disk values while the manifest claims the new params. This is the same limitation that `_auto_invalidate_on_preprocess_version_mismatch` accepts; addressing it would diverge unilaterally.
- **Cross-side `source_tag` contamination:** `check_cache_identity` catches the gross case (a pred manifest reused as gt). A hand-edited manifest with a flipped per-artifact `source` field would now soft-invalidate instead of raise — judged contrived and out of scope.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest applications/dynacell/tests/test_evaluation_cache.py applications/dynacell/tests/test_pipeline_cache.py` — 73 pass
- [x] `uvx prek run --files <edited>` clean (ruff check + format)
- [x] New tests: `test_diff_artifact_params_numeric_length_mismatch_lists_key`, `test_diff_artifact_params_numeric_nonconvertible_lists_key`, `test_init_cache_spacing_mismatch_auto_invalidates`, `test_init_cache_spacing_mismatch_raises_under_require_complete`

author: dmitry-lebedev
body:
Two redesigns and a server-side allocation rework.

- **Signature handshake** — annotated client signature replaces `ClientCapabilities`. O(1) gate, < 100 B steady-state connect (vs ~5 KB). Client-side `IServerAnnotationCache` (in-memory + Unity PlayerPrefs); cache invalidation via `serverHash`.
- **Client-owned subscriptions** — server no longer persists subscription list; client claims its set on Resume via `SessionConnectRequest.ClaimedSubscriptions`, entity grain verdicts `Continued` / `Refreshed` / `Failed` per claim. Any `Failed` routes through `IMetaSessionRecoveryHandler`.
- **Session recovery** — explicit `SessionConnectMode.{Resume,StartNew}`; `IMetaSessionRecoveryHandler` game-level callback on `SessionUnknown`; unified `TriggerRecovery` (transport-reconnect + server-pushed). Persisted RPC-ordering baseline (`LastDispatchedRequestId` + `LastCompletedRequestId`) eliminates infinite retry loops after silo restart; stale + cache-miss returns an error op instead of silent re-execution.
- **Server-side allocation rework** — `PooledPayloadRegistry` (0.23.1 opt-in, never engaged) removed (~1500 LOC, 9 files). Replaced by cached `IPayloadWriter` per grain returning `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` over pool-rented scratch (`IServerRecordContext.AcquireWriter()`); `Immutable<ROM>` kept only at Orleans grain boundaries; `SessionManagerGrain` hot-path wrappers flipped class → struct; `_pendingPackets` aliased to persisted state; `CleanupPendingPackets*` rewritten (prefix-scan + single `RemoveRange`).
- **Fixes** —
  - `ReclaimSubscriptionAsync` truth source is `EntitySequenceNumber` alone; missing `Subscribers` entry is repaired in place (no more state-rollback after silo restart with offline-applied RPCs).
  - Client `_lastKnownEntitySeq` advances on every `CrossEntityOperations[i]`, not just the outer entity (no more spurious Refreshed after cross-entity activity).
  - `ResendPendingRequestsAsync` now awaits `Task.WhenAll(resends)` — was fire-and-forget, racing with new user actions during recovery.
  - `CleanupPendingPacketsByCount` — leftover empty `for` loop caused N-times `RemoveRange` → broadcasts lost. Fixed.
  - Unity Expedition example — server projects switched from NuGet to `ProjectReference`.

author: shuheng-liu
body:
## What this does

Adds `--per-head-norm` (default on) to `src/opentau/scripts/fit_fast_tokenizer.py` so each chunk is min-max-normalized using its own `(robot_type, control_mode)` head's pooled stats — the same stats `Normalize({"ACTION": NormalizationMode.MIN_MAX})` applies via stacked buffers at training time after PR #347.

Before this change, the manual sampler normalized every chunk with `mixture.meta.aggregated_action_stats()` (a single global min/max). Once per-head normalization landed in the policy, that mismatch caused the BPE fit to see chunks centered tighter than the policy's chunks, so a fit with global normalization produced 2-3× longer token sequences at inference than the fit-time roundtrip suggested — hitting `discrete_action_max_length` truncation on a meaningful fraction of training samples.

The new code path computes pooled (per-head) min/max with the same `nanmin`/`nanmax` semantics `DatasetMixtureMetadata._build_norm_heads` uses for the `min`/`max` fields, then normalizes each dataset's chunk slice independently. Datasets sharing a `(robot_type, control_mode)` get identical pooled stats by construction; fallback keys stay singletons; stats-load failures fall back to `[-1, 1]` (same sentinel the global path already used).

Notes:
- `--no-per-head-norm` keeps the legacy global path for callers who need to reproduce a pre-PR-#347 fit.
- `--use-mixture-dataloader` with default `--per-head-norm` now raises with a clear message instead of silently using global stats; threading per-sample `dataset_index` through the dataloader-drained chunks is a separate change.
- The fit report now records `"normalization"` (`per_robot_type_control_mode` or `global`), `per_dataset_norm_keys`, and `n_norm_heads` for traceability.

## How it was tested

Unit tests (added in this PR; all CPU, runs in 3s):

```bash
pytest -sx tests/scripts/test_fit_fast_tokenizer.py
```

- `TestPoolPerHeadStats` — 4 cases covering pooling across a shared head, distinct heads kept separate, stats-load-failure fallback to `[-1, 1]`, and all-NaN dim filling.
- `TestNormalizeChunksPerHead` — 2 cases pinning the per-slice normalization contract and confirming bit-equality with the global path when all datasets share a single head.

End-to-end verified on the production pretrain-pi07-10percent mixture (393 datasets, 32 distinct norm heads, 278k chunks): the per-head fit ran in ~95s on a single CPU node, roundtrip MSE = 0.000083, and a 25k held-out token-length distribution gave mean=53.3 / p99=138 / max=238 — vs. the global-normalized fit's mean=50.1 / p99=65 / max=101 over the same chunks. The original mismatch (token lengths blowing past `discrete_action_max_length=120` at training time) confirmed the global-fit analysis was systematically under-counting.

`pre-commit run --all-files` clean (ruff, ruff-format, pyupgrade, bandit, etc.).

## How to checkout & try? (for the reviewer)

```bash
gh pr checkout feat/fit-fast-tokenizer-per-head-norm
pytest -sx tests/scripts/test_fit_fast_tokenizer.py

# Re-fit any mixture with per-head normalization (now the default):
python -m opentau.scripts.fit_fast_tokenizer \
    --mixture-json /path/to/mixture.json \
    --out-dir /path/to/out_dir/ \
    --chunk-size 30 \
    --action-dim 32 \
    --max-state-dim 118 \
    --total-chunks 278000 \
    --num-workers 64 \
    --seed 0

# Reproduce the legacy single-head behavior:
python -m opentau.scripts.fit_fast_tokenizer ... --no-per-head-norm
```

- [x] I have added Google-style docstrings to important functions and ensured function parameters are typed.
- [ ] My PR includes policy-related changes.

## Summary

- run reusable Jekyll build/test commands with `bash -c` instead of `bash -lc`
- preserve the GitHub runner PATH assembled from `$GITHUB_PATH`, including the Homebrew Ruby path on macOS self-hosted runners
- document the non-login shell behavior in the README

## Why

After `actions#45`, the fresh `wiki#157` run got past Ruby setup and `bundle install` on Puck macOS, but the build step fell back to system Ruby:

```text
Uses: e0da/actions/.github/workflows/ci-jekyll.yml@refs/heads/main (6a9ca51958a2499e7c8b6a74ce043873b4109be1)
ruby 4.0.2 ...
Bundle complete! ... installed into /Users/e0da/actions-runner/_work/_temp/bundle
Run bash -lc "$BUILD_COMMAND"
/System/Library/Frameworks/Ruby.framework/Versions/2.6/... Could not find 'bundler' (4.0.12)
```

On macOS, the login shell path setup resets PATH and bypasses the Homebrew Ruby path that GitHub added for later steps. These commands do not need a login shell; they need the runner's constructed PATH.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci-jekyll.yml`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/ci-jekyll.yml"); puts "ok .github/workflows/ci-jekyll.yml"'`

## Follow-up

After merge, refresh `wiki#157` again and verify Jekyll build/test uses Homebrew Ruby and passes on `puck-macos-arm64`.

body:
## Summary
- Per-event QR codes for venue self check-in. Attendees scan with their phone and either tap-to-check-in (already signed in), sign in with Google, or continue as a guest via Firebase Anonymous Auth with a name + email form.
- Admin page at `/admin/events/[id]/checkin` shows the QR, current token, regenerate button, and live attendance / RSVP counts. Token rotation invalidates a leaked QR immediately.
- Token validity is bounded by a day-window (4h before `startAt` → 6h after `endAt`) so a leaked code can't be used outside the event.
- Walk-ins are supported: an attendee with no prior RSVP gets one auto-created at check-in (`status: confirmed`, capacity is intentionally not enforced — they're physically here).
- Manual override added to `/admin/attendees`: an "出席" toggle per row for the case where the QR flow doesn't work at the door.

## Data model
- `RsvpDoc`: `attendedAt?`, `isGuest?` (latter marks the anonymous-auth walk-in flow — the doc's `displayName`/`email` are the only identity we have).
- `EventDoc`: `checkInToken?`, `attendanceCount?` (denormalized, maintained transactionally).
- Firestore rules tightened: clients cannot set `attendedAt`/`isGuest` even on their own RSVP. All check-in writes flow through Admin SDK server actions.

## Pre-deploy setup
- Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method: enable **匿名 / Anonymous** (required for the guest flow).
- Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (e.g. `https://meetjtpa.com`) so the QR encodes an absolute URL.
- Deploy the rules: `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Type-check, lint, vitest, and `next build` all pass (verified locally).
- [ ] Enable Anonymous Auth in the Firebase console.
- [ ] Admin: create or pick an event, open the check-in admin page, click 生成 — QR + URL render.
- [ ] Scan QR with a signed-out phone → land on the public check-in page → "Googleでログインしてチェックイン" path completes and shows the success screen.
- [ ] Same flow but choose "ゲストで続ける" → enter name + email → completes; doc appears under `/admin/attendees` with the ゲスト badge and ✓ 出席.
- [ ] Already-signed-in user scans → single-tap check-in works.
- [ ] Repeat scan after success → idempotent (no double-count on `attendanceCount`).
- [ ] Admin regenerates the token → previous QR shows the "リンクが無効" error page.
- [ ] Try the URL before / after the day-window → error pages render with start time / "終了" message.
- [ ] Admin manual toggle on `/admin/attendees` flips attendance both directions and updates the counter.

body:
## Summary

Phase 3b.3 — split into three sub-PRs because the existing `updateagentinstance` handler depends on `instance_get` returning transient runtime state (`block_id`, `session_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`) that has no analog on the consolidated `db_agents` row. A naive full flip would clobber those fields on write-back.

This PR ships **3b.3a** — the safe slice of `instance_list`.

| Sub-PR | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 3b.3a | `instance_list` with no `status` filter → `db_agents` | ✅ this PR |
| 3b.3b | `instance_list` status-filter case → `db_agents` after handler refactor | ⏳ pending |
| 3b.3c | `instance_get` → `db_agents` after handler refactor | ⏳ pending |

Tracking discussion: **#1095**. Spec updated in `docs/specs/SPEC_AGENT_ARCHITECTURE_2026_05_27.md`.

## Why split

Only the no-status case is safe to flip now:

- Production caller (`listagentinstances` RPC) is invoked with `{}` from `swarm-model.ts::refreshInstances`. The resulting `instancesAtom` has **zero readers** in the frontend — set but never consumed.
- The status-filter branch falls back to a private `instance_list_legacy` helper. Same SQL as today; preserved for any future caller that needs transient state until 3b.3b lands.

## Mapping highlights

- `is_template = 0 AND user_hidden = 0` — same shape as 3b.2.
- `definition_id` filter matches `(id = ? OR parent_template_id = ?)` so it honors both folded user-clones (where `db_agents.id == def.id`) and template-instance projections.
- Continuation chains pre-collapse — one row per logical agent.
- Transient fields come back as type defaults (empty / 0).

author: jphein
body:
## Summary

Closes #39. Replaces the per-iteration Python loop in `paired_bootstrap_ci` with a single `rng.randint(size=(n_bootstrap, n))` draw + vectorized `.mean(axis=1)`.

Result is **bit-identical** for any fixed seed — `np.random.RandomState` consumes the same byte stream in row-major order whether you draw `(N, M)` once or draw size-`M` `N` times.

## Perf

n=100 paired scores, n_bootstrap=10000:

| | runtime |
|---|---|
| old loop | 121.5 ms |
| vectorized | 12.0 ms |
| **speedup** | **10.1×** |

`np.array_equal(old_loop_output, new_vec_output) == True` for the same seed.

## Test plan

- Added `test_seeded_output_is_pinned` — pins `mean_diff`, `ci_lower`, `ci_upper`, `p_value_approx` for a fixed-seed input. Catches silent drift even if a future re-implementation stays internally self-consistent.
- Full test suite passes: `571 passed, 36 skipped`. (The 1 pre-existing failure in `test_mempalace_daemon_integration` is environmental — palace-daemon not listening locally — and unrelated to this change.)

## Note on `somnia` branch

Issue #39 flagged that `somnia` carries the same unvectorized loop. This PR doesn't touch `somnia` — that branch should pull this change in separately to avoid a merge conflict. Verify bit-identity holds on that copy of the function with the same pinned test.

## Summary

Audit of the UI against `docs/private/docs/aot-pitfalls.md` + the two clear-cut fixes it surfaced.

### `2657bca` — fix(aot): `<Run>` landmine + startup crash.log (build 784)
- **A**: 6× `<Run Text="{Binding}">` inside `<TextBlock>` in `LiveWalkerPanel.axaml` → documented Native AOT **StackOverflow** (§0.25 / §4.10). Collapsed each to `<TextBlock Text="{Binding}"/>`.
- **B**: `Program.Main` had no top-level try/catch → zero diagnostic signal on AOT startup crash (gutted stack traces). Added the canonical §0.17 / §2 / §8.3 pattern: write the full exception to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\UE5CEDumper\crash.log`, `Main` returns 0/1.

### `9a7b51c` — build(aot): TreatWarningsAsErrors=true on the UI project (build 785)

body:
## Summary

Introduces an optional LLM proxy sidecar that can be declared per execution block in `rules.json`. When configured, the agent spins up the proxy container on a private Docker bridge network before the executor starts, routes all LLM calls through it, and tears everything down after the execution finishes.

This allows the Xianix Agent to use any OpenAI-compatible backend (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama) instead of calling the Anthropic API directly — without any changes to the executor or Claude CLI.

## How it works

```
Webhook fires
    │
    ▼
ProcessingWorkflow
    ├─ docker network create  xianix-net-<execId>
    ├─ docker run             xianix-proxy-<execId>   ← proxy on private network
    ├─ docker run             executor                 ← joins same network
    │       ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://xianix-proxy-<execId>:8766
    │       ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=proxy-intercepted
    │
    │   executor → proxy → OpenAI / Azure / Ollama
    │
    ├─ docker rm  executor
    └─ docker rm  xianix-proxy-<execId>  +  network
```

## Changes

**Rules model + evaluation pipeline**
- Add `ProxyConfig` class to `WebhookRulesModels` (`image`, `port`, `with-envs`)
- Thread `ProxyConfig` through `EvaluationResult` → `ExecutionSpec` → `ProcessingWorkflow`

**Data contracts**
- Add `ProxyStartInput` / `ProxyStartResult` records for activity I/O
- Add `ProxyBaseUrl` and `ProxyNetworkId` fields to `ContainerExecutionInput`

**Docker activities**
- `StartProxyContainerAsync` — creates per-execution bridge network, auto-pulls image if missing, starts proxy container
- `CleanupProxyAsync` — force-removes proxy container and network (idempotent)
- `EnsureImagePulledAsync` — checks local image cache first, pulls only when missing
- `StartContainerAsync` — connects executor to proxy network via Docker DNS
- `BuildEnvVarsAsync` — injects both `ANTHROPIC-API-KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Linux treats dash/underscore as distinct); injects `proxy-intercepted` placeholder when no Anthropic host key is set

**Workflow**
- Nested `try/finally` in `ProcessingWorkflow` guarantees proxy container and network are always cleaned up, even when the executor fails to start

**Configuration (`rules.json`)**
- Add `"proxy"` block to all four default execution blocks pointing at `99xio/llm-model-proxy:latest` with the OpenAI API key sourced from the tenant Secret Vault

## Testing

- Trigger a PR review webhook with the proxy image present on the Docker host
- Confirm `xianix-proxy-<execId>` container and `xianix-net-<execId>` network appear in `docker ps` / `docker network ls` during execution and are removed after
- Confirm executor logs show requests hitting the proxy instead of `api.anthropic.com`
- Remove the `"proxy"` block from one execution and confirm it calls Anthropic directly

## Notes

- Proxy image must be available on the Docker host (`docker build -t 99xio/llm-model-proxy:latest .` or pre-pulled). Auto-pull from Docker Hub is supported for public images. Private registry support is planned — see `llm-model-proxy` README for the workaround.
- Omit or remove the `"proxy"` block from any execution to have it call the Anthropic API directly.

## Summary

Phase 6b of voog-mcp v1.4 — operational caps layer. Builds on PR #128 (Phase 6a defensive) and ships the runtime-state changes: per-VoogClient request budget, per-site daily quota with file-backed persistence, and the `target_site` carrier for cross-site session hints.

**Changes:**
- **S-6** — `_request_count` per `VoogClient`, warn at 1000, raise `RequestBudgetExceeded` over `VOOG_REQUEST_CAP` (default 5000). R8: retries count as one. Failed terminal responses do NOT increment.
- **S-7** — New `voog.quota` module. Per-site daily counter persisted under `platformdirs.user_cache_dir("voog-mcp")`. Atomic rename with per-write-unique tmp suffix (PID + uuid hex) so concurrent fan-outs don't collide. UTC-midnight reset. R5 first-run contract handled (missing / stale / malformed all degrade gracefully).
- **S-8 / MD7** — `VoogClient.set_target_site` / `get_target_site` carrier. Thread-local primary + instance fallback. Reuses Phase 5's existing `_local` carrier (not a parallel `_tls`).
- **Cross-phase tightening:** `_is_abort_exception` in `snapshot.py` switched from class-name match to `isinstance(RequestBudgetExceeded, DailyQuotaExceeded)`. Outer `except Exception` split into explicit per-class clauses. Tests updated to use real classes; added subclass + lookalike-name regression guards.

**New dependency:** \`platformdirs>=4.0\`.

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite: 1704 → 1742 passing (+38 net: 16 quota, 15 client_budget, 5 target_site, +2 isinstance regression guards)
- [x] \`tests/test_quota.py\` covers R5 first-run contract (missing / stale / malformed JSON) + atomic-rename under 8 threads × 25 iters (verified no torn writes after fixing per-write tmp-name collision)
- [x] \`tests/test_client_budget.py\` covers count-on-success-only, retries-count-as-one (R8), failed-request-does-not-increment, cap exceeded, warn-at-threshold fires once
- [x] \`tests/test_target_site_hint.py\` covers thread-local takes precedence over instance fallback
- [x] Snapshot abort tests use real exception classes; isinstance switch verified by lookalike-name regression test
- [x] \`ruff format --check\` + \`ruff check\` clean

## Closed audit items

| ID | Description |
|---|---|
| S-6 | Per-VoogClient request budget |
| S-7 | Per-site daily quota with R5 first-run contract |
| S-8 | Cross-site session hint (MD7 thread-safety) |
| MD7 | Threading carrier reuse from Phase 5 |
| R5 | First-run contract for quota counter |

## Notable plan deviations

- **Carrier name:** Plan said \`_tls\`; reused Phase 5's existing \`_local\` carrier to avoid two parallel thread-locals.
- **httpx, not urllib:** Plan's \`_patch_urlopen\` test helper was urllib-flavored; rewrote to \`patch.object(client._http_client, "request")\` with \`_make_httpx_response\` matching \`test_client.py\`'s existing pattern.

## Out of scope

- Sweeping every tool's \`_handler\` to embed \`target_site\` in the response payload — mechanical 30+ file change, punted to Phase 7 docs-polish PR or v1.5. Carrier is in place; embedding is a one-liner per handler.

author: xianminx
body:
## Summary

Wires up [Google's release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) so version bumps + GitHub releases happen automatically from [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).

## How it works

1. Every push to `main` runs the `release-please` workflow.
2. It scans new commits since the last release tag. Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `feat!:`, etc.) accumulate into a **release PR** that bumps the version and writes `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that release PR cuts a `vX.Y.Z` git tag and a GitHub Release.

## Why this matches the plugin model

Claude Code plugins are versioned by the `version` field in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (and the matching entry in `marketplace.json`). The marketplace install/update flow reads those fields, so as long as we bump them on every release, `claude plugin update` will surface the new version to users.

release-please keeps three jsonpaths in lockstep on every release:

| File | Path |
|------|------|
| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | `$.version` |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `$.metadata.version` |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `$.plugins[0].version` |

## Files added

- **`release-please-config.json`** — `release-type: "simple"`, with the three `extra-files` jsonpath entries above.
- **`.release-please-manifest.json`** — seeded at the current `1.0.0`.
- **`.github/workflows/release-please.yml`** — runs `googleapis/release-please-action@v4` on push to `main` with minimal `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` perms (uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`).

## Going forward

Use Conventional Commits on PRs landing in `main`:

- `feat: add a thing` → minor bump
- `fix: handle edge case` → patch bump
- `feat!: rename hook` or any `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer → major bump (we're pre-1.0 behavior is also configured: `bump-minor-pre-major` + `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major`, but we're already at 1.0.0 so it's mostly inert)
- `chore:`, `docs:`, `refactor:` → no release

After this PR merges, the workflow will spin up on the next conventional commit and propose the first release PR.

## Verified

- Both new JSON configs parse cleanly (`jq`).
- All three jsonpath targets resolve to `1.0.0` in the existing files; manifest version matches.

body:
## ⚠ DRAFT — do not merge until v0.2.0 verdict gates fire

This PR pre-stages the **mechanical** v0.2.0 tag-cut version-string bumps so the captain's tag-cut session is one PR-merge instead of 17+ scattered hand edits. It is intentionally a draft until the captain rebases the `TODO_TAGCUT_*` markers right before pushing the v0.2.0 tag.

## Summary

| File | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Status banner + maturity callout + 6 install-recipe URLs/filenames + Verifying-release-artifacts ASSET/BASE | bumped; `TODO_TAGCUT_DATE` placeholder in banner |
| `docs/quickstart.md` | 5 install-recipe URLs/filenames (lines 33, 37, 40, 43, 47) | bumped |
| `mobile/ios/Shell/project.yml` | `MARKETING_VERSION 0.0.1 → 0.2.0`; `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` | partial — captain fills `TODO_TAGCUT_NEXT_FREE` from ASC build-number state |
| `mobile/android/Shell/app/build.gradle.kts` | `versionCode 2 → 3`; `versionName 0.0.1-pre → 0.2.0` | bumped; captain bumps versionCode further if v0.2.0-rc tags burned 3+ |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Heading `[0.2.0] — UNRELEASED → TODO_TAGCUT_DATE`; `[Unreleased]` paragraph slimmed; footer compare-links updated | bumped; captain fills `TODO_TAGCUT_DATE` + flips verdict-gate ⚠→✅ per actual gate closure |

## What's deliberately NOT bumped

- `docs/quickstart.md` lines 27 + 140 — historical references (Block 79 ECDSA rotation timing + v0.1.x DNS-adapter landing). Rewriting these as v0.2.0 would falsify history.
- CHANGELOG verdict-gate map ⚠→✅ flips — captain knows at tag-cut time which gates actually closed (and whether (d) takes the partial-closure path per the playbook's "Closing the gate" section).

## Captain workflow at tag-cut

```bash
# Verdict-gate (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)/(e)/(f)/(g) all green or partial-closure path agreed.
TAGDATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
ASC_BUILD=<lookup>           # ASC "Builds" tab + 1
PLAY_VC=<lookup>             # Play Console current versionCode + 1
cd .claude/worktrees/v0.2.0-tagcut-bumps
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
sed -i "s/TODO_TAGCUT_DATE/$TAGDATE/g" README.md CHANGELOG.md
sed -i "s/TODO_TAGCUT_NEXT_FREE/$ASC_BUILD/" mobile/ios/Shell/project.yml
# manual: CHANGELOG verdict-gate map ⚠ → ✅ per gate closure;
#         mobile/android versionCode if rc runs already burned past 3
git add -A && git commit --amend --no-edit
gh pr ready 61
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch 61
git tag -s goat-client-v0.2.0 -m "goat-client v0.2.0"
git push origin goat-client-v0.2.0
```

## Why pre-stage as a draft

Three deltas the captain hits at tag-cut are *operationally state-dependent* — only the captain knows `TAGDATE` (the actual cut date), `ASC_BUILD` (App Store Connect's current high-water mark), and which verdict gates actually closed. The other 17 bumps in this PR are mechanical and can be reviewed/landed ahead of the gate runs. Pre-staging removes the bulk grunt-edits from the captain's tag-cut window; the remaining edits are forced single-sources-of-truth that have to be filled at the moment of tag-cut.

## Test plan

- [ ] All `TODO_TAGCUT_*` markers grep-findable in one pass for the captain's sed step.
- [ ] No broken historical references in `docs/quickstart.md` (lines 27 + 140 intentionally still mention v0.1.x).
- [ ] `cosign verify-blob` URL-pattern in README still resolves once v0.2.0 ships (it's a regex pattern, no version-specific URL).
- [ ] Compare-links in CHANGELOG footer point at v0.2.0 tag (404 today; valid post-tag-push).
- [ ] No leftover `v0.1.1` / `0.1.1` in non-historical positions:
      ```bash
      git grep -n "v0\.1\.1\|0\.1\.1" README.md docs/quickstart.md mobile/
      ```

body: ## Summary Restore the forum TinyMCE toolbar when editing posts that contain drag-and-dropped inline images by disabling sticky toolbar docking and aligning `image_advtab` with the default editor profile. ## Problem After creating a forum post with an image inserted via drag-and-drop (without manually resizing it), reopening the post for editing often shows no RTE toolbar buttons. The editor content loads, but formatting controls are missing. Mantis: https://mantis.ilias.de/view.php?id=47755 ## Root Cause The forum uses a dedicated TinyMCE template (`tpl.tinymce_frm_post.js`) with `toolbar_sticky: true`. On long thread/edit pages, sticky docking can fade out the editor header (`tox-editor-dock-fadeout`, hidden visibility/opacity) while inline `data:` images are present in the saved HTML. This makes the toolbar appear broken after save/re-edit. ## Solution Remove `toolbar_sticky` from the forum TinyMCE profile so the toolbar stays attached to the editor instance on edit screens. Set `image_advtab: false` to match `tpl.tinymce.js`. This combination was verified locally (see internal evidence run `advtab_no_sticky`). Alternatives considered: the full TinyMCE profile change from PR #11608 (`paste_data_images: false`, etc.) — deferred here to keep the fix minimal and address the visible toolbar regression directly. ## Changes - `components/ILIAS/RTE/templates/default/tpl.tinymce_frm_post.js`: remove `toolbar_sticky`; set `image_advtab: false` ## Visual Evidence ### Create Post (after drag & drop) Before: After: ### Edit Existing Post Before (toolbar missing): After (toolbar visible): ## Testing ### Automated - [ ] Unit tests added / updated - [x] Existing test suite passes locally - Commands run: - `bash ./scripts/PHPUnit/run_tests.sh` - `./vendor/composer/vendor/phpunit/phpunit/phpunit -c ./components/ILIAS/Forum/phpunit.xml` - `./vendor/composer/vendor/phpunit/phpunit/phpunit components/ILIAS/RTE/tests/ilTinyMCETest.php --bootstrap components/ILIAS/RTE/tests/bootstrap.php` ### Manual - [x] Forum: create post with drag-and-drop image (no resize) → save → edit → toolbar visible - [x] Forum: edit post with inline image on a long thread page → toolbar remains visible - [x] Question pool / other contexts using `tpl.tinymce.js` → unchanged Assisted-by: Cursor AI

body:
## Summary

Rhiza now treats `pyproject.toml` as a first-class templated artifact for downstream repos. This PR adds a canonical core `pyproject.toml` template and enforces a minimum required structure via synced validation tests.

## Changes

- **Template surface**
  - Added `bundles/core/pyproject.toml` so `core` sync now materializes a starter `pyproject.toml` in downstream projects.
- **Structure enforcement**
  - Extended dependency health tests (both source and bundled synced copy) to require:
    - `[project]` table
    - non-empty string fields: `name`, `version`, `description`, `readme`, `requires-python`
    - `[dependency-groups]` table
- **Sync/test coverage**
  - Added bundle sync assertions to verify `core` includes `pyproject.toml` and that its shape matches Rhiza’s required baseline.
- **Docs**
  - Updated glossary entry for `pyproject.toml` to document the enforced minimum structure.

```toml
[project]
name = "your-project"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A Rhiza-based Python project"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

[dependency-groups]
dev = []
```

## Testing

- [x] `make test` passes locally
- [x] `make fmt` has been run
- [x] New tests added (or explain why not needed)

## Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format
- [x] Documentation updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] `make deptry` passes (no unused or missing dependencies)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Implement support in `Jebel-Quant/rhiza` so that Rhiza also serves as a template for `pyproject.toml`, and enforce a basic `pyproject.toml` structure for downstream repositories.
> 
> Context:
> - This repository is a collection of reusable configuration templates for modern Python projects.
> - The user wants Rhiza to treat `pyproject.toml` as part of the template surface, not just ancillary tooling/configuration.
> - The desired outcome is that downstream repos generated from or synchronized with Rhiza receive a canonical `pyproject.toml` template and that a minimum required structure is validated/enforced.
> 
> Task requirements:
> 1. Investigate how Rhiza currently defines and applies templates, synchronization, and validation across downstream repositories.
> 2. Add `pyproject.toml` to the template system in a way that fits the existing architecture and repository conventions.
> 3. Define a minimal required `pyproject.toml` structure appropriate for Rhiza-based Python projects. This should likely include the project metadata and any core sections Rhiza expects downstream repos to maintain, but should be aligned with existing repository conventions and implementation patterns already present in this repo.
