body: ## Summary Filters third-party Plausible analytics noise from client-side Sentry reporting. These events are not application bugs. ## Error signatures addressed - `TypeError: Failed to fetch (plausible.io)` — [SOKOSUMI-NQ](https://masumi.sentry.io/issues/121884772/) - Related: [SOKOSUMI-5J](https://masumi.sentry.io/issues/SOKOSUMI-5J/) ## Root cause Plausible is loaded via Google Tag Manager (not application source). When beacon requests to `plausible.io` fail—commonly due to ad blockers, privacy extensions (`frame_ant.js`, `injectScriptAdjust.js`), or network issues—the Plausible script surfaces an unhandled promise rejection. Sentry's global `onunhandledrejection` handler captures it (~206 events, 0 users impacted). Stack traces contain only third-party frames (Plausible script, browser extensions, Sentry fetch instrumentation)—no Sokosumi application code. ## Fix - Added `beforeSend` filter in `instrumentation-client.ts` to drop Plausible fetch failures by message and stack signature - Added `ignoreErrors` and `denyUrls` for the known Plausible pattern - Unit tests in `src/lib/sentry/__tests__/third-party-error-filter.test.ts` ensure first-party `Failed to fetch` errors are not dropped ## Validation - `pnpm --filter web test src/lib/sentry/__tests__/third-party-error-filter.test.ts` - `pnpm --filter web check` ## Remaining risk - Other GTM-loaded analytics hosts (e.g. Google Analytics) could produce similar noise with a different hostname; extend `THIRD_PARTY_ANALYTICS_FETCH_HOSTS` if new patterns appear - Legitimate Plausible outages would also be filtered (acceptable trade-off for non-critical analytics)

## Summary

Decomposes `search.svelte.ts` (923 lines) into four focused collaborators, each independently testable with no cross-cutting dependencies:

| File | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `search.svelte.ts` | 282 | Worker lifecycle, wiring, `search()` |

author: propodeum
body:
## Summary

- Introduces a behavioral-continuity substrate. `Agent.run(input, thread_key=...)` loads a per-thread `Message` prefix from a configured `ThreadStore` before `_execute` and appends the run's new messages on successful completion, so a subsequent run on the same key sees prior assistant turns, tool calls, and tool results as its own conversation history.
- New public surface under `nanitics.composition`: `ThreadStore` protocol, `InMemoryThreadStore` reference implementation, `ThreadLocks` per-key serialization. `ThreadInUseError` on concurrent same-key runs (re-exported from `nanitics.errors`). `Agent.__init__` gains `thread_store` and `thread_locks`; `Agent.run` gains a `thread_key` keyword. `AgentResult.thread_key` and `AgentStartEvent.thread_key` / `replayed_message_count` are additive.
- Replayed messages bypass the `<nanitics:context>` wrapper by design — the model treats them as its own prior turns. On suspend, the prefix snapshots into `RunCheckpoint.state`; the resume uses that frozen view. Only `ReActAgent` consumes the prefix in this phase.

Implements the [`temp/sdk-thread-identity/`](temp/sdk-thread-identity/) plan.

## Test plan

- [x] `just check` — auto-fix, format, lint, mypy, guide snippets, SDK tests all pass.
- [x] 100% line coverage on the new `nanitics/composition/threads/` module and the new branches in `Agent.run` / `_run_in_span` / `_load_thread_prefix` / `_peek_resume_thread_context` / `_new_messages_after_prefix`.
- [x] Existing 4118-test suite green (one orchestrator subclass needed its `_execute` signature updated to forward `thread_key`).
- [ ] Live-provider validation: `just validate validation/threads/` (real Anthropic call; verifies behavioral continuity across two runs).

## Summary
- **F5 sweep (29 sites)**: every `on Object catch` fallback in the data layer embedded raw exception text (`Failure.X(message: e.toString())` / `'<ctx>: $e'`) into `Failure.message`. `failure_ui` surfaces message via the `AuthFailure` passthrough and `kDebugMode` branches, so HiveError box names / key paths / stack fragments could reach the UI. author: copilot
body:
This PR adds automated npm publishing for package releases in the monorepo. On `master` pushes, it publishes only packages whose `packages/*/package.json` `version` changed.

- **Workflow entrypoint**
  - Added `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`.
  - Triggers on `push` to `master` with path filter `packages/*/package.json`.

- **Version-change detection**
  - Compares `github.event.before` vs `GITHUB_SHA` for changed package manifests.
  - Parses old/new `version` values and keeps only packages with an actual version delta.
  - De-duplicates package directories before publish.

- **Selective publish execution**
  - Configures Node + npm registry auth.
  - Iterates detected package directories and runs `npm publish --provenance` per package.
  - Skips publish step when no package version change is detected.

```yaml
changed_files=$(git diff --name-only "$before_sha" "$GITHUB_SHA" -- 'packages/*/package.json')
# ...
if [ -n "$new_version" ] && [ "$old_version" != "$new_version" ]; then
  pkg_dir=$(dirname "$file")
  packages="${packages}${pkg_dir}"$'\n'
fi
# ...
(cd "$pkg" && npm publish --provenance)
```

## Summary
This PR introduces a reusable `ModelPicker` component to standardize model selection across the application, replacing scattered inline input fields and dropdowns. It also updates model catalogs to reflect current API offerings and adds per-provider model overrides for TTS.

## Key Changes

### New Component
- **ModelPicker** (`src/settings/ModelPicker.jsx`): A unified component that renders a preset dropdown (when available) plus a "Custom…" option for freeform model IDs. Simplifies model selection UI across image providers, Art Director, and TTS settings.

### Model Selection Refactoring
- **CodexSection**: Replaced hardcoded model inputs for Pollinations, Replicate, and OpenAI image providers with `ModelPicker`, using metadata from `IMAGE_PROVIDER_META`.
- **Art Director model selection**: Now uses `ModelPicker` instead of plain text input.
- **TTSRow**: Integrated `ModelPicker` for TTS model selection when provider supports multiple models.

### Model Catalog Updates
- **LLM providers** (`src/llm/providers.js`): Updated model IDs to current published versions:
  - Gemini: `gemini-3.5-flash` → `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.0-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`
  - OpenAI: `gpt-5.x` → `gpt-4.1` family
  - DeepSeek: `deepseek-v4-flash` → `deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-reasoner`
  - Qwen, Kimi, Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras: Updated to current model IDs
  - Added `claude-opus-4-7` to Anthropic options

- **Image providers** (`src/llm/imaging.js`): Added `models` arrays with tier metadata:
  - Pollinations: `flux`, `flux-realism`, `turbo`
  - Replicate: `black-forest-labs/flux-schnell`, `flux-1.1-pro`, `sdxl`
  - OpenAI: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3`, `dall-e-2`

- **TTS providers** (`src/tts/catalogue.js`): Added `models` arrays and updated defaults:
  - OpenAI: `tts-1` (default), `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts`
  - Voxtral: `voxtral-mini-2503` (default), `voxtral-2507`
  - ElevenLabs: `eleven_multilingual_v2` (default), `eleven_turbo_v2_5`, `eleven_flash_v2_5`

### TTS Model Overrides
- **App.jsx**: Added `ttsModelOverrides` state to track per-provider model selections independently of voice settings.
- **TTSController**: Extended `setProvider()` to accept optional `model` parameter; added `setModel()` method.
- **SettingsModal**: Wired up `onChangeTtsModel` callback to update overrides.

### Migration & Cleanup
- **App.jsx**: Added `MODEL_MIGRATIONS` table to automatically upgrade old fabricated model IDs to current published ones on load.
- Removed unused imports: `REPLICATE_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `POLLINATIONS_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `OPENAI_IMAGE_DEFAULT_MODEL` constants from CodexSection (kept in imaging.js).
- Removed `FREE_MODELS_BY_PROVIDER` usage in favor of direct `PROVIDER_META` lookups.

### Documentation
- **README.md**: Updated model tables to reflect current offerings and added note about Free model selection covering image provider, Art Director, and TTS models.

## Implementation Details
- `ModelPicker` uses a controlled component pattern with `value` and `onChange` props.
- When presets are available, it shows a dropdown; selecting "Custom…" reveals a text input for arbitrary model IDs.
- When no presets exist, only the text input is rendered.
- Model metadata includes `id` and optional `tier`

body:
## Summary

`docs/dogfooding-findings.md` §1 で記録した「Workflows DB が integration \"HOKUSAI\" に share されていない → 同期 outbox 全滅で 404」運用穴の解消ガイドを既存 `notion-dashboard-operation-guide.md` に追加。

Notion の権限モデルでは「親ページに integration を share しても **子 DB は自動継承されない**」という落とし穴があり、`notion-setup` 後に各 DB（Workflows / Pull Requests / Review Issues）を **個別に** integration に share する必要がある。これを知らないと `cleanup` / `workflow_started` 同期等で常時 404 になる。

## 追加内容

### `docs/notion-dashboard-operation-guide.md`

- **「2.2.1. 生成された DB を integration に share（重要）」** セクションを追加:
  - 必須手順 4 step（DB ページを開く → ⋯ Add connections → integration 選択 → 3 DB 繰り返す）
  - `--scaffold` 時の Documentation 配下サブページは share 不要である旨
  - **自己診断**: `hokusai start` 起動時に自動チェックが走る（PR #83 の `check_db_share_health()`）、明示的に手動チェックする場合は Python REPL ワンライナーで `dispatcher.check_db_share_health()` を呼ぶ
  - **トラブルシューティング表**（症状 / 原因 / 対処 の 3 ケース）

### `README.md` / `README_JP.md`

- Notion dashboard セットアップセクションに **⚠️ 警告ブロック**を追加し、新セクションへ直接リンク
- 「Missing share is the #1 cause of `NotionAPIError: 404`」と明示

## 効果

これで §1 運用穴の解消手順が docs として整備され、**新規 user / 既存 user が share 漏れに気付く前に対処できる状態**になる。`hokusai start` 起動時の自動チェックと組み合わせて、share 漏れの早期検出と修正の両方がガイドされる。

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

PR #3 of the public-API stack — waldoctl half. PR #3 folds in what was
originally PR #4 (the diff-edit GUI) so the MCP server in Waldo-Commander
can route LLM edits through a real propose/approve/reject lifecycle
instead of overwriting program source.

- ` programs.py`: replace the \`NotImplementedError\` stubs on
  \`EditFlow.propose / approve / reject\` with real bodies, plus an
  inline ~80-line unified-diff parser/applier (no new deps). \`EditFlow\`
  carries a \`_program\` back-ref set in \`Program.__post_init__\` so
  \`approve\` mutates the parent's \`source\` in place. Diffs are
  validated at \`propose\` time; drift between propose and approve
  raises \`ValueError\`; unknown ids raise \`KeyError\`.
- \`settings.py\`: add \`McpSettings\` (\`enabled\` / \`host\` / \`port\`
  / \`auth_token\` / \`allow_motion\`). Defaults are off and
  loopback-only — surfacing the API is opt-in. \`allow_motion\` is
  consulted on every motion tool call so the user can flip it live.
- \`__init__.py\`: export \`McpSettings\`.
- Tests: 7 new \`EditFlow\` behaviour tests covering happy path, drift
  detection, unknown-id, double-approve, multi-hunk, binding
  propagation; 3 new \`McpSettings\` tests.

author: ajcvickers
body:
Models the EF Core provider's review system, adapted for this repo's
smaller surface: a single flat src/MongoDB/ tree, four functional file
groups, two test projects.

AGENTS.md hierarchy (each with a CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md shim):
- root: tech stack (multi-target net10/net8/netstandard2.1/net472,
  AOT-compat, MEVD/driver pinning), commands, area + reviewer table.
- src/MongoDB/: provider internals — pipeline overview, per-file-group
  area sections, boundaries with MongoDB.Driver and MEVD ProviderServices,
  common pitfalls (_id swap, local-skip semantics, AOT/trim attribution).
- test/MongoDB.UnitTests/: mocking patterns and unit-test conventions.
- test/MongoDB.ConformanceTests/: MEVD spec-suite inheritance,
  Testcontainers Atlas Local, and the search-index rebuild dance.

Reviewers in .claude/agents/ (9 total vs the EF Core provider's 14):
- area: collection-, mapping-, search-, public-api-reviewer
- test infra: conformance-reviewer
- cross-cutting (every run): api-stability-, mevd-conformance-,
  security-reviewer
- external-PR-only: pr-summary-reviewer

Slash command at .claude/skills/review-mevd-provider/SKILL.md: three
modes (local range / external PR / external clone), --iterate loop with
[fix-in-code]/[external-action] x [blocking]/[substantive]/[nit] tags,
file-pattern mapping table adapted to the flat src/MongoDB/ layout.

.claude/settings.json pre-approves dotnet build/test and docker info so
reviewer dispatches don't trigger per-command prompts.

This PR updates [redis](https://pypi.org/project/redis) from **2.10.6** to **8.0.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.5.3
   ```
   * Restore try/except clauses to __del__ methods. These will be removed
      in 4.0 when more explicit resource management if enforced. 1339
  * Update the master_address when Sentinels promote a new master. 847
  * Update SentinelConnectionPool to not forcefully disconnect other in-use
      connections which can negatively affect threaded applications. 1345
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.2
   ```
   * Tune the locking in ConnectionPool.get_connection so that the lock is
      not held while waiting for the socket to establish and validate the
      TCP connection.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.1
   ```
   * Fix for HSET argument validation to allow any non-None key. Thanks
      AleksMat, 1337, 1341
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.0
   ```
   * Removed exception trapping from __del__ methods. redis-py objects that
      hold various resources implement __del__ cleanup methods to release
      those resources when the object goes out of scope. This provides a
      fallback for when these objects aren't explicitly closed by user code.
      Prior to this change any errors encountered in closing these resources
      would be hidden from the user. Thanks jdufresne. 1281
  * Expanded support for connection strings specifying a username connecting
      to pre-v6 servers. 1274
  * Optimized Lock's blocking_timeout and sleep. If the lock cannot be
      acquired and the sleep value would cause the loop to sleep beyond
      blocking_timeout, fail immediately. Thanks clslgrnc. 1263
  * Added support for passing Python memoryviews to Redis command args that
      expect strings or bytes. The memoryview instance is sent directly to
      the socket such that there are zero copies made of the underlying data
      during command packing. Thanks Cody-G. 1265, 1285
  * HSET command now can accept multiple pairs. HMSET has been marked as
      deprecated now. Thanks to laixintao 1271
  * Don't manually DISCARD when encountering an ExecAbortError.
      Thanks nickgaya, 1300/1301
  * Reset the watched state of pipelines after calling exec. This saves
      a roundtrip to the server by not having to call UNWATCH within
      Pipeline.reset(). Thanks nickgaya, 1299/1302
  * Added the KEEPTTL option for the SET command. Thanks
      laixintao 1304/1280
  * Added the MEMORY STATS command. 1268
  * Lock.extend() now has a new option, `replace_ttl`. When False (the
      default), Lock.extend() adds the `additional_time` to the lock's existing
      TTL. When replace_ttl=True, the lock's existing TTL is replaced with
      the value of `additional_time`.
  * Add testing and support for PyPy.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.4.1
   ```
   * Move the username argument in the Redis and Connection classes to the
      end of the argument list. This helps those poor souls that specify all
      their connection options as non-keyword arguments. 1276
  * Prior to ACL support, redis-py ignored the username component of
      Connection URLs. With ACL support, usernames are no longer ignored and
      are used to authenticate against an ACL rule. Some cloud vendors with
      managed Redis instances (like Heroku) provide connection URLs with a
      username component pre-ACL that is not intended to be used. Sending that
      username to Redis servers < 6.0.0 results in an error. Attempt to detect
      this condition and retry the AUTH command with only the password such
      that authentication continues to work for these users. 1274
  * Removed the __eq__ hooks to Redis and ConnectionPool that were added
      in 3.4.0. This ended up being a bad idea as two separate connection
      pools be considered equal yet manage a completely separate set of
      connections.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.4.0
   ```
   * Allow empty pipelines to be executed if there are WATCHed keys.
      This is a convenient way to test if any of the watched keys changed
      without actually running any other commands. Thanks brianmaissy.
      1233, 1234
  * Removed support for end of life Python 3.4.
  * Added support for all ACL commands in Redis 6. Thanks IAmATeaPot418
      for helping.
  * Pipeline instances now always evaluate to True. Prior to this change,
      pipeline instances relied on __len__ for boolean evaluation which
      meant that pipelines with no commands on the stack would be considered
      False. 994
  * Client instances and Connection pools now support a 'client_name'
      argument. If supplied, all connections created will call CLIENT SETNAME
      as soon as the connection is opened. Thanks to Habbie for supplying
      the basis of this change. 802
  * Added the 'ssl_check_hostname' argument to specify whether SSL
      connections should require the server hostname to match the hostname
      specified in the SSL cert. By default 'ssl_check_hostname' is False

  * Slightly optimized command packing. Thanks Deneby67. 1255
  * Added support for the TYPE argument to SCAN. Thanks netocp. 1220
  * Better thread and fork safety in ConnectionPool and
      BlockingConnectionPool. Added better locking to synchronize critical
      sections rather than relying on CPython-specific implementation details
      relating to atomic operations. Adjusted how the pools identify and

## Summary
- keep cron memory skipped by default, preserving the existing safety invariant
- allow explicit cron memory opt-in (`enabled_toolsets: ["memory"]` or `platform_toolsets.cron`) to initialize MemoryManager-backed provider tools
- add regression coverage for default skip behavior and explicit memory opt-in paths

## Why
Cron jobs pass `skip_memory=True` today, which prevents memory provider tools from being initialized. A cron job can opt into the legacy `memory` toolset but still cannot call provider-backed tools such as `mnemosyne_recall`. This makes memory-aware scheduled jobs fail even when the operator explicitly enabled memory tools.

The change keeps default cron runs isolated from memory providers, but makes explicit memory opt-in meaningful.

author: alii
body:
`bun:sqlite` returned an **empty string** (the whole field) for a non-UTF-8 `TEXT` value shorter than 64 bytes — e.g. `SELECT CAST(x'4A6F73E9' AS TEXT)` (Latin-1 "José") came back as `""` instead of `"Jos�"`. The `SQLITE3_TEXT` fast path for short strings used `WTF::String::fromUTF8`, which returns a **null** string on any invalid UTF-8 byte, and `jsString(null)` becomes `""`. The `>= 64`-byte path already decodes leniently (invalid → U+FFFD), so the two paths disagreed on identical data, with a hard discontinuity at exactly 64 bytes.

Use `WTF::String::fromUTF8ReplacingInvalidSequences` in the short-string branch so invalid bytes become U+FFFD, matching the long path (verified byte-identical across the maximal-subpart replacement classes) and node:sqlite. The fast WTF path is kept for the common valid-ASCII/UTF-8 case.

Adds a regression test sweeping a non-UTF-8 TEXT value across the 63↔64-byte boundary (no discontinuity; node:sqlite parity).

author: aidanallchin
body:
## Summary

This change adds support for GitHub App registration in local and NAT'd deployments that cannot be reached from GitHub's servers. When a deployment is not publicly reachable, the manifest now omits the `hook_attributes` block (which GitHub validates at manifest-creation time), and the callback handler gracefully handles Apps registered without a webhook secret.

## Key Changes

- **New `isPubliclyReachable()` function** — Validates whether a deployment URL is reachable from the public Internet by checking for loopback, unspecified, private (RFC 1918), and link-local addresses. Returns `true` for public DNS names and public IPs, `false` for localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0, ::, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, and link-local ranges.

- **Conditional `hook_attributes` in manifest** — The manifest now only includes the `hook_attributes` block when `isPubliclyReachable(publicURL)` returns `true`. Local/NAT'd deployments omit it entirely, avoiding GitHub's URL validation error.

- **Removed installation lifecycle events from default manifest** — Removed `"installation"` and `"installation_repositories"` from the `default_events` list, as GitHub rejects these in the manifest conversion response. Local deployments will discover installations via API backfill instead.

- **Graceful handling of missing webhook secret** — The callback handler now:
  - Treats `webhook_secret` as optional in the manifest conversion response
  - Only stores the webhook secret in Vault if it is present and non-empty
  - Stores an empty `webhook_secret_ref` in the database for hookless Apps
  - Updated validation to not require `webhook_secret` in the conversion response

## Implementation Details

- The `isPubliclyReachable()` function uses `net/netip.ParseAddr()` to distinguish between DNS names (assumed public) and IP literals (checked against reserved ranges).
- Hookless Apps are identified by an empty `webhook_secret` in the conversion response; the callback handler conditionally adds the webhook secret key to the Vault storage list.
- Three new tests pin the expected behavior:
  - `TestIsPubliclyReachable` — validates the reachability check against loopback, private, and public addresses
  - `TestGitHubAppRegister_LocalManifest_HooklessAndNoInstallationEvents` — verifies the manifest omits `hook_attributes` and installation events for localhost deployments
  - `TestGitHubAppRegister_Callback_HooklessNoWebhookSecret` — confirms the callback succeeds with no webhook secret and stores an empty `webhook_secret_ref`

Fixes SKY-362

author: outofcoffee
body:
Splits the docs workflow into a per-push test job and a main-only deploy job, so docs deployment can no longer be triggered from non-main branches.

## Summary
- `test` job runs on every push and on docs-related PRs. It builds and serves the docs via \`scripts/local-docs.sh\` (now supporting \`DETACH=1\`) and curls a handful of pages (home, gRPC plugin, deployment patterns) to verify the site renders.
- `deploy` job runs only on \`push\` events to \`main\` (gated at the job level), depends on the test job, and runs \`mkdocs gh-deploy --force\` as before.
- \`scripts/local-docs.sh\` gains a \`DETACH=1\` env var to support CI/scripted use; default interactive behaviour is unchanged. Container is named \`imposter-docs\` so callers can clean it up with \`docker rm -f\`.

## Implementation details
The previous workflow guarded only the final \`Deploy to GitHub Pages\` step with \`if: github.ref_name == 'main'\`, but the job itself still ran on \`develop\` pushes and any PR — including running \`mkdocs build\`. Splitting into two jobs makes the boundary unambiguous: a non-main push physically cannot reach the deploy job.

The mermaid-class check now runs against the live served site (\`curl /deployment_patterns/\`) rather than the built static output, which keeps the verification in one place.

## Related issues
Closes #2034

## Summary

This PR fixes a critical API reliability bug where `POST /api/v1/imports` could return `201 Created` even when CSV row generation failed internally.

- Fail API create request when `generate_rows_from_csv` raises.
- Return explicit error response:
  - `error: "import_row_generation_failed"`
  - `message: "Import could not be created"`
- Clean up the partially created CSV import record so clients do not see phantom successful imports.

## Why

Previously, row-generation exceptions were logged but swallowed, and the endpoint continued to return success. That caused silent partial failures for API clients and automation pipelines.

This change makes API behavior truthful and deterministic: if ingestion fails, the request fails.

## Scope of changes

- `app/controllers/api/v1/imports_controller.rb`
  - In `create`, stop swallowing row-generation exceptions.
  - Add `clean_up_failed_csv_import(import)` helper to destroy failed persisted imports.
  - Return `500` JSON error when row generation fails.
- `test/controllers/api/v1/imports_controller_test.rb`
  - Add regression test: returns error and leaves no persisted import when row generation raises.

## Test plan

## Risk and rollout notes

- API behavior change: clients that previously received false `201` on this failure path will now receive explicit `500` errors.
- This is expected and improves data integrity and client correctness.

author: sahilm-ai
body:
## Motivation (retro from t_4ba269e5)

t_4ba269e5 (Ledger Bot missing elapsed timer) burned **$9.26, 22M cache-read tokens, 42 minutes** without shipping. Post-mortem revealed three compounding failures:

- **120/154 tool calls were `execute_code`** wrapping a single `terminal()` command — a 2× cost amplifier
- **Zero `kanban_heartbeat` calls** over 42 minutes — zero observability, no chance to intervene
- **150-iteration budget too low** for investigate+fix+test+PR work

All three are now structurally impossible.

---

## Fix 1: `execute_code` pre-execution gate (`tools/code_execution_tool.py`)

Adds three helpers + gate check at the top of `execute_code()`:

- `_count_hermes_tool_calls(code)` — AST-parses the script and counts hermes tool calls
- `_has_nontrivial_logic(code)` — detects loops, comprehensions, try/except, regex/JSON processing
- `_check_single_tool_call(code)` — returns a guidance message when the gate fires, None otherwise

**Gate rule:** reject scripts that make exactly 1 hermes tool call with no processing logic.

**Gate is intentionally lenient** — passes:
- 0 tool calls (pure Python)
- 2+ tool calls
- 1 tool call + loop/comprehension/try/except/regex/JSON

**29 unit tests** in `tests/tools/test_execute_code_gate.py` covering all acceptance criteria from the task body.

---

## Fix 2: Dispatcher missing-heartbeat enforcement (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`)

Adds `enforce_missing_heartbeat()` — targets workers that have **never** sent a heartbeat (different from `detect_stuck_workers` which fires only after the first heartbeat goes stale):

- **15-min soft warning**: writes a `missing_heartbeat_warning` event on the task. Idempotent (one warning per run).
- **30-min hard block**: calls `block_task()` with a clear protocol-violation reason + SIGTERMs the worker if host-local.

Adds `MISSING_HB_WARN_SECONDS` / `MISSING_HB_BLOCK_SECONDS` constants. Adds `missing_heartbeat_warned` / `missing_heartbeat_blocked` to `DispatchResult`. Wired into `dispatch_once()` in a try/except (never breaks dispatch on enforcer fault).

**6 unit tests** in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_discipline.py`.

---

## Fix 3: Task-scoped `max_iterations` (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`, `tools/kanban_tools.py`)

- `Task` dataclass: new `max_iterations: Optional[int]` field
- DB schema + migration: new `max_iterations INTEGER` column
- `create_task()`: accepts `max_iterations=N` parameter
- `_default_spawn()`: injects `HERMES_MAX_ITERATIONS=N` into worker env when non-NULL
- `kanban_create` tool schema: new `max_iterations` parameter with docstring
- Default unchanged (None = use profile default)

**5 unit tests** covering schema→DB→dispatch\_once E2E.

---

## Fix 4: Skill updates

- **kanban-worker**: new `execute_code anti-pattern` section with good/bad code examples and gate explanation
- **kanban-orchestrator**: new `When to set max_iterations on a card` section with sizing guide table

---

## Test summary



All 248 existing `test_kanban_db.py` tests pass unchanged.

## Summary

Fixes "Failed to create tenant" by eliminating the underscore/hyphen contradiction across the platform and restoring atomic creation semantics with structured errors.

### What changes

- **Single canonical normalizer** (`services/common/tenant_utils.py`): hyphens (K8s-native, MongoDB-safe, Keycloak-compatible), NFD transliteration, idempotent, 3–47 chars, regex `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`. Mirrored byte-for-byte in `services/tenant-user-api/common/tenant_utils.py`.

Drops Mongo + deletes namespace on any partial failure. Every 5xx returns `{error, error_code, request_id}`.

### Motivation
- Provide an end-to-end lightweight Persian NLP toolkit (NetAi) including data collection, corpus analysis, simple language generation, memory-backed chat, and a small MLP training stack for experimentation.
- Enable reproducible workflows for building unlabeled corpora from the web, analyzing learning capacity, and running lightweight training/inference without external APIs.
- Offer a unified CLI and example datasets/seeds to bootstrap experiments and demos.

### Description
- Added a CLI (`src/cli.py`) that wires commands for `collect-text`, `crawl-learn`, `analyze-corpus`, `generate-text`, `train-text`, `eval-text`, `chat`, `learn-chat`, `import-instruct`, `train` and `infer` orchestration.
- Implemented dataset collection and crawling with robots.txt handling, link discovery and concurrent workers in `src/dataset_collect.py`, plus URL encoding and HTML text/link extraction helpers.
- Added corpus utilities in `src/corpus_tools.py` to load CSV texts, compute corpus statistics and estimate generation capacity; and a simple `src/generate.py` tri-/bigram-based sentence generator.
- Implemented a memory-backed chatbot (`src/chatbot.py`) with greeting detection, memory matching, and corpus-based reply stitching, plus an instruct-importer (`src/instruct_import.py`) to convert open instruct datasets into memory JSON.
- Built a minimal ML stack: vectorizer (`src/features.py`), dataset helpers (`src/text_data.py`, `src/data.py`), metrics (`src/metrics.py`), MLP implementation with optimizers (`src/mlp.py`), training/inference scripts (`src/train.py`, `src/infer.py`) and a thin training CLI flow in `src/cli.py`.
- Project scaffolding and examples: Persian README, `requirements.txt`, `.gitignore`, a small sentiment sample CSV, a curated `data/datasets_catalog.md`, and seed URLs in `data/seed_urls.txt`.
- Added a comprehensive unittest suite under `tests/` covering chatbot, crawler, corpus tools, generator, feature vectorizer, MLP save/load, data utilities and training flow, and wired `README` test instruction.

### Testing
- Added a full unit test suite and executed it with `python -m unittest discover -s tests` against the new modules and example data, and the tests passed successfully.
- Tests exercised crawling helpers via mocks (`tests/test_dataset_collect.py`), corpus parsing (`tests/test_corpus_tools.py`), chatbot behavior (`tests/test_chatbot.py`), feature and model save/load (`tests/test_features.py`, `tests/test_model.py`), generation (`tests/test_generate.py`) and training routines (`tests/test_train.py`).

body:
## Resumo

Fase 2 — substitui o motor de geração **muapi.ai** por **Replicate** (chaves próprias, server-side), começando pelo **Image Studio** end-to-end.

- Novo adapter server-side `app/api/replicate/adapter.js`: traduz a requisição do front (formato muapi) em uma *prediction* do Replicate, aguarda concluir (`Prefer: wait` + polling de fallback) e **normaliza a resposta** para o formato que o front já espera (campo `url` + `outputs`).
- Novo route handler `app/api/replicate/[endpoint]/route.js` (POST): recebe a geração reescrita pelo middleware e chama o adapter. Lê `process.env.REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` (Replit Secret) — **nunca exposto ao browser**.
- `middleware.js`: os endpoints de imagem (`flux-schnell-image`, `flux-dev-image`, `sdxl-image`) passam a ser reescritos para `/api/replicate/*` em vez de `https://api.muapi.ai`. O restante segue no proxy muapi (intacto).

### Modelos cobertos nesta entrega (Image Studio / text-to-image)
| UI (id) | endpoint | Replicate |
|---|---|---|
| Flux Schnell | `flux-schnell-image` | `black-forest-labs/flux-schnell` |
| Flux Dev | `flux-dev-image` | `black-forest-labs/flux-dev` |
| Sdxl Image | `sdxl-image` | `stability-ai/sdxl` |

- Flux: `aspect_ratio` passado direto (sanitizado contra o enum aceito; fallback `1:1`).
- SDXL: `aspect_ratio` convertido para `width`/`height` (resoluções recomendadas do SDXL).

### Detalhe importante de integração
O front (`packages/studio/src/muapi.js > submitAndPoll`) inicia polling se a resposta tiver `request_id`/`id`. Como o adapter resolve **sincronamente**, a resposta **omite** esses campos (usa `prediction_id` para debug) e devolve `url`/`outputs` direto — o front consome sem polling, evitando bater no `/api/v1/predictions/...` (que ainda vai pro muapi).

## Fora de escopo (próxima fase)
- **Video / LipSync / Cinema**: seguem no proxy muapi. Mapeamento Replicate levantado e anexado na thread da tarefa.
- A tela de entrada de chave muapi (`StandaloneShell`) continua existindo (usada para balance/upload/demais estúdios). A geração de imagem **não** usa mais essa chave — usa o token Replicate server-side. Remover/ajustar esse gate é follow-up.
- `image-to-image` (upload) do Image Studio ainda usa o upload do muapi; migração de hosting de imagem fica para a fase de i2i.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build:packages && npm run build` compila com sucesso; rota `/api/replicate/[endpoint]` e middleware registrados.
- [x] Smoke test das funções puras do adapter (mapeamento de endpoints, `buildInput` p/ Flux e SDXL, sanitização de aspect_ratio, normalização de output).
- [ ] **Pendente (precisa do ambiente Replit)**: setar `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` nos Secrets e gerar uma imagem real no Image Studio com Flux Schnell/Dev e SDXL.

author: val4evr
body:
## Summary

This PR allows kanban cards to be dragged across columns while sorting is enabled.

Previously, any board drag while a sort was active opened the “Remove sorting?” modal. That makes sense for same-column reordering, because manual reorder conflicts with the active sort. But for cross-column moves, the user is changing the grouped field, not trying to manually reorder the destination column.

With this change:

- Same-column drag with sorting enabled still opens the existing remove-sorting modal.
- Cross-column drag with sorting enabled updates only the group field.
- The destination column keeps using the active sort to determine where the card appears.
- Unsorted board drag behavior continues to update `position` as before.

## Why

On sorted kanban boards, moving a card to another column is a valid workflow even though manual reordering is not. The previous guard blocked both cases because it only checked whether sorting was active, not whether the card stayed inside the same column.

## Implementation

The drop behavior now distinguishes between:

- sorted same-column drops, which remain blocked
- sorted cross-column drops, which are allowed without a position update
- unsorted drops, which keep the existing position-update behavior

A small helper captures that decision and has focused unit coverage.

## Validation

- Manually verified sorted cross-column drag persists after refresh.

author: tsedekey
body:
## Description

- Adds an inline warning banner in the variable filter modal whenever any condition row uses the `contains` operator
- The banner appears reactively (via `FormSpy`) and disappears as soon as all `contains` rows are switched to another operator
- No backend query logic is changed

## Why

Variable values longer than ~8 000 characters are stored **truncated** in Elasticsearch (`variableSizeThreshold = 8 191` chars, configured in `application-elasticsearch.yaml`). The `contains` filter runs a wildcard query against this truncated `varValue` field in `operate-list-view`. If the search term falls past the truncation boundary, the filter silently returns zero results — a false negative with no user-visible signal.

This was verified by injecting synthetic Elasticsearch documents that mirror exactly what `VariableHandler.java` and `ListViewVariableFromVariableHandler.java` write for a long variable, then confirming the wildcard query returns 0 hits for a term past position 8 191.

Closes #51812

author: ttraenkler
body:
## Summary

`Array.prototype.{forEach,map,filter,find,...}` callbacks declaring fewer formals than the spec arity (e.g. `function(v){...}` for forEach which passes value/index/array) saw `arguments.length` lying as the formal-param count instead of the actual 3.

**Root cause**: these methods are compiled **inline** in `compileArrayForEach` & siblings (`src/codegen/array-methods.ts`) — the call never reaches the `__call_fn_<arity>` host dispatcher the issue's framing pointed at. Direct probe with a tracing host import confirmed `__proto_method_call` is never invoked for `[…].forEach(fn)`.

## Fix

Two-layer plumbing of the existing `__argc` + `__extras_argv` globals (already consumed by `emitArgumentsVecBody` from #1053):

1. **Inlined array-callback path (dominant — ~41 fails)** — `buildClosureCallInstrs` now invokes a new helper `emitArrayCallbackArgsPlumbing` that sets `__argc = numFormals` and builds an externref vec containing the missing positional slots (index and/or array) boxed via `__box_number` / `extern.convert_any`. Receive-side code unchanged.

2. **Host-bridge dispatcher (Map.forEach, Array.from mapFn, sort comparator)** — `emitClosureCallExportN` sets `__argc = numFormals` and populates `__extras_argv` with locals beyond `closureArity` so host-invoked callbacks get the same plumbing.

## Test plan

- [x] 6/6 new tests in `tests/issue-820l.test.ts` pass (forEach/map/filter, 0/1/3 formals)
- [x] Equivalence: **101 → 98 fails** (net −3, no regressions in arguments/array buckets)
- [x] Typecheck clean
- [ ] Test262 (CI will validate)

## Out of scope

The general direct-call path (`fn(1,2,3,4)` with `fn` declaring 1 formal) still drops extras — that requires `compileCallExpression` to emit the same plumbing, which is cross-cutting; carved as a follow-up. `Function.prototype.bind` sub-bucket coordinates with #1632a.

author: ksted
body:
## Issue:

One aspect of the application that's difficult to track at the moment is how different elements are distributed across `z-index` layers. Changes in one component may easily affect another and because we use magic number for indexes, this is hard to detect. Additionally, plain number may lead to a steady but unnecessary increase in the number of layers.

## Describe your changes

- Adds `z-index` classes in Tailwind config
- Updates all components to use the defined classes instead of numbers

Furthermore, this change request provides three tools for managing `z-index` layers:

- A custom ESLint rule to detect `z-index` with numbers instead of classes
- A codemod to update `z-index` usage across all components
Run with `node scripts/zindex-codemod/migrate.mjs`
Note that a small number of changes have to be done manually, refer to the migration script for details
- A report script to quickly ascertain which elements use which `z-index`
Run with `npm run report:zindex`, see script annotations for different output formats

<details>
<summary>Original prompt</summary>
Plan: Centralise z-index usage in apps/web

## Context (findings)

- `z-*` Tailwind classes used in 80+ Vue templates in `apps/web/`, totaling ~120 occurrences.
- Tailwind config (`apps/web/app/configuration/tailwind.config.ts`) does NOT extend `theme.zIndex` — so most usages are arbitrary values `z-[N]`.
- Distinct numeric values seen: 0, 1, 2, 5, 9 (note: `z-9` is invalid — typo in `Breadcrumbs.vue` line 4 `z-9`), 10, 15, 20, 40, 50, 51, 100, 150, 200, 201, 202, 300, 500, 600, 700, 999, 1000, 9999, 99999.
- Inconsistent: same role uses different values (loaders use `z-[999]` _and_ `z-[99999]`; tooltips mostly `z-10` but some `z-[9999]`).
- `!important` overrides exist: `!z-50`, `!z-[201]`, `!z-0`, `overlay-classes="z-[1000]"` in modals — symptoms of stacking-context fights.
- Responsive breakpoints mutate z (e.g. `z-[1] md:z-[10] lg:z-[150]` in `SettingsToolbar.vue`, and `z-[0] md:z-[1] lg:z-[40]` in `PageBlock.vue` / `BlockActions.vue`). These exist to keep editor chrome above storefront chrome only on wide screens.
- Inline `style="z-index: 9999"` in `NotifyMe.vue` line 24 bypasses Tailwind entirely.

## Logical layers detected

1. base content / cards / carousel arrows: 0–2
2. sticky storefront chrome (NavbarTop, Header, NavbarBottom, MegaMenu sticky): 10
3. editor inline UI (drag handles, block actions, add-block buttons): 15–40
4. backdrops / drawers / dropdowns: 40–50
5. notifications: 51
6. category sidebar (mobile), search popovers, language list: 100–200
7. AddBlockPopover stack (overlay/panel/arrow): 200/201/202
8. RichText sub-menus / HtmlEditor modal: 200–600
9. PageSearch / MegaMenu mobile sheet: 700–1000
10. Loaders: 999 or 99999 (inconsistent)
11. Color/Emoji pickers, tooltips on Notify settings: 9999
12. Stray maxima: 99999 for full-page loaders

---

## Implementation Plan — Centralised z-index scale via Tailwind theme

User decisions:

- Include `apps/web/modules/paypal/` PayPal files.
- Add ESLint rule discouraging arbitrary `z-[N]`.
- Replace responsive z shifts: see "Responsive shifts" section — recommendation is keep Tailwind responsive prefixes but with named tokens, NOT switch to `useViewport`, because the latter introduces SSR hydration mismatch for purely-CSS concerns. `useViewport` is already available (`nuxt-viewport` is in `package.json` and auto-imported), so it remains a fallback for the few cases where a clean swap is impossible.
- Migration via codemod: `ast-grep` (`@ast-grep/cli`), Vue-SFC aware, single binary, declarative YAML rules.

TL;DR: Define a semantic z-index scale in `tailwind.config.ts` and migrate templates to named classes. Removes magic numbers, makes intent explicit, allows ordering to be changed in one place.

**Scale proposal** (names map to layer roles above):

- `z-base` = 0
- `z-raised` = 1
- `z-overlap` = 2 (badges, breadcrumb chevron, gallery arrows)
- `z-editor-inline` = 30 (BlockActions, drag handles, add-block buttons in canvas)
- `z-sticky` = 40 (headers, NavbarBottom, sticky MegaMenu)
- `z-dropdown` = 50 (account dropdown, language list, MegaMenu panel, tooltips default)
- `z-notifications` = 60
- `z-drawer-backdrop` = 70 (MegaMenu mobile overlay)
- `z-drawer` = 80 (slide-in nav)
- `z-cookiebar` = 90
- `z-editor-toolbar` = 100 (SettingsToolbar lg)
- `z-editor-drawer` = 110
- `z-modal-backdrop` = 200
- `z-modal` = 210
- `z-popover` = 220 (AddBlockPopover panel, RichText menus)
- `z-loader` = 300 (page-blocking spinners)
- `z-picker` = 400 (ColorPicker, IconEmojiPicker — must sit above modals because invoked from inside them)
- `z-toast` = 500
- `z-max` = 9999 (escape hatch, lint-discouraged)

### Phase 1 — ESLint rule first (verify the guardrail works)

1. Add custom rule `apps/web/eslint-rules/enforce-z-index-tokens.js` (follows pattern of existing custom rules in `eslint-rules/`).
   - **Allowlist-based**: the rule knows the set of valid z-index token names from the scale (`z-base`, `z-raised`, `z-overlap`, `z-editor-inline`, `z-sticky`, `z-dropdown`, `z-notifications`, `z-drawer-backdrop`, `z-drawer`, `z-cookiebar`, `z-editor-toolbar`, `z-editor-drawer`, `z-modal-backdrop`, `z-modal`, `z-popover`, `z-loader`, `z-picker`, `z-toast`, `z-max`).
   - Scans string literals in Vue template `class` / `:class` attributes and string-array `:class` bindings.
   - Flags any token that matches `/(?:^|\s)!?(?:[a-z]+:)*z-[^\s]+/` AND whose suffix (after stripping responsive/`!` prefixes) is NOT in the allowlist.
   - This catches BOTH arbitrary `z-[N]` AND plain numeric `z-10`, `z-50`, etc. — the magic-number elimination goal.
   - Severity: `warn`.
   - To keep the allowlist as the single source of truth, export it from a shared file (e.g. `apps/web/eslint-rules/z-index-tokens.js`) so the codemod in Phase 3 can import the same list.
2. Register the rule in `apps/web/eslint.config.mjs` alongside the existing custom-rules plugin entry.
3. Run `npm run lint` once.
   - **Expected outcome on this first run: MANY warnings** — every `z-*` class in `apps/web/app/` and `apps/web/modules/paypal/` that isn't already a named token. With ~120 z usages and zero tokens yet defined, expect ~120 warnings. This is correct and expected — the rule is doing its job. Do NOT try to fix them manually; they are addressed by the codemod in Phase 3.
   - Failure modes that would indicate a problem with the rule itself (and need fixing now):
     - Lint command crashes or throws (rule has a bug).
     - Zero or near-zero warnings reported (selector or allowlist comparison is wrong — fix and re-run before continuing).
     - Warnings reported on classes that are NOT z-related (e.g. `mb-10`, `top-10`) — selector too greedy on suffix.
   - Sanity tests (each one-line edit, then revert):
     - Add `z-[123]` → expect warning.
     - Add `z-10` → expect warning.
     - Add `md:z-10` → expect warning (prefixes stripped before allowlist check).
     - Add `!md:z-10` → expect warning (prefixes stripped before allowlist check).
     - Add `@md:z-10` → expect warning (prefixes stripped before allowlist check).
     - Add `z-dropdown` → expect NO warning.
     - Add `md:z-dropdown`, `@md:z-dropdown` and `!z-dropdown` → expect NO warning (prefixes stripped before allowlist check).
     - Add `mb-10` → expect NO warning (not a z class).

### Phase 2 — define the scale

4. Add `theme.extend.zIndex` map in `app/configuration/tailwind.config.ts` with the tokens listed above.
5. Add a brief comment block above the map describing each token's role.

### Phase 3 — codemod migration via ast-grep

Tool: `@ast-grep/cli` — add as devDependency at the workspace root.

6. Author `sgconfig.yml` + rule files under new directory `scripts/zindex-codemod/` containing one YAML rule per mapping (e.g. `z-[999]` → `z-loader`, `z-[200]` → `z-modal-backdrop`, `z-50` → `z-dro

| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/blueprints/{name}/{version}` | `delete` | `409` if `deploymentCount > 0` |

## PR #58 round-1 independent review — addressed in `b9854c3`

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| `[Important #1]` `internal/api/blueprints.go` `create()` — CRD-required fields not validated handler-side, so a missing `useCase` reaches the apiserver and surfaces as a generic 500 via the catch-all branch (admission validation under `client.fake` doesn't enforce kubebuilder constraints) | `b9854c3` adds explicit handler-side validation: `useCase` required + whitelisted against `validUseCases` (mirrors the CRD enum `rag\|vision\|fine-tuning\|inference\|other`); `source.type` must be `Published` (or omitted, in which case it defaults to `Published` server-side). Also adds `apierrors.IsInvalid → 400` translation so any future schema drift surfaces as a structured client error rather than a 500. |
| `[Important #2]` `internal/api/blueprints.go` `create()` — `ai.suse.com/blueprint-source` label hardcoded to `"published"` while `spec.source.type` is `aifv1.BlueprintSourcePublished`; drift risk if the enum gains values | `b9854c3` derives the label from the validated `req.Source.Type` via `string(req.Source.Type)`. Guarantees label ↔ spec parity. |
| `[Important #3]` `internal/api/blueprints.go` `deprecate()` — un-gated state set lets a `?deprecated=false` request silently re-activate a `Withdrawn` blueprint, bypassing the one-way `Active → Deprecated → Withdrawn` lifecycle | `b9854c3` rejects PATCH against a `Withdrawn` blueprint with `409` + `ErrCodeConflict` and a message explaining the lifecycle constraint. |
| `[Important #5]` `internal/api/blueprints.go` `NewBlueprintsHandler` — silent acceptance of nil `repo` / nil `counter` defers nil-pointer crashes to the first incoming request | `b9854c3` panics at constructor with `"BlueprintsHandler: repo is required"` / `"BlueprintsHandler: counter is required"`. Crash-at-startup is preferable to crash-in-handler. |

**New tests pinning the fixed behavior** (`internal/api/blueprints_test.go`, all in `b9854c3`):

- `TestBlueprintsCreate_MissingUseCase` — POST without `useCase` → 400 + `ErrCodeInvalidInput`
- `TestBlueprintsCreate_InvalidUseCase` — `useCase: "bogus"` → 400 + `ErrCodeInvalidInput`
- `TestBlueprintsCreate_RejectsWrapsVendorChartSource` — `source.type: "WrapsVendorChart"` → 400 (vendor-wrapped Blueprints are operator-minted, not user-POSTed)
- `TestBlueprintsCreate_DerivesSourceLabel` — verifies the `blueprint-source` label matches `spec.source.type` rather than a hardcoded literal
- `TestBlueprintsCreate_DefaultsSourceTypeToPublished` — omitted `source` block defaults both spec and label to `Published`
- `TestBlueprintsDeprecate_RejectsWithdrawn` — PATCH against `Withdrawn` → 409 + `ErrCodeConflict`
- `TestNewBlueprintsHandler_PanicsOnNilRepo` / `_PanicsOnNilCounter` — pins the constructor contract

Two pre-existing tests (`TestBlueprintsCreate_Conflict` and `_SARAllowed`) now include `useCase: "inference"` in their request bodies to clear the new required-field check; otherwise unchanged.

## Integration notes

Three task branches cherry-picked onto `mvp-migration-wave-1` in dependency order. The only shared file across tasks was `cmd/operator/main.go`; both 2-1 and 3-0 touched it but at non-overlapping positions, so git auto-merged cleanly (helm inspector type assertion at line 177, `BlueprintsHandler` constructor at line 278, `manager.Register` varargs at line 286).

l10n discipline: 1-1 owns `aif.pages.apps.*` only; 3-0 / 2-1 are backend-only and write no l10n.

P2-7 (Vendor-Chart Wrapper) is deferred to post-MVP. The `source.type` validation + `blueprint-source` label derivation + `Published`-defaulting added in `b9854c3` are correct defensive mirrors of the current CRD shape; once the CRD shrinks (drop `BlueprintSource` / `BlueprintSourceType` / `WrapsVendorChartRef` from `api/v1alpha1`), they collapse together with the field via a ~10-line follow-up PR. The full cleanup punch list is recorded under `P2-5` in `docs/spec/PROJECT_PLAN.md` (commit `0708985`). This PR completes the Phase 4.5 authenticity baseline by adding detached public-key signatures, mixed-algorithm keyring support, and deterministic burst reliability reporting.

## What changed

- Added detached Ed25519 authenticity support in core:
  - `DetachedEd25519Signature`
  - `sign_detached_payload_ed25519(...)`
  - `verify_detached_payload_ed25519(...)`
  - new core error: `InvalidAuthenticityKeyMaterial`

- Extended CLI authenticity tooling:
  - `auth-sign-ed25519`
  - `auth-verify-ed25519`
  - `decode`/`scan` detached verification now auto-routes:
    - `tag_hex` => MAC detached verify
    - `signature_hex` => Ed25519 detached verify

- Added versioned keyring schema support (CLI + wasm):
  - `{"version":1,"keys":[...]}`
  - mixed algorithms supported per key entry:
    - `alg: "mac-blake3"` + `key_hex`
    - `alg: "ed25519"` + `public_key_hex`
  - legacy array keyring format remains supported for backward compatibility

- Extended wasm auth APIs:
  - `signDetachedEd25519`
  - `verifyDetachedEd25519`
  - retained detached MAC APIs and added keyring parsing parity with CLI

- Burst reliability improvements:

author: shashank-reddy-nr
body:
## Problem

The [test-prerelease-linux / provision](https://github.com/newrelic/infrastructure-agent/actions/runs/26525484833/job/78281080049) job started failing with exit code 2 and no visible error in GitHub Actions logs.

### CouldWatch Logs:

`Error: [0m[0m[1mcreating EC2 Instance: operation error EC2: RunInstances, https response error StatusCode: 400, RequestID: e771XXX-XXX-XXX-XXX-XXX, api error InvalidAMIID.NotFound: The image id '[ami-0b7b425050b12e3f9]' does not exist[0m`

## Root cause

`terraform apply` attempted to launch an EC2 instance using AMI
`ami-0b7b425050b12e3f9` (SLES 15.3 amd64). This AMI was deregistered by
SUSE  confirmed via CloudTrail (no `DeregisterImage` event in our
account, meaning it was removed by the AMI owner, not by our team).

SLES 15.3 reached EOL in January 2023. Newer versions (15.4–15.7) are
already covered in the test matrix.

## Why the error was invisible

`fargate-runner-action` uses `log_filters` to stream only matching lines
from CloudWatch to GitHub Actions output. The existing filters only
allowed success-path patterns (`TASK [...]`, `PLAY [...]`,
`Apply complete!`). Terraform and Ansible error lines were silently
dropped, making diagnosis require direct CloudWatch access.

## Changes

1. **`test/provision/terraform/caos.auto.tfvars.dist`** — remove
   `amd64:sles-15.3` (same approach as the earlier `sles-15.2` removal)

2. **`.github/workflows/component_prerelease_testing.yml`** — add three
   error patterns to all `log_filters` blocks:
   - `ERROR!` — catches Ansible and ansible-galaxy errors
   - `fatal:` — catches Ansible fatal task failures
   - `Error:` — catches Terraform errors (validated against the actual
     CloudWatch log line which contains ANSI escape codes between the
     Terraform box character and `Error:`, making a `│\s+Error` pattern
     unreliable)

author: cstuncsik
body:
## Summary

Relaxes the workflow update guard introduced in IAM-626. Pre-IAM-703, any change to `settings.redactionPolicy` was rejected when `N8N_ENV_FEAT_REDACTION_ENFORCEMENT=true`. Under the progressive restriction model agreed on 2026-05-19, only changes that drop the policy **below the instance floor** are rejected — equal-or-stricter changes succeed.

When a change is rejected, the API returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with:

> Workflow redaction policy cannot be weaker than the instance floor.

The guard covers all three write paths (unchanged from IAM-626):

1. **REST `PATCH /workflows/:workflowId`** (Editor UI, internal API)
2. **Public API `PUT /api/v1/workflows/:id`** (routes through `WorkflowService.update`)
3. **Source-control pull** (workflow import from a remote repo)

`RedactionEnforcementService` now reads the active floor from `InstanceRedactionEnforcementService` (cache-backed, shipped in IAM-425) instead of the bare env flag. `assertPolicyChangeAllowed` is now async; both call sites already lived in async methods, so adding `await` was mechanical.

Pre-existing below-floor state is preserved — an update only fails when the **incoming** policy weakens the redaction below the floor. This honours the project's "no retroactive application" decision.

### Floor → required scope

| Floor | Required redactions | Allowed `redactionPolicy` values |
|---|---|---|
| `off` | none | any (`none`, `manual-only`, `non-manual`, `all`) |
| `production` | production redacted | `non-manual`, `all` |
| `all` | production + manual redacted | `all` |

### Behaviour matrix (replaces IAM-626 matrix)

| Floor | Incoming policy | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `off` | any | Update succeeds |
| `production` | `non-manual` or `all` | Update succeeds |
| `production` | `none` or `manual-only` | **422** |
| `all` | `all` | Update succeeds |
| `all` | anything else | **422** |
| any | omitted from payload | Update succeeds |
| any | unchanged vs stored value | Update succeeds (preserves legacy state) |

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

https://linear.app/n8n/issue/IAM-703

Builds on:
- IAM-626 — the original (now-relaxed) guard
- IAM-425 — `InstanceRedactionEnforcementService` (DB + cache layer)
- IAM-619 — Security & Policies API surface (floor read/write)

Related:
- IAM-701 (in review) — FE companion (per-select lock + floor hints)
- IAM-700 — execution-side mirror (strictest-per-channel resolution)
- IAM-625 — E2E Playwright coverage

## Manual testing steps

Prereqs: a fresh n8n instance with the data-redaction license active and at least one existing workflow. Each scenario assumes `N8N_ENV_FEAT_REDACTION_ENFORCEMENT=true` unless stated otherwise.

### Scenario 1 — Floor `off`: any change succeeds (regression check)

1. Start n8n with the flag on, but leave the floor unset (or set it to `off` via **Settings → Security & Policies → Data redaction**).
2. Pick a workflow whose stored `redactionPolicy` is `none`.
3. Public API:
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"wf","nodes":[],"connections":{},"settings":{"redactionPolicy":"all"}}'
   ```
4. **Expected**: `200 OK`. `GET` confirms `redactionPolicy: "all"`.
5. Repeat downward (`all` → `none`). Also succeeds.

### Scenario 2 — Floor `production`: weaker policy rejected, stricter accepted

1. Set the floor to **Production executions** via the Security & Policies UI (or `POST /rest/settings/security` with `redactionEnforcement.floor = "production"`).
2. Pick a workflow stored as `redactionPolicy: all`.
3. **Reject path** — downgrade to `none`:
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"wf","nodes":[],"connections":{},"settings":{"redactionPolicy":"none"}}'
   ```
   **Expected**: `HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity`, body contains `"Workflow redaction policy cannot be weaker than the instance floor."`. `GET` shows the workflow still has `redactionPolicy: "all"`.
4. **Accept path** — switch to `non-manual` (meets floor) or back to `all`:
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"wf","nodes":[],"connections":{},"settings":{"redactionPolicy":"non-manual"}}'
   ```
   **Expected**: `200 OK`.

### Scenario 3 — Floor `all`: only `all` accepted

1. Set the floor to **Manual and production executions**.
2. Pick a workflow stored as `redactionPolicy: all`.
3. **Reject paths** — try `non-manual` and `none`. Both return **422**.
4. **Accept path** — re-send `all`:
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"wf","nodes":[],"connections":{},"settings":{"redactionPolicy":"all"}}'
   ```
   **Expected**: `200 OK`.

### Scenario 4 — Field omitted from payload → succeeds at any floor

1. With any floor (try `all`), update only the workflow's name:
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"renamed","nodes":[],"connections":{}}'
   ```
2. **Expected**: `200 OK`, name updated, `redactionPolicy` untouched.

### Scenario 5 — Pre-existing below-floor state is preserved

1. With floor `off`, set a workflow's `redactionPolicy` to `none` and save.
2. Raise the floor to `production`.
3. From the editor, save the workflow again **without changing redaction** (e.g. tweak the name).
4. **Expected**: `200 OK`. The legacy `none` value persists — the floor is not retroactively applied.
5. Re-sending the same `none` via API also succeeds (`incomingPolicy === currentPolicy` short-circuit):
   ```bash
   curl -i -X PUT http://localhost:5678/api/v1/workflows/<id> \
     -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"wf","nodes":[],"connections":{},"settings":{"redactionPolicy":"none"}}'
   ```
   **Expected**: `200 OK`.
6. *Now* try to change it to anything still below floor (no-op since it stays `none`) — covered by Scenario 2.

### Scenario 6 — Source-control import: below-floor → rejected

1. Set up two instances against the same git repo. On instance A (floor `off`), set a workflow's `redactionPolicy` to `none` and push.
2. On instance B, set the same workflow locally to `redactionPolicy: all`, raise the floor to `production`, then restart with the flag on.
3. From instance B's UI: **Source Control → Pull**.
4. **Expected**: the pull surfaces a 422 mentioning *"Workflow redaction policy cannot be weaker than the instance floor."*. The local workflow remains `all`.

### Scenario 7 — Source-control import: meets-or-exceeds floor → succeeds

1. Same setup as Scenario 6, but on instance A push `redactionPolicy: all`.
2. Pull on instance B (floor `production`).
3. **Expected**: pull succeeds; other workflow fields (name, nodes) update normally.

## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code.
- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md))
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. (Covered by IAM-623.)
- [x] Tests included. (16 new cases in `redaction-enforcement.service.test.ts` covering the floor × policy matrix and AC scenarios; existing `workflow.service.test.ts` and `source-control-import.service.ee.test.ts` cases updated for the async signature and new error string.)
- [ ] PR Labeled with \`Backport to Beta\`, \`Backport to Stable\`, or \`Backport to v1\` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

author: hclsys
body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** `IndexError: list index out of range` on Vertex/Gemini streaming with `web_search_options` + `reasoning` + `stream=True`. Works without streaming.
- **Cause:** `web_search + reasoning` makes Gemini emit mid-stream chunks carrying only grounding/thought metadata — no content part, no `finishReason`. `_process_candidates` skips content-less candidates, and the existing fallback in `_apply_stream_candidates` only fired when `finishReason` was set, so `choices` stayed empty → the downstream streaming handler does `choices[0]` and raises.
- **What changed:** emit an empty-delta `StreamingChoices` for a content-less candidate regardless of `finishReason`, so a metadata-only chunk still yields `choices[0]`.
- **Scope:** only the content-less-candidate fallback path; final-chunk finishReason handling and content chunks unchanged.

## Tests
`uv sync --group dev` then:
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/test_gemini_streaming_tool_call_finish_reason.py -q
# 6 passed
```
New `test_streaming_metadata_only_chunk_does_not_yield_empty_choices` feeds a grounding-only chunk; it fails on main (IndexError-prone empty choices) and passes with the fix.

Fixes #28884

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis (40th NEW MECHANISM CLASS — Body LR topology: depth-scaled per-layer MuonH LR)

**Test whether the H148+H203 single-LR-across-all-72-body-matrices structure is optimal, or whether depth-scaled per-layer LRs (μP prescription) improve FFS.**

All 94 closed hypotheses apply ONE uniform LR to all body parameters via a single MuonH param group. This is the first hypothesis to break that structure — introducing per-layer LR variation across the model's 12 transformer blocks.

**Mechanism class freshness** (distinct from all 94 closed axes):
- Distinct from MuonH HP/schedule axes (H225 beta1, H226+H219 cosine asymptote, H229+H236 momentum FORM, H222 scheduler off, H224 warmup): those are HP shape, not LR-per-layer topology
- Distinct from H148+H203 baseline tuning history (uniform LR sweep): the body LR has been scalar-tuned but never made non-uniform across depth
- Distinct from H242 thorfinn WSD MuonH schedule (WIP): that varies decay shape over TIME for the uniform LR, not LR magnitudes across LAYERS

This is the **first per-layer body LR experiment** in the campaign.

## Why this might help

μP theory (Tensor Programs V, Yang et al. 2022 arXiv:2203.03466) prescribes that for stable training dynamics across depth, later layers in residual networks need smaller step sizes to keep logit-update magnitudes stable. For sign-normalized updates (matching NS5-Muon at p=0 polar), Everett et al. 2024 (arXiv:2407.05872) show the correct per-layer exponent is closer to **linear** taper than invsqrt.

In our H148+H203 baseline:
- 12 transformer blocks → 72 body weight matrices (6 per block: qkv, proj_o, mlp_in, mlp_out, plus optional)
- All share a single MuonH `lr_init` (currently the H203-tuned scalar)
- Cooldown applies uniformly: `group["lr"] = initial_lr * eta(step)` for all groups, but `initial_lr` is identical

Hypothesis: a depth-scaled `initial_lr` per block — keeping the cosine cooldown shape unchanged — improves convergence-step efficiency by allocating "more aggressive descent" to early layers (which carry more representational change in the early/mid training) and "more conservative descent" to late layers (which accumulate small refinements).

The H203 baseline uniform-LR scalar was tuned. If μP is the correct depth-scaling, the uniform-LR baseline is suboptimally compromised across depth — early layers under-LR'd, late layers over-LR'd.

## Paper references

- Yang et al., "Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer," NeurIPS 2022. arXiv:2203.03466
- Everett et al., "Scaling Exponents Across Parameterizations and Optimizers," ICML 2024. arXiv:2407.05872

If you find recent μP-on-Muon papers (2024-2026) during implementation, incorporate the LR taper exponent they recommend (likely between linear and invsqrt).

## 3-arm design

| Arm | Label | Per-layer LR | Predicted |
|---|---|---|---|
| arm_a | CTRL | `lr_l = lr_init` for all layers (uniform, current baseline) | FFS ~3025, bit-id baseline |
| arm_b | LINEAR_DEPTH | `lr_l = lr_init * (1 - l/24)` for layer l in 0..11. Layer 0 = 1.0×, layer 11 = 0.542×. | WIN target — primary μP test |
| arm_c | INVSQRT_DEPTH | `lr_l = lr_init / sqrt(1 + l/12)` for layer l in 0..11. Layer 0 = 1.0×, layer 11 = 0.722×. | WIN/NULL — milder taper, robustness check |

**Rationale arm_b**: linear taper to 54% by layer 11. More aggressive μP-style depth reduction. Tests whether the H203 uniform LR is over-allocated to late layers.

**Rationale arm_c**: invsqrt taper to 72% by layer 11. Milder taper. Tests whether the depth-scaling effect is monotonic with aggressiveness.

## Asymmetric outcome bracket

- **WIN at either arm**: depth-scaled per-layer LR helps. Strong merge candidate. Follow-up: sweep taper exponent (e.g. 1/depth^p for p ∈ {0.25, 0.75, 1.0}).
- **arm_b > arm_a > arm_c (WIN at arm_b, NEG at arm_c)**: monotonic improvement with more aggressive taper — implies even more aggressive taper might win further.
- **NULL bilateral**: body LR topology is NOT a critical lever — uniform-LR is structurally robust. 95th NULL/NEG closure, 40th mechanism class CLOSED.
- **NEG bilateral**: depth-scaling actively harmful. PROGRAMME FINDING candidate: body LR topology is LOAD-BEARING with uniform-LR being structurally privileged for this stack.

## Implementation sketch (~80 LoC)

**Step 1: argparse parameter (2 lines)**

```python
parser.add_argument("--muonh_lr_taper", type=str,
                    default=os.environ.get("MUONH_LR_TAPER", "none"),
                    choices=["none", "linear", "invsqrt"],
                    help="Per-layer LR taper across 12 transformer blocks. "
                         "none (default, baseline) = uniform LR for all body params. "
                         "linear = lr_l = lr_init * (1 - l/24). "
                         "invsqrt = lr_l = lr_init / sqrt(1 + l/12).")
```

**Step 2: per-layer param group construction**

In `train_gpt_simple.py` body optimizer setup, identify the loop where body parameters are added to MuonH. Currently they're added as a single group:

```python
# BEFORE (single group):
body_params = [p for name, p in model.named_parameters() if name not in aux_names and name not in embed_names]
muonh_optimizer = MuonH([{"params": body_params, "lr": args.muonh_lr_init, ...}])
```

Replace with per-block grouping when `muonh_lr_taper != "none"`:

```python
# AFTER (per-layer groups when taper != none):
if args.muonh_lr_taper == "none":
    # Baseline path — single group, bit-identical
    muonh_optimizer = MuonH([{"params": body_params, "lr": args.muonh_lr_init, ...}])
else:
    # Per-layer groups
    param_groups = []
    for layer_idx, block in enumerate(model.blocks):
        # Compute per-layer LR multiplier
        if args.muonh_lr_taper == "linear":
            lr_mult = 1.0 - layer_idx / 24.0  # layer 0 = 1.0, layer 11 = 0.542
        elif args.muonh_lr_taper == "invsqrt":
            lr_mult = 1.0 / (1.0 + layer_idx / 12.0) ** 0.5  # layer 0 = 1.0, layer 11 = 0.722
        layer_lr = args.muonh_lr_init * lr_mult
        layer_body_params = [p for name, p in block.named_parameters() if (name in body filter conditions)]
        param_groups.append({
            "params": layer_body_params,
            "lr": layer_lr,
            "initial_lr": layer_lr,  # IMPORTANT: cooldown scales from this
            "lr_mult": lr_mult,  # for logging
        })
    muonh_optimizer = MuonH(param_groups, defaults={...})
```

**Step 3: Cooldown propagation check**

The existing `set_hparams(step)` function iterates all param_groups and applies `group["lr"] = group["initial_lr"] * eta(step)`. Verify that:
- Each per-layer group has `initial_lr` correctly stored at construction
- The cooldown `eta(step)` calculation does NOT depend on a single shared `lr_init` — should be a scalar from cooldown shape, applied multiplicatively to each group's `initial_lr`
- If `initial_lr` isn't already stored on the group, add it before the first step

**Step 4: W&B logging**

Currently line ~1193 logs `param_groups[0]["lr"]` — only the first group's LR. With per-layer groups, this logs only layer 0. Add:

```python
# Log mean/min/max LR across all body groups
body_lrs = [g["lr"] for g in muonh_optimizer.param_groups]
wandb.log({
    "train/body_lr_mean": sum(body_lrs) / len(body_lrs),
    "train/body_lr_min": min(body_lrs),
    "train/body_lr_max": max(body_lrs),
    "train/body_lr_layer_0": body_lrs[0],
    "train/body_lr_layer_11": body_lrs[-1] if len(body_lrs) >= 12 else body_lrs[-1],
}, step=step)
```

And W&B config:

```python
"muonh_lr_taper": args.muonh_lr_taper,
"muonh_num_body_groups": len(muonh_optimizer.param_groups),  # 1 for CTRL, 12 for treatment
```

**Total**: ~50-80 LoC including the per-block parameter grouping logic and the W&B logging additions.

## Bit-identity gate (REQUIRED, per H214 retracing discipline)

arm_a CTRL with `--muonh_lr_taper none` MUST reproduce step-0 val=10.82583 EXACT and FFS=3025 EXACT (default=none routes thr

body:
## Summary
- Game Journal is now the default note mechanism for every now-playing entry -- no opt-in required
- Journal is open to all users, not just Regulars
- Existing notes are migrated to public journal entries via a SQL script

## Changes

### SQL migration (`20260528_enable_journal_for_all_convert_notes.sql`)
- Enables journal (`IS_ENABLED=1`) for every existing now-playing entry via MERGE
- Converts non-empty notes to public journal entries for any game that has no existing journal entries

### Member.ts
- `getNowPlaying`: `NVL(jp.IS_ENABLED, 1)` so entries without a pref row are treated as journal-enabled
- `addNowPlaying`: after inserting the now-playing row, merges a journal pref row (`IS_ENABLED=1`) in the same transaction

### now-playing.command.ts
- **Removed**: Journal Opt-In button, `handleNowPlayingEditMenuJournal`, `handleNowPlayingJournalOptInSelect`, `NOW_PLAYING_EDIT_MENU_JOURNAL_PREFIX`, `NOW_PLAYING_JOURNAL_OPTIN_SELECT_PREFIX`
- **Removed**: `canUseJournalFeature`, `hasRegularsRoleForInteraction`, and all their call sites across every journal handler
- **Removed**: `ownerCanUseJournal` parameter from `buildNowPlayingEntryComponents` and all callers
- **Edit menu**: "Edit Notes" and "Journal Opt-In" removed; menu now has Sort, Edit Platform, Add Completion, Remove Game
- **Add flow**: when a note is provided at add time, it is also written as a public journal entry
- **Journal buttons**: now show whenever `journalEnabled` is true and a public entry exists (no role gate)

## Test plan
- [ ] Run SQL migration on desktop
- [ ] `/now-playing list` -- journal buttons appear for all games with public entries
- [ ] Non-Regular user opens another user's journal via the view select or button -- works
- [ ] `/now-playing add` with a note -- note appears as a public journal entry on that game
- [ ] Edit menu (header button) -- no Journal Opt-In button
- [ ] Paging, editing, and deleting journal entries -- all work without role check

body:
## 1줄 비유

"공항에서 호텔 가는 안내가 빈칸이었고 (P269) + Gemini 가 안 만든 도착/예산 필드를 식당이 일반 골격으로만 채웠던 (P271) — 운영자 직접 명령 '문제점 있으면 먼저 고치고 종합보고해' 받아 두 sleeper bug 통합 fix."

## 배경

운영자 challenge "지금 플랜결과물은 어때? 다음 사이클 진행하기 전에 오류 다잡은거맞아?" → 5/28 dispatch 5 plan 결과물 검증 → P270 (호텔 복귀 안 됨) PR #663 머지 후 남은 2 sleeper bug.

## P269: arrival_guide.route_to_hotel 4-fallback chain

### Root cause
- `RouteAgent.js:611` `if (hotelLat && hotelLng && arrivalAirportKey && AIRPORT_COORDS[...])` strict check → hotel_address='' 시 skip
- departure 측 (line 642+) 은 `_resolveHotelOrFallback` 4-fallback chain 적용 (hotel 좌표 → arrival_guide.address → zone anchor → 도시 중심) + `_failed` 마커
- arrival 측만 누락 → 5/5 plan `arrival_guide.route_to_hotel` 미생성

### Fix
- arrival 측 if 분기를 departure 패턴 동일하게 변경 (`_resolveHotelOrFallback` 호출 + `_failed` 마커 fallback)

## P271: block_mode minimal default (2 파일)

### Root cause
- `expandBlocksToItinerary` (line 537) 반환 itinerary 가 `arrival_guide / departure_guide / daily_budget_summary` 3 field 모두 누락
- `handlerCore.js:294` `tryRunBlockMode` 호출 userInput 에 `arrival_airport / departure_airport / pax` 누락
- → backend self_heal 가 generic 5-step placeholder 합성 (5/5 plan)

### Fix
1. `handlerCore.js` — userInput 에 `arrival_airport, departure_airport, pax` 추가
2. `blockMode.js` — `expandBlocksToItinerary` + `expandBlocksToItineraryMultiCity` 둘 다 minimal default:
   - `arrival_guide: { airport: arrivalAirport }` (`already_in_korea` 시 skip)
   - `departure_guide: { airport: departureAirport }`
   - `daily_budget_summary`: per-day skeleton (day/transport_krw/food_krw/activity_krw/total_krw)

## P266 결정 (false alarm — design constraint)

block_mode 는 Gemini main itinerary 안 거침 (block 선택만) → `_cache_metadata` 미수집 = design intent. P195 measurement scope = legacy 1-pass 만 의미. **별도 cycle** (legacy 1-pass dispatch + measurement scope 재정의) spawn 권고.

## 운영자 시점 효과 표

| 지표 (5/5 plan) | 머지 전 | 머지 후 |
|---|---|---|
| `arrival_guide.route_to_hotel` | 누락 | 4-fallback chain (hotel/zone/city) |
| `arrival_guide` minimal | self_heal placeholder | user-aware default |
| `departure_guide` minimal | self_heal placeholder | user-aware default |
| `daily_budget_summary` | self_heal placeholder | per-day skeleton |

## 검증

3 unit test files, **16/16 통과**:
- `tests/unit/arrival-guide-fallback-p269.test.ts` (5)
- `tests/unit/block-mode-minimal-default-p271.test.ts` (6)
- `tests/unit/lodging-bookend-call-chain-p270.test.ts` (5, P270 회귀 차단)

## 의무 체크리스트

- [x] 5-step audit 면제 (위자드 직접 수정 X, post-Gemini default 만)
- [x] deep-search 면제 (P269 = departure 패턴 그대로 적용 / P271 = expand return 추가)
- [x] 비용: Naver Geocoding 추가 호출 가능 (fallback chain) — 무료 quota 내, < \$0.01
- [x] handlerCore 500 line cap 준수 (P271 comment 1 line 압축)
- [x] 한국어 라벨 우선

## 후속 (spawn task 등록)

- **P266 후속**: P195 instrumentation persistence (legacy 1-pass measurement scope 재정의)

### Motivation

- Aplicar internamente, sem efeitos externos, a trajetória temporal escolhida para cada data e enriquecer o artefato final `ResultadoMotorTemporalConjunto` com o estado e auditoria dessa aplicação.
- Fornecer auditoria e regras de fechamento funcional da Etapa 5 para tornar o resultado consumível de forma exclusiva pela Etapa 6. 
- Preservar limites operacionais explícitos (sem pagamento, sem ledger, sem alterações em dados/console/XLSX/saída canônica). 

### Description

author: sindre-maskin[bot]
body:
## Summary

The delete trigger on the object detail header already opens a shadcn `Dialog` confirm, but the body just says "This action cannot be undone" with no mention of *what's about to be deleted*. This PR pipes the title through and adds the two analytics events the bet's First Test needs.

- `apps/web/src/components/objects/object-document.tsx`
  - `DeleteConfirmDialog` accepts `objectTitle: string | null` and renders `This will permanently delete the {type} '{title}'. This can't be undone.` (generic fallback when the object is untitled).
  - `ObjectDocument` (the parent) fires `delete_confirmation_shown` from the trash icon's click handler and `delete_confirmation_cancelled` from the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` when a `confirmedDeleteRef` flag isn't set. The flag is flipped from the wrapper around `onConfirm`, so the navigation-on-success that follows a real delete isn't counted as a cancel.
- `apps/web/src/lib/analytics.ts` — minimal `trackEvent(name, props)` helper that emits `console.info('[analytics]', { ts, name, actorId, ...props })`. Identical to the helper being introduced in PR #485 (`task/instrument-objects-page-events`); if both PRs land, the file conflict is a textual no-op.
- Existing `delete-confirm-dialog.test.tsx` updated to pass `objectTitle` and to assert the new body text (including the untitled-fallback case).

### Why event handlers instead of `useEffect`?

The dialog is fully controlled, so Radix never calls `onOpenChange(true)` on programmatic open — `shown` has to fire from the click that flips the parent's state. Effect-driven firing would also double under `React.StrictMode` because refs reset on each strict-mode remount.

## How to verify

1. `cd apps/web && pnpm vitest run src/__tests__/lib/analytics.test.ts src/__tests__/components/objects/delete-confirm-dialog.test.tsx src/__tests__/components/objects/object-document.test.tsx` — 24 passing.
2. `pnpm lint && pnpm type-check` — both clean.
3. `pnpm dev`, open any object detail page, click the trash icon in the header. Confirm:
   - Dialog body reads `This will permanently delete the {type} '{title}'. This can't be undone.`
   - DevTools console shows `[analytics] { name: 'delete_confirmation_shown', object_type: '<type>', object_id: '<id>', actorId: '<actor>', ts: '<iso>' }` on open.
   - Press ESC / click outside / click Cancel → console shows `[analytics] { name: 'delete_confirmation_cancelled', ... }`.
   - Click Delete → no `delete_confirmation_cancelled` event fires before the page navigates away.

## Scope

Confirm Dialog wiring + analytics only. **No kebab menu, no `MoreHorizontal` trigger, no `⌘ .` listener, no mobile `Sheet`** — those are gated behind the cancel-rate read on the bet's follow-up decision task. This PR targets the bet branch (`bet/aux-action-menu`); the umbrella PR opens once the bet resolves whether to ship the full menu or shrink to copy-actions polish.

Task: [Confirm Dialog on object-detail delete + cancel-rate instrumentation](https://maskin.sindre.ai/fe944fe6-7b45-478c-afc7-b889cea63c08/objects/b8197934-4f70-4c17-952b-822f7f119d09)
Bet: [Auxiliary action menu in top nav per page context](https://maskin.sindre.ai/fe944fe6-7b45-478c-afc7-b889cea63c08/objects/5ad27abf-fbb2-4d86-baf6-0f3879685dd6)
