body:
## Summary

POST_V01 **Item 6 — Expanded credential ruleset (4 → 19 patterns)**.

Adds 15 high-precision, structurally-distinct provider token patterns to
`casket/ruledata/creds.yaml`, taking the regex creds ruleset from 4 to 19
patterns (the entropy rule from Item 3 is unchanged). All new patterns have a
fixed prefix and/or length, so they need no entropy analysis and keep
false-positive rates negligible.

New patterns:

- GitHub PAT (`ghp_`), OAuth (`gho_`), app/Actions (`ghs_`/`ghu_`)
- Slack (`xox[baprs]-`)
- Stripe live secret (`sk_live_`) and restricted (`rk_live_`) keys
- GCP service-account key JSON marker
- SendGrid (`SG.<22>.<43>`)
- npm automation token (`npm_`)
- Docker Hub PAT (`dckr_pat_`)
- JWT (`eyJ….eyJ….<sig>`)
- Heroku API key (UUID, context-guarded by a `heroku…=` prefix)
- Mailchimp (`<hex32>-us<N>`)
- Twilio account SID (`AC<hex32>`) and API key SID (`SK<hex32>`)

No source-code change to the check logic was needed: `creds.run()` already
dispatches `kind: regex` (the default) generically, so this is a pure rule-data
addition plus tests.

## Implementation notes

- **No new dependencies.** Stdlib + existing YAML rule loader only.
- **Severity is per-pattern**: Stripe live secret and GCP service-account key →
  `critical`; Twilio SIDs (lower confidence) → `medium`; the rest → `high`/`medium`.
- **Secret-scanning safety**: the new `multi-secrets-image` test fixture assembles
  its fabricated token strings from inert fragments at build time rather than
  embedding literals, and the secret-bearing fixture tarballs are gitignored
  (conftest regenerates them every session). This keeps token-shaped strings out
  of git history so GitHub push protection passes.

## Tests

New `tests/test_creds_rules.py` (20 tests):
- ruleset well-formedness (every expanded id present, valid severity, has regex)
- each pattern fires against its fabricated example (parametrized)
- all expanded rules fire together on the fixture
- none false-positive on a clean image
- existing AWS regex rules still fire (no regression)
- critical/medium severity mapping verified

author: erans
body:
## What

Follow-up to rc10 (#403). erans's rc10 run **disproved the model that PR was built on**: the `WEDGE` alarm never fired for #2 — even on confirmed hangs — so the lost stop is **never consumed by the Run loop**, i.e. lost *upstream* of `handleStop`. rc10 also **masked** the hang (per-event `slog` added enough latency to suppress the timing race — a Heisenbug).

v2 reworks the diagnostic to (a) instrument the layer *below* `handleStop`, (b) use `/proc` as ground truth, and (c) replace per-event `slog` with a ring buffer so it stops perturbing the race.

## Changes (`internal/ptrace`)

- **Lock-free in-memory ring buffer** (single Run-goroutine writer → no locks, ~struct-copy cost) records every `wait4` **call/return**, every stop dispatched, and every resume/park. Dumped to `slog` **only on an alarm**.
- **`traceWaitCall`/`traceWaitRet`** at both `Wait4` sites: the Run-loop `Wait4(-1)` (`tracer.go`) and `waitForSyscallStop`'s `Wait4(tid)` (`inject.go`). The dump shows whether the kernel reports the stop and **which layer consumes it**.
- **`reconcileProc`**: idle-tick `/proc` reconciliation (throttled to 500ms). Flags any tracee the Run loop believes is running that `/proc` reports kernel-stopped (`State` `t`/`T`) with `TracerPid == us` for >1.5s, then dumps the ring. **Ground truth, independent of where the stop was lost** — fires even though the stop never reached `handleStop`. Reuses existing `procStateChar` + `readProcStatusField`.
- v1 `scanWedged` retained as a secondary signal (also dumps the ring if it ever fires).
- `TraceeState` gains `procStuckSince`/`procWedgeLogged` (written only when enabled).

## Verification

- `go test -race ./internal/ptrace/` ✅ (decode table, disabled-is-silent-and-inert incl. ring untouched, ring append+dump, `readProcStopState` self/missing, v1 scan, v2 running-tracee-not-flagged, v2 throttle), `go build ./...` ✅, `GOOS=windows go build ./...` ✅, `go vet` ✅.
- **End-to-end (erans):** with `AGENTSH_PTRACE_TRACE=1`, reproduce the FUSE-on hang **trace-off-reproduces-style** (the ring is low-overhead, unlike rc10's slog). On the `/proc` alarm the ring dumps the wait/stop/resume history → shows whether `Wait4(-1)` ever saw the stop or `waitForSyscallStop` ate it.

Still a **diagnostic**, not the #2 fix. Refined hypothesis to test: the stop is consumed by `waitForSyscallStop`'s `Wait4(tid)` during a FUSE-lengthened injection and never reaches the Run loop.

Refs #369.

author: lbibollet16
body:
## Le bug observé

Tu as cliqué un bouton sur \`/amazon-sp-api\` et tu as récupéré :
\`\`\`
{
  \"ok\": false,
  \"error\": \"POST /reports/2021-06-30/reports -> 429\"
}
\`\`\`

Aucune indication sur combien de temps attendre. Amazon throttle ce endpoint à \`0.0167 req/sec\` (= 1 jeton par minute, burst 15). Le client a déjà 3 retries avec backoff capped à 10s — mais dès que le burst est consommé, ces 30s d'attente cumulées ne refillent pas le bucket assez.

## Le fix

### 1. \`lib/sp-api/client.ts\`

- \`SPAPIError\` gagne \`retryAfterSeconds\` + getter \`isRateLimited\`
- Quand les retries sont épuisés sur un 429, on calcule le wait depuis le header \`x-amzn-ratelimit-limit\` (réciproque = secondes par jeton), round up + 5s de jitter, fallback à 60s si header absent
- Nouveau helper \`spApiErrorResponse(err)\` retourne \`{ body, status }\` structuré : \`{ ok: false, rate_limited: true, retry_after_seconds, retry_at, error: '...message friendly...' }\`

### 2. Les 4 routes SP-API

\`ledger-sync\`, \`ledger-debug\`, \`settlements-sync\`, \`sync-all\` (POST + GET) → catch passe par \`spApiErrorResponse\`. Plus jamais de \`error: 'POST /... -> 429'\` brut.

### 3. \`/amazon-sp-api/page.tsx\`

- Nouveau state \`rateLimitedUntil\`
- Nouveau composant \`<RateLimitBanner>\` qui tick chaque seconde, affiche le compte à rebours en gros monospace + l'heure de déblocage
- \`run()\` détecte \`body.rate_limited\` → set le banner → bloque les clics
- Idem pour la boucle \`runBackfillChunked\` : si un chunk hit 429, on stoppe les chunks suivants et on lève le banner
- Le banner masque la bannière rouge d'erreur générique tant qu'il est actif (pas double affichage)
- Auto-clear à l'expiration

## Aperçu UI

\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⏳ Amazon SP-API t'a rate-limité                │
│                                                  │
│ Le bucket Amazon se remplit à 1 jeton par       │
│ minute sur ce endpoint. Aucun bouton ne va      │
│ déclencher d'appel tant que le compteur         │
│ ci-dessous n'est pas écoulé — réessayer         │
│ maintenant remet le compteur à zéro.            │
│                                                  │
│    1 min 47s  (déblocage vers 17:42:13)         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

## Pas dans cette PR

- Cooldown par bouton stocké en localStorage entre sessions (l'utilisateur a explicitement décliné)
- Server-side cooldown qui empêche carrément l'appel Amazon si on sait qu'on est rate-limited (plus complexe, on peut faire en suivi)

## Notes

- 1 commit, rien d'autre à pousser après — la branche est gelée.
- TypeScript clean. ESLint pas configuré sur ce projet (juste TS).
- Aucun changement de comportement métier — pur UX.

## Summary
- include OpenAI/Codex `usage_limit_reached` reset details in user-facing API error summaries
- format `resets_in_seconds` as both raw seconds and `reset_hhmm=HH:MM`
- treat `usage_limit_reached` as terminal/actionable instead of retrying three times, since the provider already reports the reset window

## Why
OpenAI/Codex returns useful structured 429 payloads like:

```text
{"error":{"type":"usage_limit_reached","message":"The usage limit has been reached","plan_type":"plus","resets_at":1779987634,"resets_in_seconds":8464}}
```

Before this patch, Hermes collapsed that into:

```text
API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached
```

That hides the actual recovery time and burns extra calls before telling the user anything useful.

body:
## Jira
[RHINENG-26680](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHINENG-26680)

## What
Add new sortable fields for host apps on the `/beta/hosts-view` endpoint, bring the Swagger spec into full alignment with all runtime-sortable fields, and introduce a `policies_count` generated column for efficient compliance policy sorting.

## Why
Several host app fields were either not sortable or sortable at runtime but missing from the OpenAPI spec, preventing consumers from discovering and using them via the API documentation. The compliance `policies` field (JSONB) needed a dedicated integer column to enable meaningful and performant sorting by policy count.

## How
- **Model changes** (`app/models/host_app_data.py`): Added `last_status` (Malware) and `template_name` (Patch) to `__sortable_fields__`. For Compliance, added a PostgreSQL stored generated column `policies_count` (computed from `jsonb_array_length`) instead of sorting by the raw JSONB `policies` column.
- **Migration** (`migrations/versions/b3e9f1a2d7c4`): Adds the `policies_count` generated column to `hosts_app_data_compliance`. Existing rows are backfilled automatically by PostgreSQL during the ALTER TABLE.
- **Swagger spec sync** (`swagger/api.spec.yaml`, `swagger/openapi.json`): Updated both `hostViewOrderByParam` and `AppSortableFields` enums to include all 30 runtime-sortable fields. Added `policies_count` to the `ComplianceAppData` response schema. Previously missing fields:
  - Advisor: `critical`, `important`, `moderate`, `low`
  - Vulnerability: `high_severity_cves`, `cves_with_security_rules`, `cves_with_known_exploits`
  - Patch: 9 advisory/package count fields + `template_name`
  - Malware: `total_matches`, `last_status`
  - Compliance: `policies_count`
- No changes to the query or ingestion layers — sorting is picked up automatically via the `__sortable_fields__` dynamic field map, and the generated column is maintained by PostgreSQL on every write.

## Testing
- 31 unit tests in `test_filtering_app_data_sorting.py` (7 new `resolve_app_sort` tests + 3 updated exact-set assertions)
- 24 integration tests in `test_api_host_views.py::TestHostViewAppDataSorting` (7 new sort tests covering each new field, including `policies_count` with order assertion)
- All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, swagger-validation, redoc)

## PR Guidelines

You can find the documentation of the guidelines [here](https://redhat.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RHIN/pages/384311342/HBI+PR+Guideline)

author: lattln
body:
## Overview

This PR addresses several miscellaneous UI and UX issues across the builder canvas and field components. It improves interaction clarity for matrix, ranking, boolean, dropdown, and long-text fields, while also fixing layout overflow in the builder field header.

Closes #45
Closes #44
Closes #42

## What Changed

* Fixed long field IDs overflowing the builder canvas header by allowing the ID chip text to truncate cleanly.
* Improved matrix field interactions by making the full radio/checkbox cell clickable across desktop and mobile layouts.
* Removed nested label usage in matrix fields to avoid invalid interactive markup.
* Fixed ranking drag behavior so the Sortable instance is not recreated on every ranking state update.
* Added clearer ranking drag feedback with an active border, elevated shadow, and suppressed hover styles while dragging.
* Adjusted boolean Yes/No hover styling so unselected options no longer look selected.
* Added a “— None —” option to dropdown fields when a value is selected, allowing users to clear the selection.
* Made long-text fields vertically resizable while capping max height to prevent layout overflow.
* Added a reusable `XIcon` for clear/close actions.

## How to Test

1. Open the builder and create or load a field with a long ID.
2. Verify the field header ID truncates instead of overflowing the canvas.
3. Add single-select and multi-select matrix fields.
4. Verify clicking anywhere inside an enabled matrix cell toggles the correct radio or checkbox.
5. Verify disabled matrix cells show disabled cursor behavior and do not toggle.
6. Add a ranking field and reorder items multiple times.
7. Verify ranking drag state remains stable and does not duplicate items or leave stale drag highlights.
8. Add a boolean field and hover over unselected Yes/No buttons.
9. Verify hover styling remains subtle and does not look like the selected state.
10. Add a dropdown field, select a value, then choose “— None —”.
11. Verify the dropdown value clears correctly.
12. Add a long-text field and resize it vertically.
13. Verify the textarea can resize but does not expand beyond the max height.

## Breaking Changes

No breaking changes.

author: nicobrinkkemper
body:
## Summary

The README's "Third-party \`\"use client\"\` packages" section claimed you can `import { Heading } from "@chakra-ui/react"` **directly inside a server component, no wrapper needed**. That's false for client-only libraries.

Chakra UI v2 is client-only by design — its [own Next.js App Router guide](https://v2.chakra-ui.com/getting-started/nextjs-app-guide) states *"Chakra UI only works in client-side components"* and requires wrapping `ChakraProvider` in a `'use client'` component. So a server component importing Chakra throwing under the `react-server` condition is **expected RSC behavior in any framework**, not a vprs defect.

Reworded to:
- Client-only component libraries must be used within a `"use client"` boundary (matching their own RSC guidance, with a link to Chakra's guide).
- Kept the accurate description of vprs's `react`-in-peerDeps client-package auto-detection (`vitefu.crawlFrameworkPkgs`) + the `clientPackages` / `excludeClientPackages` escape hatches.

Docs-only; no code change.

## Background

Downstream (mission-control) had filed this as a P1 vprs bug ("use-client not honored, Chakra throws"). On inspection it's a docs over-claim, not a functional bug — the standard client-boundary wrapper is the correct, expected pattern everywhere. That issue is being closed as not-a-bug.

### What changed? Why was the change needed? ## What changed This PR moves the dashboard from a Clerk "satellite" handshake model to cookie-based auth for Connect by documenting and aligning code to a primary same-registrable-domain host model. Comments, environment guidance, and some auth utilities were removed or refactored so Connect and the primary product share Clerk session cookies (eTLD+1), avoiding SDK handshake/return-URL mechanics and reducing cross-origin redirect complexity. ## Affected areas **dashboard**: Comments, env docs, and auth-related logic were updated to reflect the primary same-root-domain model; Netlify caching guidance was clarified to avoid stale auth pages. **dashboard (enterprise)**: EEAuthProvider was refactored to drop satellite variables, compute `isCrossProductHost`, and route sign-in/sign-up to primary auth URLs when appropriate. **dashboard/hooks & components**: Inline docs updated in cross-app navigation, CrossAppLink, HostnameGuard, SignIn/SignUp pages, settings, and other auth-adjacent components; removed satellite-specific return-URL utilities from product-auth-urls.ts. **config / env**: `.example.env` guidance adjusted to require shared eTLD+1 for cookie visibility and to instruct adding Connect hosts to Clerk allowed subdomains. ## Key technical decisions - Rely on shared registrable-domain (eTLD+1) Clerk session cookies for cross-product auth instead of a satellite SDK handshake or CNAME-based satellite mapping. - Remove satellite return-URL utilities and simplify auth routing by using `isCrossProductHost` in EEAuthProvider to choose primary auth routes. ## Testing No automated tests were added; changes are primarily comments, env guidance, and small auth-routing refactors with no API/schema changes. author: zzstoatzz
body:
Part of #15008 — chipping away at the remaining `@sync_compatible` usages, which now live only in the integrations.

This PR converts the 11 `@sync_compatible` methods on `AzureBlobStorageContainer` to explicit async (`a`-prefixed) implementations dispatched via `@async_dispatch`, the same pattern already used by the other async-native integrations (`prefect-kubernetes`, `prefect-shell`).

<details>
<summary>details</summary>

- Each method now has a real async implementation (`adownload_folder_to_path`, `aread_path`, `awrite_path`, …) plus a `@async_dispatch`-decorated sync wrapper that keeps the original public name and docstring.
- Internal cross-calls between methods now call the explicit `a`-prefixed versions directly (e.g. `aput_directory` → `awrite_path`).
- The sync wrappers drive the coroutine on the global loop thread via `from_sync.call_soon_in_loop_thread(create_call(...))`, and still expose `.aio` for backwards compatibility.
- Bogus `-> Coroutine[Any, Any, T]` return annotations (an artifact of `@sync_compatible` typing) are replaced with the real return types.
- Azure's blob SDK is async-native (`azure.storage.blob.aio`) and the credentials block only exposes async clients, so — unlike `prefect-gcp`/`redis`, whose SDKs ship sync clients — the sync path still bridges the event loop rather than running a native-sync implementation. This mirrors `prefect-kubernetes`/`prefect-shell`.
- Adds `tests/test_blob_storage_async_dispatch.py` with regression coverage that sync-context calls return values, not coroutines (the failure mode behind #14712 / #14625).

</details>

author: jimwallace
body:
## Summary

The MCP connector OAuth flow failed with a CSRF 403 on **Authorize** in Safari (and any browser that blocks cross-site cookies). The consent submit (`POST /oauth/authorize`) runs in the connector's cross-site context, where Safari/ITP drops the session cookie — taking both the session-bound CSRF token *and* the authenticated user with it, so the CSRF middleware rejected the request before the handler ran. `SameSite=None` (PR #776) can't fix this, because Safari gates cross-site cookies independently of `SameSite`.

This makes the consent submit **cookie-independent**:

- New `MCPConsentRequest` model + migration: a single-use, ~10-min, server-stored record minted at `GET /oauth/authorize`. It freezes the OAuth params **and the consenting user's identity** (captured from the cookie that *is* present on the top-level GET). Only the SHA-256 hash of the token is stored.
- The consent form now submits just a `request_token`. `POST /oauth/authorize` looks the record up by hash, burns it (single-use), re-validates client/redirect, **re-checks the bound user's role**, and mints the auth code — no session cookie needed on the POST.
- CSRF protection comes from the token: high-entropy, single-use, short-lived, and delivered only into the same-origin consent page (so a cross-origin attacker can't read it). The POST moves off the CSRF middleware into the rate-limited group; the `GET` keeps session auth.
- Reaper sweeps expired consent requests alongside auth codes/grants.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` clean; `swift-format` + SwiftLint (`--strict`) 0 violations
- [x] Full MCP suite (118 tests) + auth/session suites (72 tests) pass
- [x] New coverage: cookieless POST succeeds (the Safari case), unknown/expired/consumed token rejected, role-downgrade-between-GET-and-POST rejected, deny path
- [ ] **Manual:** run the real connector in Safari and confirm Authorize completes (validates the assumption that the GET still carries the session cookie to identify the user)

author: zhepang
body:
## Summary
- Adds a tiny `packages/daemon/src/logger.ts` wrapper (`log` / `warn` / `error`) that prepends `new Date().toISOString()` to the existing `console.{log,warn,error}` args.
- Replaces all 55 `console.*` call sites under `packages/daemon/src/` (excluding `*.test.ts`) with the wrapper. Touched: `main.ts`, `claimer.ts`, `spawner.ts`, `start.ts`, `repo-runs.ts`, `update.ts`.
- Existing `[daemon]` / `[daemon/spawn]` / `[daemon/claim]` / `[daemon/repo-run]` prefixes stay in the args; the wrapper just prepends the timestamp.

## Why
Tail/grep across long-running daemon sessions is painful when every line is timestamp-free. ISO 8601 prefixes make `tail -f /tmp/beevibe-daemon.log | grep sess=abc` line up with claimer / spawner / done events in real time.

## Scope notes
- Daemon ONLY. The same gap exists in `packages/api/` and `packages/scheduler/` — explicitly out of scope here per the task spec (user opted out of a wider sweep).
- Test files left alone on purpose: vitest captures stdout/stderr and the existing tests assert on un-timestamped lines, so wrapping them would require test changes for no real benefit.
- No log-level, env-var gating, JSON output, or other features — pure timestamp prefix, 11 LOC of wrapper.
- `warn` / `error` keep going to stderr (the wrapper calls `console.warn` / `console.error` under the hood).

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @beevibe/daemon build` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @beevibe/daemon test` — 20 passed / 2 skipped (existing suites: claimer, spawner, supervisor, config; e2e skipped as usual).
- [x] `rg "console\.(log|warn|error)" packages/daemon/src --type ts -g '!*.test.ts'` returns zero matches (the wrapper itself is the only producer).
- [ ] CI green on the PR (DCO + lint + workspace build/test).

Sample line shape after this change:
```
2026-05-28T17:59:24.203Z [daemon/spawn] sess=sess_123 agent=agent_123 runtime=opencode type=task cwd=/tmp/ws-opencode
```

author: koichimurakami
body:
## Summary

The `Run Unit Tests` step hangs for ~20 minutes and is cancelled on every PR (all 3 node matrix versions). Build/TypeCheck/Audit/Trivy pass; only the test step hangs, and GitHub Actions captures **no test output** from the cancelled step (its buffer is never flushed), so the failing suite was invisible.

Root cause: several test suites mock `process.stdout.write` — either directly via `jest.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write')` or indirectly by routing the SUT's real write callback (`makeLinePrefixer(prefix, s => process.stdout.write(s))`) straight to it. Jest's own default reporter writes test results over `process.stdout`. When a test replaces / occupies `process.stdout.write` (and in the docker suites also pushes multiple MB through it), the Jest worker's reporter output is blocked and the worker fails to exit — a D-state hang on the hosted Linux runner that the step timeout and the 5-minute killer cannot recover (kill -9 does not free a process blocked in an uninterruptible write). This matches a previously documented project finding that spying on `process.stdout.write` hangs Jest.

PR #341 attempted to fix this by *adding* `process.stdout.write` spies to the docker suites — which is the very pattern that triggers the hang — so it did not help. This PR removes that whole class of mocks.

## Changes
- `docker-supervisor` / `project-image-builder` / `docker-runner` specs: mock the logger's `makeLinePrefixer` to capture writes into an in-memory array instead of forwarding to `process.stdout.write`. This removes all `jest.spyOn(process.stdout/stderr, 'write')` calls and stops the multi-MB real-stdout writes. Re-enables the two `logTruncated` branch tests that were previously `xdescribe`-skipped only because of the spy.
- `log-rotate-command`: make the tee target injectable (`TeeSink`, defaults to `process.stdout`) so the spec asserts tee behaviour against a fake sink instead of spying on `process.stdout.write`.

- [x] Full suite green locally: 129 suites / 3549 tests; coverage S98.92 / B94.77 / F97.29 / L99.22 (above S95/B90/F95/L95)
- [x] Also green under `--runInBand` (mimics CI's single-worker mode)

body:
## Summary

- **Forced password-change flow.** Users flagged `mustChangePassword: true` (e.g. after an admin reset or first login) are routed through a dedicated `/auth/change-password` page before any protected route. New protected `POST /api/auth/change-password` verifies the current password, writes the new one + clears the flag, and revokes the user's *other* sessions — all in a single transaction (the caller's current session survives). `GET /api/auth/me` now returns `mustChangePassword`, so the forced-change state survives a page reload (the short-lived access token can't carry it).
- **Login timing-safety hardening.** The email-enumeration dummy bcrypt hash is now a real, memoized hash derived from the password module instead of a malformed literal that could let bcryptjs short-circuit. Backed by new backfill integration tests (login enumeration-parity, dual-auth token-cleanup endpoint).
- **Frontend.** `AuthStore.changePassword` + `AuthApi.changePassword`, the change-password page (signal-forms + `FormField`, min-12, surfaces `OLD_PASSWORD_MISMATCH`), a `forcedPasswordChangeGuard` (redirects must-change users; route ordered before the `noAuthGuard` group to avoid a redirect loop), and en/es i18n.

## Stacked on #423

This PR is **stacked on #423** (#420 — `AuthService` decomposition) and targets the `420-decompose-auth-service-into-focused-services` branch, so the diff shows only the #388 changes. Merge after #423; GitHub auto-retargets this PR to `main` once #423 merges (or it can be rebased onto `main`).

author: ogyrec-o
body:
## Summary

Implements frevenengine/freven-vanilla#94 using the client lifecycle state boundary from frevenengine/freven-sdk#123 / frevenengine/freven-engine#405.

Vanilla block interaction now registers a runtime-owned `BlockInteractionClientState` instead of stateless client tick hooks.

This state owns a tiny bounded pending-place buffer:

- isolated RMB/place is held for one client tick as a cancelable intent;
- if the next tick contains an exact LMB/break of that same predicted-only placed block, Vanilla coalesces the pair to a local no-op before `submit_action`;
- if no inverse arrives within the bounded window, the place flushes normally;
- same-tick place->break coalescing from frevenengine/freven-vanilla#93 remains intact.

## Why

After frevenengine/freven-engine#400 was fixed as a server-authority rollback/reject class, the remaining bad UX was near-frame rapid RMB -> LMB:

- tick N submits place;
- tick N+1 submits break;
- both commit successfully;
- user sees a bad place-then-break presentation/flicker.

That is not a server validation problem. It is a client intent aggregation problem.

This PR fixes it without process-global state by using the runtime-owned client lifecycle handler added for frevenengine/freven-sdk#123.

## Boundaries

- Vanilla client-side intent buffering only.
- Runtime-owned client lifecycle state, no `static` / process-global client state.
- No server authority weakening.
- No client prediction as authority.
- No validator strictness weakening.
- No protocol changes.
- No broad magic delay for all block interaction.
- No hiding true server rejects.
- Break->place remains a real ordered mutation chain.
- Double-place remains submitted.
- Real rapid break/place chains remain submitted.
- Only exact place->break cancellation of the same pending/predicted-only placed block collapses to no-op.

## Validation

- `cargo +stable test --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials isolated_place_intent_flushes_after_bounded_cancel_window -- --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials near_frame_place_then_break_predicted_only_block_coalesces_to_noop -- --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials same_tick_place_then_break_predicted_only_block_coalesces_to_noop -- --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials same_tick_left_then_right_is_not_net_neutral_place_break_coalesce -- --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials ordered_same_tick_double_right_submits_two_place_actions -- --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable check --locked -p freven_vanilla_essentials`
- `cargo +stable fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo +stable test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo +stable clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git --no-pager diff --check`

## Manual validation required after Boot bump

After merge and Boot bump, rerun focused rapid RMB -> LMB smoke on `freven.vanilla.visual_validation`.

Expected:

- near-frame RMB -> LMB exact pending-place cancel no longer submits two server actions;
- no valid rapid break/place rollback;
- no unexpected `PolicyDenied`, `Occluded`, `FaceMismatch`, `HitMismatch`, or `ActionResult ok=false`;
- no normal local/inproc `LocalPredictionBacklog`;
- real/non-neutral rapid break/place interactions still work.

body:
## Summary
Makes the app safe for multiple users on different computers to track their own sales data without leaking it to each other. Three pillars: an email-domain allowlist, server-side authentication + rate limiting on every API route, and per-user data isolation across Firestore, IndexedDB, and browser storage.

### Access control
- New `src/config/accessControl.js` with an env-configurable email-domain allowlist (fails closed to admin-only when unset).
- Registration and all sign-in paths (Google, email/password) enforce the allowlist; an `onAuthStateChanged` backstop signs out unauthorized/stale sessions before data loads.
- `firestore.rules` gates every collection by ownership/admin/allowed-domain.

### Server auth + rate limiting
- New `api/_lib/`: `firebaseAdmin.js` (ID-token verification), `http.js` (`withAuth` wrapper — CORS locked to `APP_ORIGIN`, Bearer-token verification + allowlist), `rateLimit.js` (Firestore fixed-window), `tokens.js` (per-user OAuth token store for future use).
- All AI endpoints plus HubSpot/Sheets/email/Outlook routes now require a verified user; shared-key routes are rate-limited per user.
- New `src/utils/apiFetch.js` attaches the caller's ID token; 15 frontend files migrated to it.

### Per-user data isolation
- `secureStorage.js`, `utilityRatesStore.js`, and `portfolioSourceFileStore.js` scope keys by uid, with one-time migration of legacy un-scoped records.

### Config
- New `.env.example` documenting all client and server variables.

## Deployment checklist
- [ ] Edit `allowedDomains()` placeholder in `firestore.rules` and deploy rules
- [ ] Set `VITE_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS` + `ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS` (must match each other and the rules)
- [ ] Set `APP_ORIGIN` and `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` in Vercel
- [ ] Carry over existing Firebase/HubSpot/Apollo/Anthropic/Outlook/Google/Resend keys

## Notes / follow-ups
- HubSpot and Google Sheets still use a single shared credential (now auth-gated + rate-limited). True per-user OAuth requires registering OAuth apps in the HubSpot/Google consoles.
- `calendar-webhook.js` uses `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` while new helpers use `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` — set both (can be the same value).
- ~86 UI-preference localStorage keys remain unscoped (no PII, view prefs only).

## Test plan
- [ ] Sign in with an allowlisted email — succeeds
- [ ] Sign in / register with a non-allowlisted email — rejected and signed out
- [ ] API calls from the app succeed; unauthenticated/cross-origin calls are rejected
- [ ] Two accounts on the same browser cannot see each other's stored files/rates/tokens
- [ ] Rate-limited endpoints return 429 after the configured threshold

## Summary Recurrence guard for the `sanjay3290/jules-pr-reviewer@v1` case that stuck PR #13916 on a `jules/review` blocking status. The next abandoned third-party action gets caught before it damages a PR — directly answers "what do we need to add to revvel-standards so it doesn't happen again?" ## What changed ### `scripts/audit-third-party-actions.sh` Greps every `uses: /@` from `.github/workflows/`, dedupes to `owner/repo`, classifies by publisher tier (trusted / multi-author / single-author), queries `gh api repos/.../releases/latest` for each, and flags any **single-author action with no release in 12+ months**. Exits 1 on flagged actions so CI fails visibly. ### `.github/workflows/third-party-action-audit.yml` Quarterly cron (1st of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct at 09:00 UTC) plus `workflow_dispatch`. On flagged actions, opens (or comments on existing) `[WR]` tracking issue with labels `work-request, third-party-action-audit, needs-triage`, then fails the run so the regression is visible in the Actions tab. ### `docs/THIRD_PARTY_ACTION_AUDIT.md` The standard: - **Publisher tiers** — trusted (`actions/*`, `github/*`, `docker/*`, etc.), multi-author (`cypress-io/*`, `dopplerhq/*`, `BeksOmega/*`, etc.), single-author (everything else) - **Staleness threshold** — 12 months, configurable per run - **Disposition table** — for each flagged action: pin to commit SHA / replace / silence the auto-trigger (per the comment-don't-delete convention) / accept the risk and move tiers - **Originating case** — the `sanjay3290` failure that motivated this - **Provenance** — every flag and disposition traces back to the script + run ## Sample local run (no `gh` auth) ``` warn single-author sanjay3290/jules-pr-reviewer single-author, no release found warn single-author binowork/match-labels single-author, no release found ok trusted actions/checkout ok multi-author BeksOmega/jules-action ... Scanned 42 unique third-party actions. ``` In CI with `GH_TOKEN: github.token` the script gets real release ages and only stale single-author actions get the `flag` status (which exits 1 and files the WR). ## Cross-refs - `docs/PROVENANCE_STANDARD.md` (name publisher + package) - `docs/AGENT_MONITORING_STANDARD.md` (the supervision loop) - PR #13974 (the specific `sanjay3290` silencing that motivated this) - PR #13916 (the affected PR) ## Test plan - [x] Script runs locally, syntax-checks, lists all 42 third-party actions in the repo - [x] Workflow YAML parses - [ ] First quarterly run on 2026-07-01 (or trigger via `gh workflow run third-party-action-audit.yml` for an on-demand verification) https://claude.ai/code/session_01GnDB4t4i3hnTDgPSfnHxEs --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01GnDB4t4i3hnTDgPSfnHxEs)_ ## High-level PR Summary This PR adds a **recurrence prevention system** for abandoned third-party GitHub Actions after `sanjay3290/jules-pr-reviewer@v1` (a single-author action) blocked PR #13916 indefinitely. The implementation includes a quarterly automated audit that scans all workflow files, classifies actions by publisher trustworthiness (trusted/multi-author/single-author), checks release freshness via GitHub API, and **automatically files a tracking work request** when single-author actions haven't released in 12+ months. author: alii
body:
The multipart `FormData` parser never reversed the WHATWG `%22`/`%0D`/`%0A` escaping that goes into `Content-Disposition` `name=`/`filename=` values, so a field or file name containing a quote, CR, or LF came back **literal** on every `Bun.serve` `formData()` upload (a name `x"y` arrived as `x%22y`, a filename `a\r\nb.txt` as `a%0D%0Ab.txt`). Because Bun's own multipart encoder emits exactly those sequences, even Bun→Bun round-trips corrupted.

Reverse the three WHATWG sequences when decoding `name`/`filename` — `%0A`→LF, `%0D`→CR, `%22`→`"` — leaving every other byte (incl. `%20`/`%25`/`%41` and unknown `%xx`) untouched, matching undici (`%0A`/`%0D` case-insensitive, `%22` exact). The common path stays zero-copy — it only allocates when a `%` is present. Applied to both name and filename.

Decodes byte-identically to Node across name/filename and a Bun→Bun round-trip; literal percent sequences are preserved. Not a port regression — the Zig decoder omitted it too; Node is the reference.

## Summary

Customizes this repo's cloud environment so Claude Code on the web sessions land with the same baseline a freshly-set-up local worktree has, plus repo-local `/ship` and `/babysit-pr` adapters under `.claude/skills/` so the familiar workflows still resolve when the user's personal skills are not present.

Parallel to #672 (Codex Cloud setup, now merged). This PR mirrors that contract for Claude Code on the web and adds a graceful Playwright Chromium step on top.

## What changed

- **SessionStart hook** — `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` (registered in `.claude/settings.json`) gates on `$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` and delegates to a new bootstrap script. Local Claude Code sessions are unaffected (the hook is a no-op when the env var is unset). Invoked via `bash <path>` so the executable bit isn't required.
- **Bootstrap script** — `scripts/claude-code-web-setup.sh` mirrors #672's `scripts/codex-cloud-setup.sh` contract: marks `safe.directory`, configures `core.hooksPath`, activates pnpm via `corepack`, runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, verifies the dashboard's `@sentry/nextjs` resolution, runs Envio codegen, validates agent context. Adds Playwright Chromium install on top as a non-fatal step — restricted-egress envs warn instead of failing the bootstrap when `cdn.playwright.dev` is not in the network allowlist.
- **Repo-local `/ship` and `/babysit-pr` skill adapters** — `.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md`. author: torresashjiancyber
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a security vulnerability (CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation) in the VMware AVI connector by enabling TLS certificate verification for all client connections.

## Finding

The AVI client was configured with `session.SetInsecure` option, which disables TLS certificate verification. This allows potential man-in-the-middle attacks by accepting any certificate, including self-signed or invalid certificates.

**Severity:** High  
**CWE:** CWE-295 - Improper Certificate Validation  
**Finding ID:** avi-client-CWE-295-tls-verify-disabled

## Remediation

Removed the `session.SetInsecure` option from both `clients.NewAviClient()` calls in `internal/app/vmware-avi/client.go`:
- Line 77: Initial version check connection
- Line 101: Tenant-specific connection

With this change, the VMware AVI SDK will use secure TLS verification by default, validating certificates according to the system's trust store.

## Verification

The changes are minimal and focused:
- 1 file modified
- 2 insertions, 4 deletions
- Only removed insecure TLS settings

**Note:** Build and test failures in CI are due to a pre-existing GOROOT environment configuration issue and are not related to these security changes.

## Summary

- Add `createPayloadGuardMiddleware()` in `services/relayer/src/middleware/payloadGuard.ts` that rejects requests with a `Content-Length` exceeding the configured maximum **before** body parsing, preventing resource abuse
- Limit is configurable via `PayloadGuardOptions.maxBytes` or `RELAY_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` env var; defaults to 512 KiB (`DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`)
- Rejected requests receive HTTP **413** with structured JSON body containing error code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`
- Structured `console.warn` log on rejection includes reason code, content-length, limit, path, and method
- Wire middleware early in `server.ts` stack — before `express.json()` — to drop oversized payloads at the earliest possible point

## Test plan

- [ ] Valid payloads (Content-Length ≤ limit) pass through to next middleware
- [ ] Oversized payloads (Content-Length > limit) receive HTTP 413
- [ ] Response body contains `error: "PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE"`
- [ ] Requests with no `Content-Length` header pass through
- [ ] Custom threshold via `options.maxBytes` is respected
- [ ] `RELAY_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` env var overrides default
- [ ] `console.warn` is called with reason code on rejection

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

- Binds `Cmd+R` (`Ctrl+R` on Win/Linux) to reload the focused dev preview webview without restarting the dev server.
- Two code paths cover both focus scenarios: a scoped keybinding handles panel chrome focus; a main-process intercept handles when the webview guest itself has DOM focus (Chromium routes those keypresses straight to the OOPIF, so the renderer `keydown` never fires).
- Scoped to dev-preview panels only — browser panels are untouched.

Resolves #9497.

## Changes

**Scoped keybinding (panel chrome focus)**
- New `"dev-preview"` `KeyScope` in `keymap.ts`.
- `devPreview.reloadPreview` registered in `defaultKeybindings.ts` at priority 20.
- `DevPreviewPane` activates the scope via `useKeybindingScope(isFocused)`.

**Main-process intercept (webview guest focus)**
- `before-input-event` listener added in `protocols.ts`; fires `WEBVIEW_RELOAD_SHORTCUT` IPC when `Cmd/Ctrl+R` is detected (Shift variant excluded).
- `DevPreviewPane` subscribes to the channel, hard-reloads on panel match, and unsubscribes on unmount.
- Panel kind tracked in `WebviewDialogService` and threaded through `registerPanel` / `useWebviewDialog` so the intercept is scoped to dev-preview panels only.

## Testing

- `protocols.test.ts` — reload routing, Shift guard, browser-panel passthrough.
- `DevPreviewPane.webview.test.tsx` — reload on match, ignore on non-match, cleanup on unmount.
- Keymap registration verified against existing `KeyScope` precedents.

author: sgbirmingham
body:
## What

Adds `--rate N` to `replay.py` so the replay paces emissions based on each row's `ts_epoch_s`, scaled by `N`:

- `--rate 1.0` — real-time (1 s of CSV = 1 s wall)
- `--rate 10.0` — 10× faster (1 s of CSV = 100 ms wall)
- `--rate 60.0` — 60× faster (1 s of CSV = ~17 ms wall)
- _(omitted)_ — current burst behavior (default; runs in <1 s)

Implementation is a small generator (`_pace_frames`) wrapping `batch_frames()`. First frame yields immediately to anchor both clocks; subsequent frames wait until the proportional wall time has elapsed. Frames with non-advancing timestamps (logger pauses, duplicates, clock jitter) yield without blocking. Non-positive rates raise `ValueError` and `parser.error()` at the CLI level.

## Why

During today's bench session we observed that burst-mode replay pushes 22 events through the IPC chain in under a second — useful for "compare event lists" validation, but not for observing the daemon's queue / ACK-timing behavior under realistic load. A captured 48-min drive replayed at `--rate 1.0` produces events at the same cadence the vehicle would, exercising the daemon's TDMA scheduler and our `IpcTransport` keep-alive over an hour-long run.

10× and 60× modes are a useful middle ground: still spaces events out (so you can watch them scroll, observe ACK round-trip times) but finishes in a bench-friendly time window.

## How tested

- Local (Windows venv): **34 passed, 1 skipped** (was 29+1; +5 new pacing tests)
- Pi (ARM, Python 3.11): **38 passed in 1.14s** (was 33; +5 new)

New tests in `tests/test_replay_pacing.py` cover:

1. `test_introduces_proportional_delay` — 0.5 s of CSV @ rate=10 takes ~50 ms wall (generous 20-300 ms tolerance for jitter)
2. `test_first_frame_yields_immediately` — first frame doesn't block even with absurdly slow rates
3. `test_non_advancing_timestamps_do_not_sleep` — duplicate / backward timestamps yield immediately, never block for negative time
4. `test_rejects_zero_rate` — `_pace_frames` raises `ValueError` on rate=0
5. `test_rejects_negative_rate` — same for rate=-1.0

The CLI also calls `parser.error()` if `--rate <= 0`, surfacing the validation as a normal argparse error before any work starts.

## Files

- `src/skybounce_app_logistics/scripts/replay.py` — adds `import time`, `Iterator` typing, `_pace_frames` generator (~30 lines), `--rate` CLI arg, validation, "Rate:" line in startup banner, and the pacer wrap.
- `tests/test_replay_pacing.py` — new (5 tests, ~70 lines total)
- `docs/pi_deploy_cheatsheet.md` — Section 6 gets an "Optional: pace the replay" subsection showing the three useful rates and when to use each.

## Wire / runtime impact

None. Adds a CLI option; default behavior unchanged. No encoder, transport, or wire-format changes.

author: jwhui
body:
This commit fixes a frequent unit test flake in ot-test-trickle_timer under the TestTrickleTimerMinMaxIntervalChange test case.

The test case starts the trickle timer with Imin = 2000 and Imax = 2000. The random time t (mTimeInInterval) is chosen in [1000, 2000), so t can range up to 1999.

When t randomly evaluates to 1999, t + 1 becomes 2000. Calling timer.SetIntervalMax(2000) triggers an early-exit optimization in TrickleTimer::SetIntervalMax because mIntervalMax is already 2000, leaving the scheduled timer's fire time unchanged. The test then crashes on the assertion expecting the fire time to have changed.

This is resolved by setting the new interval max to Min(t + 1, interval - 1). This ensures that the requested value is strictly less than 2000 even when t = 1999, successfully triggering the interval shortening and rescheduling logic tested by this case.

author: neo37
body:
Core problem

  The extension was migrated to Chrome Manifest V3, which replaces the background page with a Service Worker. SWs have no document, no
  URL.createObjectURL, and in this environment DOMParser was also inaccessible — breaking virtually every key feature.

  ---
  What was done today

  Service Worker compatibility
  - Replaced all URL.createObjectURL / URL.revokeObjectURL calls with data URLs (encodeURIComponent for text, arrayBuffer + btoa for blobs)
  - Replaced the UUID trick via blob URL with crypto.randomUUID()
  - Added self.window = self polyfill before importScripts so Turndown's window check doesn't fail
  
  Turndown / HTML parsing in SW
  - The root cause: TurndownService needs document/DOMParser to parse HTML strings — neither exists in the SW
  - Multiple attempts to patch turndown.js (fallbacks, typeof DOMParser checks) — all failed because DOMParser itself wasn't accessible even as a
   bare global
  - Final solution: inject turndown.js, turndown-plugin-gfm.js, and a new convert-article.js into the tab page via executeScript, parse the HTML
  with new DOMParser() there (page context always has it), and pass the resulting DOM node to TurndownService — bypassing the internal
  htmlParser() entirely
  - Fixed TurndownService.prototype.defaultEscape not existing in the tab isolated world, causing self.escape is not a function and a silent
  fallback to the broken SW path
  
  PDF export
  - Single tab: replaced CDP Page.printToPDF with window.print() — opens the browser print dialog, no black background from dark-mode pages
  - Batch tabs: restored CDP but with printBackground: false — saves directly to Downloads without dialog, no black background

  Batch Markdown save ("All → Markdown")
  - Changed forEach (fire-and-forget) to a sequential for...of with await — previously SW went to sleep before all downloads completed, so only
  the first tab was actually saved
  - Added filtering to skip chrome://, chrome-extension://, about: tabs
  - Added saveAs: false for batch mode so Chrome doesn't block downloads after the first dialog

  Download filename fix
  - generateValidFileName now applied to title before passing to downloads.download — prevents Invalid filename errors from user-edited titles or
   special characters
  - Object.entries(imageList || {}) — guard against null imageList

  Debug logging
  - dbgLog() — persistent ring buffer (200 lines) stored in chrome.storage.local._debugLog
  - "Show debug log" button in popup downloads markdownload-debug.txt to the Downloads folder
  - Key conversion steps are logged (inject start, success/failure, markdown length)

## Summary
- Two public leaderboards: **XP** (weekly + all-time) and **completion %** (active bars solved), gated to onboarded users but viewable by anyone.
- **First-sign-in onboarding**: a blocking gate prompts for a unique `@handle` (case-insensitive unique via a `lower(handle)` index, with reserved-name + DE/EN/TR profanity validation). `avatarKey` column is stubbed for a future avatar pack.
- Rank rows show position, handle, level badge, and metric; caller's own rank sticks to the bottom when outside the top 100.

## Implementation notes

body:
## Summary

Operators routinely paste full UUIDs into curl / spreadsheets / bug reports. Adds a small **Copy** button next to the font-mono ID rendered on:

- **eval-run detail header** (`/preview/agents/eval-runs/[id]`)
- **run detail header** (`/preview/agents/workflows/[id]/runs/[runId]`)

## Implementation

New `components/agents/CopyId.tsx` — shared `'use client'` component:

- Renders `<id>` in font-mono with a Copy button beside it.
- `onClick`: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(id)`, flips label to **\"Copied!\"** for 1.5s via a `setTimeout` cleanup, then resets.
- Clipboard failure (insecure origin, document hidden) falls back to a no-op rather than throwing — operators can still select + Cmd-C the id; we don't want the click to bubble up an exception.
- `aria-label` is parameterized via the optional `label` prop (`\"eval run ID\"`, `\"run ID\"`) so screen readers announce which kind of id is being copied.

## Stacked PR

Stacked on #816 (M5.50 — row error excerpts). Merge that first.

## Definition of Done

- [x] **Reference audit**: Standard browser copy-to-clipboard pattern.
- [x] **Clean-room**: Hand-written.
- [x] **Local-first**: `pnpm typecheck` ✓, `pnpm prettier --write` ✓, `pnpm lint` ✓ (only pre-existing FileSharingLanding warning).
- [x] **Naming conventions**: `CopyId` in `components/agents/` matches the existing per-domain shared-component convention.
- [x] **Security**: Clipboard API is gated by the browser to same-origin secure contexts; failure swallowed safely.
- [x] **Architecture**: One small component, two consumers; no new endpoints or hooks.
- [x] **Tests**: No new logic to test — calls a single Web API and toggles local state.
- [x] **Accessibility**: `aria-label` parameterized; label change provides feedback to sighted users; falling back to text selection means non-clipboard browsers still work.

author: lusoris
body:
## Summary

- **Full sweep of all 24 `.cu` kernel files** in `core/src/feature/cuda/` and `core/src/cuda/` against every `cuModuleGetFunction` host-side lookup.
- **One broken file found**: `integer_ssim/integer_ssim_score.cu` — three `__global__` entry points not wrapped in `extern "C"`, causing `--feature ssim --backend cuda` to silently return `-EINVAL` from `init_fex_cuda` since the file was introduced.
- **Fix**: three-line insertion of `extern "C" { }` around entry points. All 23 other kernel files confirmed safe.
- **CI guard added**: `scripts/dev/check-cuda-extern-c.sh` fails if any kernel referenced by `cuModuleGetFunction` is found outside `extern "C"`. Mandatory invariant documented in `core/src/feature/cuda/AGENTS.md`.

This is a companion to PR #77 (which fixed the same pattern in `ssim_score.cu`). The ADR-0747 sweep confirms the audit is now complete across the full codebase.

## Root cause

nvcc compiles `.cu` files as C++. Without `extern "C"`, the symbols receive C++ name-mangling (`_Z31integer_ssim_horiz_8bpc...`). `cuModuleGetFunction` passes the plain C name and receives `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND`. The feature appears to init successfully up to that point but then silently produces no output.

author: iskandr
body:
Closes #105.

## What this PR does

Treats α and β chains identically at the J→C splice: peel the junction codon from the contig's first 3 nt past trimmed VDJ, translate to a per-clone residue, and prepend it to the per-clone canonical AA. Same code path for both chains.

### Pre-2.0 (asymmetric)

| Chain | Junction handling |
|---|---|
| α | None. TRAC stored as bare mature (`IQNPDPAVY...`). Every α chain assembled by tcrsift was **1 aa short** of the donor's expressed protein at the J→C boundary. The missing residue is J-dependent: across 118/118 audited B1 clones it's N (74×), Y (22×), D (13×), or H (9×). |
| β | Synthetic E prepended to `HUMAN_TRBC1_AA` / `HUMAN_TRBC2_AA` at FASTA-write time. Worked because β's junction codon is universally `GAG` (E) — but baked the universal-E case into the canonical AA instead of treating it as data. |

### 2.0 (uniform)

Both chains read the junction codon from the contig's first codon past trimmed VDJ. The packaged FASTA stores all three sequences as **bare mature**, matching UniProt directly. The junction residue is prepended per-clone in `_add_constant_regions`. NT bytes for the junction codon come from the donor's actual contig (donor fidelity preserved at the splice boundary, courtesy of #103's blend infrastructure).

## Breaking changes

- **`HUMAN_TRBC1_AA` / `HUMAN_TRBC2_AA` values change.** Direct consumers see different sequences (176/178 chars instead of 177/179, content shifted by 1 from idx 0 — no more synthetic `E`). `CONSTANT_REGION_ENDINGS` is unchanged.
- **β chains assembled WITHOUT contigs no longer get an implicit E prepend.** Same biological gap that α had pre-2.0: assembled mature β is 1 aa short, with a QC warning naming the chain. Run with `--contigs-dir` for the full-length output.

## New audit columns

- `alpha_junction_residue` and `beta_junction_residue` record what was peeled (or `None` when no prepend happened — no contig, stop codon, or N in the contig).

## Tests — LOTS, per the user's ask

**+50 net tests vs 1.3.0** (1166 → 1216 passed). New classes:

- **`TestTRACBiology`** (6 tests): mature start `IQNPDPAVY`, ending `LLMTLRLWSS`, Thr47 conservation, standard alphabet, no internal stop, no X.
- **`TestTRBC1Biology`** (10 tests): mature start `DLNK` (JOVI.1 NK tetrad), Glu9, Phe36, Val135, ending `VKRKDF`, no synthetic E prepend at idx 0.
- **`TestTRBC2Biology`** (11 tests): mature start `DLKN` (JOVI.1 KN — distinct from TRBC1), Lys9, Tyr36, Ser56, Glu135, ending `VKRKDSRG`, 2-aa-longer C-tail than TRBC1.
- **`TestTRBC1VsTRBC2DistinguishingResidues`** (8 tests): parametrized across the 5 internal-region distinguishing positions (3, 4, 9, 36, 135); asserts internal shared region (residues 1..170) is otherwise byte-identical and the C-tail structural divergence (`VKRKDF` vs `VKRKDSRG`) is preserved.
- **`TestJunctionResidueUniformly`** (15 tests): α parametrized N/Y/D/H, β (TRBC1 and TRBC2 with universal E junction), JOVI.1 epitope formation at the boundary for TRBC1 (`EDLNK`) vs TRBC2 (`EDLKN`), gene-specific C-tail preservation, explicit α-and-β-use-same-code-path integration. Also: stop-codon-at-junction warning, no-contig fallback warnings naming the chain.

author: egonschiele
body:
Brings the `tests/examples/markdown` example up to near-CommonMark coverage plus VitePress-style YAML frontmatter, all built from Tarsec combinators (the example is meant to showcase the library, so it deliberately avoids regex and manual string slicing).

## Refactor

The original single-file `tests/examples/markdown.ts` is now a folder package:

- `types.ts` — AST types
- `inline.ts` — inline parsers (bold, italic, code, links, …)
- `blocks.ts` — block parsers (headings, code blocks, lists, …)
- `references.ts` — reference / footnote definitions + post-parse resolution pass
- `frontmatter.ts` — YAML frontmatter
- `index.ts` — composes everything into the top-level `markdownParser`

## Inline features added

Escape sequences (`\*`, `\[`, …), underscore emphasis with a snake_case guard (`_x_`, `__x__`), combined `***bold-italic***` / `___…___`, `~~strikethrough~~`, autolinks (`<http(s)://…>` and `<email>`), hard line breaks (two trailing spaces or backslash), inline images embedded in paragraphs, and deferred reference-style links / images (`[text][id]`, `[text][]`, shortcut `[text]`).

## Block features added

ATX headings (now inline-aware), setext-style headings, fenced code blocks (language tags accept hyphens / digits / `+`), indented code blocks, multi-line and nested block quotes, unordered / ordered / nested lists, pipe tables with `:--`/`:-:`/`--:` alignment, horizontal rules, and HTML block passthrough.

## Reference resolution

`[id]: url "title"` link definitions and `[^id]: …` footnote definitions are parsed as their own blocks, then resolved in a single post-parse walk of the AST (link defs fill in `inline-ref-link` / `inline-ref-image` nodes, footnote defs fill in `inline-footnote-ref` nodes).

## VitePress-style YAML frontmatter

An optional `---`-delimited block at the very top of the document, per https://vitepress.dev/guide/frontmatter. Covers a useful YAML subset:

- top-level `key: value` entries
- scalars: bare strings, single / double-quoted strings, integers, floats, `true`/`false`, `null`/`~`
- inline flow lists: `[a, b, "c d"]`
- correctly classifies `trueblue` / `nullable` as plain strings

When present it surfaces as the first AST node `{ type: \"frontmatter\", data: {...} }`; when absent existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Structural fixes to what already existed

- Paragraphs terminate at a blank line.
- Bold-vs-italic precedence is correct (`**` consumed before `*`).
- Inline text's stop set covers all the new delimiters.
- Fenced code block language tags accept hyphens / digits / `+` (so `objective-c`, `c++`, `ts2` work).

## Tests

- 368 tests pass across 53 files (was 356 / 52 on main); 0 regressions.
- Every new behaviour has at least one focused test in `tests/examples/markdown/{inline,blocks,references,frontmatter,index}.test.ts`, written before its implementation.
- Smoke test in `markdown-longer.test.ts` parses the repo's real README and tutorial files end-to-end.

## Docs

`README.md` Examples link now points to the new folder package and enumerates its capabilities. `CHANGELOG` has an `Unreleased` entry summarizing the work.

## Plan

The full TDD plan lived in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-28-markdown-parser-completion.md`.

## Summary

This PR adds network-aware activation registry tooling for checking and activating Base-native features across vibes, local devnet, Base mainnet, Base Sepolia, Base Zeronet, and custom RPCs. It introduces shared network/default resolution plus a single canonical feature list so the check and activation scripts stay in sync. The activator keeps the local devnet Hardhat key default, but remote networks require an explicit admin key and pass it to cast via scoped ETH_PRIVATE_KEY instead of argv. The scripts also report RPC/check errors separately, handle balance-query failures explicitly, and use a safer bash trim helper.

author: bruaristimunha
body:
## Summary

- `infer_source_from_dataset_id` now recognises **`on######`** (OpenNeuro-imported NEMAR mirrors). Without this, the 51 `on*` datasets on data.nemar.org never reached the nemar backend.
- The data.nemar.org safety net delegates to **[`nemar-py`](https://pypi.org/project/nemar-py/) >=0.2.0** — the official NEMAR client — instead of duplicating manifest parsing, BIDS-path → annex-key resolution, and download/verification.
- `nemar-py >=0.2.0` keeps `datalad` and `git-annex` as opt-in extras (`nemar-py[datalad]`), so the runtime install stays lean.

## Context

Two problems on `fix-s3`:

1. **`on*` IDs were invisible.** `_source_inference.py` only matched `ds*` / `nm*` / `EEG2025*` / `EEGManyLabs`. OpenNeuro-imported NEMAR mirrors (e.g. `on002181`) fell through to `None`, so `correct_storage_inplace` never set `storage.backend = "nemar"` for them, and the data-portal safety net never fired.
2. **The runtime had its own NEMAR primitives.** Constants for the manifest URL, a custom fetcher, a manifest-entry resolver, an annex-key extractor — all of which are already in `nemar-py`. After studying `/Users/bruaristimunha/Projects/nemar-py` (in particular `tests/integration/test_eegdash_trio.py` whose docstring is literally _"if this passes, the eegdash integration story holds"_), it became clear we were re-implementing nemar-py's public API.

This PR adds the missing prefix recognition and replaces ~50 lines of bespoke NEMAR plumbing with a call into `nemar.NEMARClient` + `download_one`.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `eegdash/dataset/_source_inference.py` | +6: `on######` clause + docstring |
| `eegdash/dataset/base.py` | net +90: drop `_NEMAR_DATA_MANIFEST_URL`, `_fetch_nemar_data_manifest`, `_resolve_nemar_data_entry`, `_annex_key_from_manifest_url`; slim `_download_nemar_data_file` to delegate to nemar-py; cache `_fetch_nemar_manifest` via `lru_cache` |
| `pyproject.toml` | +5: `nemar-py>=0.2.0` dependency with rationale comment |
| `tests/unit_tests/dataset/test_base.py` | +92: new `test_nemar_download_required_files_falls_back_to_data_portal` that mocks the nemar-py path |
| `tests/unit_tests/dataset/test_source_inference.py` | +25: `on*` parametrized cases + `expected_storage_base("on002181")` + `test_correct_storage_reroutes_misrouted_openneuro_mirror` |

## Test plan

- [x] Targeted unit tests: `pytest tests/unit_tests/dataset/test_base.py tests/unit_tests/dataset/test_source_inference.py tests/unit_tests/test_downloader.py tests/functional/test_dataset_constructor_contracts.py -q` → **172 passed**
- [x] Full sweep: `pytest tests/unit_tests/ tests/functional/ -q` → **979 passed, 3 skipped** (previously 19 were failing on `data.eegdash.org` IP-block; after unblock they all pass)
- [x] `ruff check` clean on touched files
- [x] **Live end-to-end**: downloaded `nm000104` `sub-01438774/ses-1625443841/emg/...bdf` (61 MiB) via `EEGDashRaw._download_required_files()` against real NEMAR S3 — MD5 matched manifest checksum, 50 s, single anonymous GET on `s3://nemar/nm000104/objects/{MD5E-...}`

## Notes

- Anonymous `GetObject` works against `https://nemar.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/{nemar_id}/objects/{annex_key}` — confirmed by direct `curl` probes. List is blocked (matches the existing comment in `downloader._filesystem_get`).
- The data.nemar.org manifest is the source of truth for the BIDS-path → annex-key mapping; once the digestion pipeline writes `annex_keys` into every record (re-digest), the safety net becomes effectively dormant and the runtime takes the verified happy path (annex-key lookup → S3 GET).

## Summary
Replaces the Chrome-handoff placeholder on the lesson play CTA with an in-app WebView viewer so PDFs, articles, and embedded videos open **inside EduLife**. Closing the viewer reports the lesson as complete through the existing idempotent endpoint.

## What changed
- **New** `LessonDetail` model + `GET /api/v1/courses/{courseId}/lessons/{id}` on `ApiService` (was missing — the player only had nav-args, no detail fetch).
- `LessonPlayerFragment`:

  - PDFs (type=`PDF` or `*.pdf`) routed through Google Docs gview embed so they render inside the WebView, not in an external reader.
  - `contentBody` fallback rendered as inline HTML for lessons with no `contentUrl`.
  - In-app back press and close button stop playback (`about:blank`) and hide the viewer before reporting completion.
  - Auto-mark complete on close for non-preview enrolled lessons; manual "Mark as Done" still works (backend is idempotent → no double-write).
  - `onDestroyView` tears the WebView down so audio cannot keep playing after navigation.

## WebView hardening
- JavaScript: **on** (Google Docs embed and most players need it)
- `allowFileAccess` / `allowContentAccess`: **off** (no reads of app-private files via crafted URLs)
- `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`: only `http(s)` schemes loaded; everything else blocked

body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in backend-only remote WebSocket bridge for live TUI gateway sessions. The bridge lets a remote/mobile client attach to existing TUI sessions over the existing gateway JSON-RPC flow (`session.active_list` / `session.activate`) without taking ownership away from the local TUI transport.

The bridge is disabled by default and keeps secure defaults:

- loopback listener by default (`127.0.0.1:8769/api/tui/ws`)
- token required for non-loopback binds
- Host/Origin checks around remote websocket connections
- event fan-out mirrors session events to remote bridge transports while preserving the primary local transport

## Related Issue

None. Related upstream PR search found adjacent remote/dashboard websocket work, but this PR is scoped specifically to live TUI gateway session mirroring.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/remote_bridge.py`
  - Adds remote bridge config parsing, listener URL metadata, FastAPI/uvicorn startup, websocket auth, host/origin validation, and the opt-in factory.
- `tui_gateway/entry.py`
  - Starts the bridge when enabled and includes bridge metadata in `gateway.ready`.
- `tui_gateway/server.py`
  - Adds bridge transport attach/detach and best-effort event fan-out for session-scoped events.
- `tui_gateway/ws.py`
  - Registers remote bridge websocket transports on `session.activate` and cleans them up on disconnect.
- `hermes_cli/config.py`
  - Adds default `tui_remote_bridge` config keys.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`
  - Documents the opt-in config and environment variables.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_remote_bridge.py`
  - Covers bridge attach behavior, mirroring without replacing primary transport, stale transport cleanup, and auth/host/origin validation.

## How to Test

1. Run focused gateway tests:
   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_remote_bridge.py tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py
   ```
2. Run syntax/config/security checks:
   ```bash
   python -m py_compile tui_gateway/remote_bridge.py tui_gateway/ws.py tui_gateway/entry.py tui_gateway/server.py
   python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff origin/main
   git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
   python - <<'PY'
   import pathlib, yaml
   with pathlib.Path('cli-config.yaml.example').open() as f:
       yaml.safe_load(f)
   PY
   ```
3. Optional manual smoke:
   ```bash
   HERMES_TUI_REMOTE_BRIDGE=1 \
   HERMES_TUI_REMOTE_BRIDGE_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
   hermes --tui
   ```
   Then connect a websocket client to `ws://127.0.0.1:8769/api/tui/ws` and use existing TUI gateway JSON-RPC methods such as `session.active_list` and `session.activate`.

Local verification run on Linux 7.0.10-arch1-1:

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_remote_bridge.py tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` — 194 passed
- `python -m py_compile tui_gateway/remote_bridge.py tui_gateway/ws.py tui_gateway/entry.py tui_gateway/server.py` — passed

- `cli-config.yaml.example` parsed with PyYAML — passed

No real mobile client/UI smoke was run; this PR is intentionally backend-only.

author: vanja-p
body:
Stacked on #12236. With #12183 and #12236 in place, the server is ready to merge a follow-up `stage=COMPLETED` Operation carrying `PostCompletionStats`. This change has the executor produce and send those stats.

- **Firecracker**: accumulate `SnapshotSavedLocally/Remotely`, `SnapshotIsDiff`, `SnapshotSizeBytes` (summing uncompressed COW chunk bytes — dirty for diff, all for full), and `PauseDurationUsec` during `Pause()`; expose via `FirecrackerContainer.PostCompletionStats()`.
- **Runner**: add `PostCompletionStats()` to `interfaces.Runner`; `taskRunner` forwards via a type assertion so non-firecracker runners return nil.
- **Executor**: after `TryRecycle` returns, if the runner exposes stats and we already publish a regular COMPLETED message, send a separate COMPLETED message with just PostCompletionStats in aux meta. Only do this if the `remote_execution.publish_post_completion_stats` is on. This prevents the executor from sending a COMPLETED message with just PostCompletionStats when the server will treat it as a full COMPLETED message.

## Autopilot Fix

**Issue:** ## REVERT: Switch contributor/recipient dropdowns from GAS to DaoMembersCache

The previous PR #4 (commit 50479ef8) switched the contributor/recipient dropdowns to use `DaoMembersCache.fetchSnapshot()` (dao_members.json), but this only contains 12 verified contributors (those with public keys). The GAS `?recipients=true` endpoint returns ~260 contributors from the Main Ledger's Contributors sheet.

This is a significant regression — the dropdown would only show 12 names instead of 260.

## The Real Fix

The proper solution is to publish the full contributors list to the treasury-cache JSON (dao_offchain_treasury.json), so it's CDN-served but includes everyone. This requires changes on the GAS publisher side (tokenomics repo) to add a `contributors` array alongside the existing `managers` array.

For now, revert to the GAS endpoint which has the complete list.

## Changes

1. **report_contribution.html** — Revert `loadContributors()` back to fetching from `DAO_FORMS_ENDPOINT?recipients=true`
2. **report_inventory_movement.html** — Revert `loadRecipients()` back to fetching from `DAO_FORMS_BASE?recipients=true`

author: rohan-c0de
body:
## What changes for someone using the site

Community College of Philadelphia (CCP) is now in PA's course search. Students looking for fall or summer CCP classes will find **3,039 published sections** on `/pa` — Fall 2026 (2,156) and Summer 2026 (883). CCP enrolls ~16,000 students and is the third-largest PA CC; together with DCCC + HACC (already in #697), the three colleges now in PA cover over half of statewide CC enrollment.

## What changes on the technical front

- New per-state wrapper `scripts/pa/scrape-banner-8.ts` — thin caller around the existing shared Banner 8 template (`scripts/lib/scrape-banner-8.ts`), following the same pattern as `scripts/mt/scrape-banner8.ts`.
- `scripts/pa/scrape-banner-8.ts` added to `StateConfig.scrapers.courses` alongside the Banner SSB 9 wrapper that landed in #697.
- CCP runs the classic Oracle PL/SQL Banner 8 self-service interface at `https://oasis.ccp.edu:4051/pls/prod`. Standard endpoints (`bwckschd.p_disp_dyn_sched`, `bwckschd.p_get_crse_unsec`) respond, so the template handles it without modification.

## Why this is a separate PR

This work was originally going to ride on #697, but two extra commits got pushed after I told you "merge when checks pass" and you'd already clicked Merge — the commits ended up orphaned on the remote branch and never reached main. Cherry-picking them onto a fresh branch off main here. The CLAUDE.md merge-race rule worked exactly as written.

## Endpoint discovery

CCP's SIS wasn't surfaced by the fingerprinter — the URL lives on a non-standard subdomain (`oasis.ccp.edu`) and non-443 port (`:4051`), and the homepage doesn't link to it. I found it by reading a hyperlink on `/admission-aid/admissions/admissions-process`. The fingerprinter initially classified CCP as `custom HTML/SPA`.

This is worth flagging as a fingerprinter-improvement signal — there are likely other "custom HTML" colleges across other states with a Banner 8 SIS hiding behind a non-standard host. Worth a re-probe pass on the 207-college untemplated set.

## Data quality

| Term | Sections | Dominant start date | Zero-credit % |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2026FA | 2,156 | 2026-09-08 | 6.5% |
| 2026SU | 883 | 2026-05-11 / 2026-07-07 | low |

All spot-checks per the state-audit playbook pass. instructor / seats_open / seats_total fields are null — CCP's Banner 8 endpoints don't expose those publicly, matching other Banner 8 deployments.

## Audit grade impact

| Dimension | Before #697 | After #697 | After this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| courses | F (0/15) | D (2/15, 13% — under F-floor) | **D (3/15, 20%)** |

## Test plan
- [ ] Vercel preview deploy renders course results on `/pa/college/ccp`
- [ ] After merge, `import-on-merge.yml` syncs CCP sections to Supabase
- [ ] Cron pickup for CCP confirmed on next scheduled tick

author: amackillop
body:
The release job was mixing actions/setup-node for npm and a one-shot `nix run nixpkgs#minisign` for signing. Two installers, two pinning stories, and the node version was set in YAML rather than in the flake.

Add a dedicated `devShells.release` with nodejs_24, minisign, and jq. Point the job's default `run` shell at `nix develop .#release --command bash`, drop `actions/setup-node`, and call `minisign` directly.

nodejs_24 is the first nodejs package in nixpkgs 25.11 that ships npm >= 11.5, which is what npm trusted publishing via GitHub OIDC requires. The switch to trusted publishing is a separate follow-up; for now token-based auth still works because we write the .npmrc ourselves, the same thing setup-node was doing for us.

Also wire up Magic Nix Cache so the release devShell survives across runs.

author: rajesh180675
body:
**Plan 9 PR-9.3** — DR backups: pure scheduler logic + restore-drill runbook.

Production data lives in two stores: Vercel KV (audit runs, comparison registries, residuals, annotations) and Vercel Blob (large envelopes, locked evidence). Neither has automatic point-in-time recovery on the Hobby plan, so we need our own snapshot mechanism.

### What ships
- **`src/lib/backupScheduler.ts`** — pure scheduler logic
  - `POLICIES` per scope (audit-runs, comparison-registries, residuals, annotations, locked-evidence, event-log)
  - `shouldSnapshotNow(lastBackupAt, now, frequency)` — gate function
  - `retentionWindow(now, retentionDays)` — cutoff timestamp
  - `snapshotKey(now, scope)` — lexicographic-sortable Blob path
  - `withinRetention(keys, policy, now)` — prune helper
- **`docs/BACKUP_RUNBOOK.md`** — quarterly drill schedule, pre-drill checklist, 8-step drill, failure-mode table, post-drill cleanup

### Retention policy
| Scope | Frequency | Retention |
|---|---|---|
| audit-runs | daily | 90 days |
| comparison-registries | daily | 90 days |
| residuals | daily | 90 days |
| annotations | daily | 365 days |
| locked-evidence | hourly | forever (legal record) |
| event-log | hourly | 7 years (compliance) |

### Why pure logic now, worker as follow-up
The Vercel Cron worker (`api/cron/snapshot.js`) is a thin shell that calls the pure scheduler — once the policy is right, the wiring is mechanical. Same pattern as PR-4.x (kvClient + identity, then per-feature stores).

### Acceptance
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- backupScheduler — 16/16 pass

author: drodriguezatcci
body:
## Resumen

Cuando un inversionista entra a un crédito en el **mes anterior** al período liquidado (caso que ya disparaba el cálculo proporcional) y ADEMÁS hizo **compras de cartera completadas** durante ese mes, hoy el sistema prorrateaba el interés sobre el `monto_aportado` completo del espejo. Eso ignora que la parte que el inversionista ya tenía **antes** de las compras tiene derecho a la tarifa mensual completa, no a la proporcional.

Este PR separa el cálculo en dos componentes y deja registro del desglose en la tabla `pagos_credito_inversionistas_espejo`.

## Ejemplo concreto

Supongamos:
- Inversionista entra al crédito en **mayo** (`fecha_inicio_participacion = 2026-05-07`).
- Ya tenía **Q10,000** en el crédito desde antes (compras viejas, históricas).
- El **día 7 de mayo** hizo una compra adicional de **Q15,000**.
- El espejo queda con `monto_aportado = Q25,000`.
- Cuando se calculan pagos para **junio**, se dispara el proporcional (mayo = mes anterior).
- Crédito con `porcentaje_interes = 5%`, inversionista con `porcentaje_participacion = 100%`.
- Mayo tiene 31 días, fecha de inicio día 7 → `diasProporcionales = 31 - 7 = 24`.

### Antes (bug)
```
montoInversionistaCalc = 25,000 × 5% × 100% = Q1,250
bigInteres = 1,250 / 31 × 24 = Q967.74
```
Se prorratean los Q25k completos. Los Q10k que ya estaban (con derecho a mes entero) se subpagan.

### Ahora
```
sumaCompras  = 15,000          ← compras_credito_inversionista (mayo, completadas, compra_cartera)
montoViejo   = 25,000 - 15,000 = 10,000

interesSinCompras = 10,000 × 5% × 100%             = Q500.00     ← mensual completo
interesConCompras = 15,000 × 5% × 100% × (24/31)   = Q580.65     ← proporcional

abono_interes = 500.00 + 580.65 = Q1,080.65
abono_iva_12  = (500 + 580.65) × 12% = Q129.68
```

El inversionista cobra **Q112.91 más** de interés en este caso. Las columnas `abono_interes_sin_compras = 500.00` y `abono_interes_con_compras = 580.65` quedan registradas en la fila del pago espejo para auditoría.

## Casos cubiertos

| Caso | Comportamiento |
|---|---|
| `sumaCompras = 0` (no hubo compras del mes anterior) | Igual que hoy — todo proporcional sobre `montoInversionistaCalc`. Las 4 columnas nuevas quedan NULL. |
| `sumaCompras > 0` y `montoViejo > 0` (caso del ejemplo) | Cálculo dual. Las 4 columnas se guardan. |
| `sumaCompras = monto_aportado` (las compras son todo lo aportado) | `montoViejo = 0` → todo proporcional como hoy. |
| `sumaCompras > monto_aportado` (inconsistencia) | `console.warn` con datos + cae al caso "todo proporcional" — no falla. En la buena teoría no debería pasar (otras validaciones del flujo lo cazarían antes), pero queda el log defensivo. |
| `!esMesAnterior` | Sin cambios — flujo normal. |
| `isCube` | Sin cambios — Cube nunca prorratea. |

## Cambios

### 1. Migration `drizzle/0005_add_pago_espejo_proporcional_compras.sql`
Agrega 4 columnas nullable a `cartera.pagos_credito_inversionistas_espejo`:
- `abono_interes_sin_compras NUMERIC(18, 10)`
- `abono_interes_con_compras NUMERIC(18, 10)`
- `abono_iva_12_sin_compras NUMERIC(18, 2)`
- `abono_iva_12_con_compras NUMERIC(18, 2)`

### 2. `schema.ts`
Refleja las 4 columnas en la definición Drizzle.

### 3. `utils/comprasAjuste.ts` — helper `obtenerSumaComprasMesAnterior`
Suma `monto_aportado` de compras filtradas por:
- `credito_id` + `inversionista_id`
- `tipo_operacion = 'compra_cartera'` (excluye reinversión)
- `status = 'completado'` (excluye pendientes — esas todavía no actualizaron `fecha_inicio_participacion`)
- `updated_at` dentro del **mes anterior** a `fechaPeriodo`

No reusamos `calcularAjusteCompras` porque ese ahora incluye reinversiones y maneja casos 2/3 con lógica distinta.

### 4. `controllers/payments.ts` — `insertPagosCreditoInversionistas`
Dos cambios:

**(a)** `esMesAnterior` ahora se compara contra `fechaDelPeriodo` (la fecha del período liquidado), no contra `new Date()` ("hoy"). Era un fix pendiente del PR #757 — incluido acá porque está en el mismo bloque.

**(b)** Bloque proporcional reescrito con lógica dual sin/con compras (ver pseudocódigo del ejemplo arriba).

## Test plan
- [ ] Correr migration `0005_add_pago_espejo_proporcional_compras.sql` (manual).
- [ ] Calcular pagos para un inversionista que **entró el mes anterior** y **no tiene compras** del mes anterior → resultado idéntico al de hoy, las 4 columnas en NULL.
- [ ] Calcular pagos para un inversionista que **entró el mes anterior** y **sí tiene compras** del mes anterior → `abono_interes` = suma del desglose, las 4 columnas con valor.
- [ ] Caso borde: `sumaCompras = monto_aportado` → resultado igual al actual.
- [ ] Caso borde: inversionista que entró este mes (no el anterior) → no aplica proporcional ni dual.
- [ ] Inversionista Cube → sigue sin proporcional ni dual.

## Notas
- El IVA se calcula sobre cada componente por separado (`ivaSinCompras = interesSinCompras × 0.12`, idem `ivaConCompras`). La suma `abono_iva_12` puede diferir en centavos vs `abono_interes × 0.12` por redondeo, pero deja claro el origen.
- Las 4 columnas nuevas son nullable. Registros viejos / casos sin desglose quedan NULL, así no hay que rellenar nada.
