author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

`LemonField` rendered every label with an empty `htmlFor`, so clicking a label did nothing — a dead-click pattern visible in session replay across the signup form and any other Kea-Forms field built with `LemonField`. PostHog inbox surfaced this from rage-clicks on the "Where did you hear about us?" label of the org-creation form.

The Kea-Forms template never threaded an id into `LemonPureField`, and for render-prop children (`{({ value, onChange }) => <LemonInput ... />}`) the underlying `LemonInput` was never given an `id` either, so both ends of the label/input association were missing.

## Changes

- `LemonField` now generates a stable id with `useId()` and exposes it as the label's `htmlFor` via `LemonPureField`.
- The id resolution prefers (1) an explicit `htmlFor` prop, (2) any id kea-forms has already injected onto a React-element child, and (3) the generated id as a fallback for the render-prop case.
- The rendered child is cloned so its `id` matches the label's `for` — `LemonInput` already forwards `id` to the underlying `<input>`, so the standard browser label-focus behavior is restored everywhere `LemonField` is used.

No call-site changes required: forms using either form (React-element child or render-prop) are fixed by the template.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Code). Only automated tests were run, no manual UI verification:

- Added `frontend/src/lib/lemon-ui/LemonField/LemonField.test.tsx` covering:
  - `LemonField.Pure` passing an explicit `htmlFor` through to the label.
  - The signup-style **function-as-child** case — confirms the rendered `LemonInput` ends up with an id matching the label's `for`.
  - The React-element-child case — confirms the kea-forms id used by the input is the same id used on the label.
- Ran `pnpm jest frontend/src/lib/lemon-ui` — 13 suites, 146 tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` for the changed files surfaces no new errors.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## 🤖 Agent context

Authored by PostHog Code in response to inbox report `019dfe02-f4b5-7077-9583-ec2394ae30bf`.

Investigation:
- Fetched the inbox report and confirmed root cause in `LemonField.tsx` (Kea-Forms template never propagated `htmlFor`) and noted that `SignupReferralSource.tsx` is one of many affected call sites.
- Read the kea-forms `Field` source (3.2.0) to confirm it already computes an id for React-element children via `cloneElement` but does **not** inject ids for function-as-child render props. That asymmetry shaped the resolution order in the fix.

Considered approaches:
- **Rejected:** updating individual call sites (e.g. passing `id` explicitly inside `SignupReferralSource`) — leaves the rest of the product still broken and easy to regress.
- **Chosen:** fix in `LemonField` itself so every consumer benefits with no API change. Cloning the rendered kids is safe because consumers that already supply an id keep theirs (precedence check in the resolver).

This PR requires human review before merge.

body:
This pull request updates the way the Android app's `versionCode` is managed, ensuring it is automatically computed from the semantic version and consistently injected into builds, both for local development and release automation. This streamlines the release process and reduces manual errors.

**Automated versionCode management:**

* The `versionCode` is now computed from the semantic version (MAJOR*10000 + MINOR*100 + PATCH) in the release script, ensuring unique and incrementing codes for each release.
* The computed `versionCode` is injected into Gradle builds via the `-Pversion.code` property for both debug and release APK/AAB builds in the release script. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-690b5575283d13f410a10259e846a31117087202b008d311a2659bf129b6585cL175-R181) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-690b5575283d13f410a10259e846a31117087202b008d311a2659bf129b6585cR193) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-690b5575283d13f410a10259e846a31117087202b008d311a2659bf129b6585cR216)
* The Gradle build script (`android/app/build.gradle.kts`) now reads `versionCode` from the injected property, defaulting to 1 for local development builds. author: danielloader
body:
## Summary
Three related fixes to the WHERE/HAVING filter editor (`FilterInput` + `FilterChip`), all verified in a live browser against real `claude-code` metrics data.

### 1. Value completion on Enter
Pressing Enter while mid-typing a **value** now accepts the highlighted suggestion (the full value) instead of committing the partial text. `textToFilter` treats a partial like `db4` as a complete filter, so Enter was submitting the half-typed value rather than the one the dropdown was showing. The same now applies to field-name completion. (Multi-value-by-arrow already worked because an empty value parsed to `null`; this makes the single-suggestion / partial-typed case behave consistently.)

### 2. Boolean fields commit on select
Selecting a boolean field — `is_root`, `error`, or any `bool`-typed attribute — commits `= true` immediately, rather than dropping into the operator phase and forcing the user to type `= true`. A boolean meta field is a complete search on its own.

### 3. Single-clickable filter chips
A committed filter now reads as **one clickable entity**. Clicking it drops the whole `field op value` back into the free-form input as a single editable string; Enter re-commits it to a chip. Previously only the field opened an editor — you couldn't click the operator or value to change them without re-typing the field.

## Test plan (Playwright, against a snapshot of the running DB)
- [x] `organization.id = db4` (single value): Enter completes to the full UUID, second Enter commits it — no longer commits `db4`
- [x] `is_` + Enter → commits `is_root = true` directly
- [x] Click `is_root = true` chip → inline single-box editor → change to `= false` → Enter → re-commits as `is_root = false`
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean; `go tool task build` clean

author: ericmehl
body:
This fixes a bug that could cause errors with isolated task dispatches.

If there is a string plug in the script `variables` plug that uses frame substitution, dispatching in isolated mode would error with `Context has no variable named "frame"`. This is a result of our use of serialisation followed by execution to copy / paste the script variables from the source script to the isolation script. `execute()` will compute values of the `variables` plugs, but the `TaskBatch` context that is active during dispatch purposefully omits the `frame` variable, resulting in an error.

One way to not perform string substitution is to get the value of a string plug outside of a compute Process. This is used by the `ScriptNodeBinding::serialise()` method and I'm using the same here.

Would it be more appropriate to put the test in `ScriptNodeTest`? I looked into that but I'm not sure how to get a `ScriptNode.execute()` call within a compute process so I couldn't get a test failure without the fix.

author: vishutdhar
body:
## Why
The single-page layout had no persistent navigation or call-to-action below the fold. The logo and Call button lived only inside the hero and footer, and the mobile call bar was removed previously (#4) for overlapping the hero — so a deep-scroll visitor, especially on mobile, had no way to call without scrolling back to the top.

## What
A fixed app-bar that:
- Stays **hidden over the hero** (preserving the approved full-bleed first impression), then **slides in once scrolled past it**.
- Carries the brand (logo + wordmark → back to top), desktop anchor nav (Services / Why Mike / Work / Areas / Contact), and an **always-available lime Call button** (compact on mobile).
- Reuses the existing brand system exactly: forest/cream/lime tokens, Manrope display font, rounded-full lime CTA, and the shared focus-ring pattern.

## Progressive enhancement (mirrors `ScrollReveal`)
- **SSR / JS disabled / crawlers** → header renders **visible, solid, interactive**. Nothing is hidden behind JS.
- **JS enabled** → hides the bar over the hero and reveals it on scroll.
- While hidden it is marked **`inert`** so its links stay out of the tab/pointer order until revealed.
- Respects **`prefers-reduced-motion`** (appears without the slide).
- Adds **`scroll-padding-top`** so in-page anchor jumps clear the revealed bar.

`fixed` (not `sticky`) so it reserves no layout space — the hero stays flush to the top.

## Files
- `src/components/site-header.tsx` — new client component
- `src/app/page.tsx` — mount header after the skip link
- `src/app/globals.css` — `scroll-padding-top` for the fixed-header anchor offset

## Verification
Production build (`next build`) clean, 0 type errors. Verified on the prod build via headless browser at 1440px and 390px:
- At `scrollY 0`: `inert=true`, `opacity 0` (hidden, non-focusable), hero untouched.
- At `scrollY 1400`: `inert=false`, `opacity 1`, pinned `top:0`, full nav + Call button.
- Mobile: brand + compact Call pill, nav hidden.

Reversible: `main` untouched until merge; the live site (manual `vercel --prod`) is unaffected by the merge.

body:
## What & why

Establishes the **post-launch operational documentation set** — the docs you reach for when
someone (often an ITS colleague) asks how Scholars *behaves in production*, as opposed to the
build-time specs.

It adds a curated, question-oriented index (`docs/DOCUMENTATION-REGISTRY.md`) and the eight
docs that close the gaps the registry's first pass identified.

## New docs

| Doc | Answers |
|---|---|
| `DOCUMENTATION-REGISTRY.md` | The index — "someone asks X → go to doc Y", grouped by operational concern. |
| `architecture-overview.md` | One-page map: request / write / ETL paths (mermaid diagrams), the six CDK stacks, environments. |
| `dependency-outage-matrix.md` | Every upstream (ED, InfoEd, COI, ASMS, Jenzabar, ReciterDB, ReciterAI, NIH/NSF/NLM, SES) and exactly what breaks vs stays up if each is down. |
| `performance-baseline.md` | Measured baseline + SLO targets + alarm thresholds + how to (re)measure. |
| `data-dictionary.md` | The public data model (35 models / 7 enums) with **source of record** per table. |
| `logging-reference.md` | Log groups + retention, the structured `event:` vocabulary, Logs Insights recipes. |
| `network-security-topology.md` | Review-ready VPC / subnet / SG / egress / edge picture + threat-model summary. |
| `cost-model.md` | Audited baseline, deployed budget/anomaly guardrails, cost drivers. |
| `access-control-rbac.md` | The three authorization layers — application RBAC (self / superuser / unit Owner / Curator), AWS IAM, DB roles — plus the deploy gate and break-glass. |

All are grounded in the actual IaC / schema / code (CDK `config.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`,
`lib/edit/authz.ts`, etc.), not prose memory. Every internal link resolves against `master`.

## Notable decisions

- **No fabricated numbers.** Per-surface latency and post-Edge cost actuals are marked
  `TBD (measure)` with the method to collect them, since a real baseline needs post-launch
  traffic. Registry § 10 tracks those data-collection follow-ons.
- **Open questions → issue #560.** Genuine decisions needing a stakeholder answer (end-user
  SLO, prod WAF topology, DR sign-off, access recert, ETL→WCM routing, SAML cert rollover,
  post-launch ops ownership, …) are listed in registry § 11 and tracked in #560.
- **Corrects two stale claims in `PRODUCTION.md`** (called out, not edited out): ETL is Step
  Functions + Fargate (not Lambda); Aurora is Serverless v2 (not `db.r6g.large`).
- **Adopts two orphaned docs** the registry links to so the index is self-consistent:
  `proposal-fidelity.md` and `waf-request-RITM0792011.md` were untracked in the working tree;
  this PR commits them verbatim. (They are standalone operational docs, unrelated to the
  concurrent #540 unit-curation work.)

## Scope / safety

- **Docs only** — no code, config, or IaC changes.
- Branch is based on `origin/master` (via an isolated worktree) so the diff is exactly these
  11 added files and nothing from the concurrent `#540` feature branches.

Refs #560.

author: mcguinness
body:
## Summary

Three per-spec commits, one per draft, applying the editorial,
structural, and correctness work from the recent review cycle:

- **Migration profile** (`e6dcf25`) — IANA fixes (correct RFC 9493
  registry name; drop conflicting `sub_id` JWT re-registration),
  Token Exchange error-code split (`invalid_request` vs
  `invalid_grant` per RFC 7522 §2.1.1), scope-envelope rewrite per
  RFC 6749 §3.3, perspective-neutral `saml_idp_entity_id`
  description so Bridge and IdP can reuse it, `# Migration Binding
  Rationale` renamed to `# Binding and Issuance Model` for
  family-level consistency, `# Authorization and Consent Model`
  demoted to a subsection, padding strength aligned with RFC 7522
  §2.1, ACR-mapping passthrough rule disambiguated, `sub_id`
  release rules consolidated, Overview section added (RFC 6749
  §1.2 style with diagram and lettered steps), abstract trimmed
  from 27 to 17 lines, terminology additions, RFC 9396 / 9449 /
  8705 informative references added.

- **Bridge profile** (`4285b4b`) — NameID derivation collision fix
  (replaced non-injective `":"`-separated SHA-256 input with a
  JWS-style segment encoding using `base64url`-per-field and `.`
  separator, with a domain-separation tag for version headroom),
  `InResponseTo` MUST omit (not SHOULD) for unsolicited
  assertions, `aud`/`azp` validation consolidated and split by
  flow, Token Exchange error-code split per RFC 7522 §2.1.1,
  freshness window MUST (not SHOULD), `max_age=0` semantics
  clarified, `@AllowCreate` scoped to persistent NameID formats,
  transient NameID requires 128 bits of entropy, `state` value
  MUST be integrity-protected, `AuthnRequest/Scoping` rejected
  with `NoSupportedIDP` instead of silently ignored, Token
  Exchange session-termination gap addressed,
  `AudienceRestriction` no longer requires sole `Audience`,
  Overview section added (two diagrams for the two modes),
  abstract trimmed from 29 to 16 lines, four example
  contradictions fixed.

- **IdP-backed OP profile** (`31c9db5`) — `SameSite=Lax` cookie
  fallback fixed (the SAML Response ACS POST is cross-site and
  does not carry Lax cookies; mandates `SameSite=None;Secure`),
  `max_age > 0` enforcement added (OP MUST treat as upper bound
  on `AuthnInstant`), `RequestedAuthnContext/@Comparison`
  required per IdP-Binding policy (default SHOULD `"exact"`),
  AuthnRequest signing now binding-specific per SAML 2.0
  Bindings (detached for HTTP-Redirect, enveloped for
  HTTP-POST), multi-valued `AuthnContextClassRef` selection rule
  defined, NameID reassignment detection required, ID Token
  `exp` constraints versus SAML times specified, OIDC Session
  Management explicitly out of scope, Multi-IdP per-IdP issuer
  aliasing permitted with explicit metadata/JWKS/rotation rules,
  SLO `LogoutResponse` signing requirements specified, `OIDC RP
  Authorization` Security Considerations section now references
  the canonical authorization-basis rules instead of restating,
  `# Multi-IdP Deployments` trimmed to a reading-aid
  cross-reference, `## Issuance Authorization` renamed
  `## Authorization Basis and Release Policy`, Overview section
  added (RFC 6749 §1.2 style with diagram and lettered steps),
  Unicode arrow replaced with ASCII, `sub_id` correctly
  attributed to RFC 9493, terminology additions.

## Verification

- All three drafts build clean (`make clean && make`):
  kramdown-rfc → xml2rfc-txt → xml2rfc-html all OK.
- No stale cross-references: every anchor removed from `main`
  (`#migration-binding-rationale`, `#saml-key-material`,
  `#iana-security-event-identifier-formats`, `#flow-overview`)
  has zero remaining `{{xref}}` references in the branch.
- All IANA registry values used in the body of any draft remain
  registered or are appropriately deferred with editor's notes.
- Normative-keyword counts (MUST/SHOULD/MAY): Migration 466→417,
  Bridge 297→282, IdP 228→247 (IdP gains 19 normatives from new
  security/correctness rules; Migration and Bridge lose 49 / 15
  from editorial consolidation, all consolidations verified as
  intentional with no rule lost).

## Test plan

- [ ] Spot-check the Overview sections in all three drafts.
- [ ] Spot-check the IANA section in Migration (Subject
      Identifier Formats registration vs the old Security Event
      Identifier Formats heading).
- [ ] Verify the Bridge NameID derivation formula renders
      correctly in the published HTML/PDF.
- [ ] Verify the IdP `<->` ASCII arrow renders as intended in
      the published text output.

## Summary

Commits the end-to-end SSE stress harness that drove the bug-find loop on PRs #35/#38/#39. These are the tests that **actually catch real-world regressions** — the bugs landed in PR #39 (single-column CSV corruption, missing \`random\` whitelist) were found by these scripts, not by the unit suite.

## What's in

- \`scripts/testing/stress/run_data_analysis_stress_v1.py\` — 12 datasets × simple questions
- \`scripts/testing/stress/run_data_analysis_stress_v2.py\` — 15 datasets × harder questions (multi-classifier ROC, 5-fold CV, PCA, time-series forecast, multi-chart composite, adversarial non-existent columns)
- \`docs/testing/stress_datasets/\` — 12 representative CSVs covering: CSV-sniff edges, UCI European format, no-numeric, NaN-heavy, PII columns, datetime, classic ML
- \`docs/testing/stress_datasets/README.md\` — usage + historical baselines

## Baseline (post-PR-#39 on main)

| Suite | PASS | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| v1 simple | 12/12 | every CSV shape works |
| v2 hard | 14/15 | the '1 fail' is graceful 'column not found' explanation, system behavior is correct |

## Why this matters

The unit tests gave 0 false positives on the bugs that #39 fixed because:
- Single-column CSV bug only fired with real \`pd.read_csv(sep=None, engine='python')\` on real numeric data
- Missing-\`random\`-import only fired when LLM obeyed the random_state prompt mandate

These harnesses authenticate via real JWT, hit the real SSE endpoint, parse the full result envelope, and classify by inspecting generated code + chart presence — not by HTTP status. Future regressions will surface here.

## Summary

The Daily Tens block in the "My scores in …" clipboard recap was rendering as a bare 6-digit number (e.g. `944415`) instead of the 🏆/❌ grid. Root cause: Daily Tens has no `score_regex` on its item, so the backend's "first number anywhere in text" fallback pulled the referral id off the trailing `dailytens.com/?ref=<id>` URL param and stored it as `score_value`. For URL-only shares, the recap formatter stripped the URL and then fell through to `String(scoreValue)`, surfacing the artifact.

Three changes:

- **`backfill-score-regex.ts`**: add Daily Tens entry capturing the puzzle number (`DailyTens\s*#(\d+)`) so `score_value` is anchored to the share itself, not the URL. Idempotent — run against prod to overwrite the bad rows.
- **`scoresSummary.summarizeScoreBody`**: when `scoreRaw` is non-empty but both per-game formatter and generic fallback strip it to nothing, return `null` instead of falling through to `String(scoreValue)`. That number is the URL artifact from above and shouldn't surface as the user's score. The existing `scoreRaw is null → fall back to scoreValue` path is preserved (still useful for hand-entered numeric scores).
- **`dailytens` formatter**: require at least one 🏆/❌ line. Defense-in-depth — without this a stray bare digit would slip through as the "grid."

## Test plan

author: sarthakb11
body:
## Summary

Adds optional `limit` and `offset` query params to `GET /sessions/{session_id}` so clients can fetch session history in chunks instead of receiving the full conversation inline (#9358).

- `limit`: maximum messages to return, counted back from the most recent.
- `offset`: messages to skip from the most recent before applying `limit`.
- Both optional. When neither is set the response is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `message_count` on `Session` still reflects the full conversation length so clients know when to stop paging.

Param shape follows the existing `SessionsQuery` pattern in `crates/goose-server/src/routes/schedule.rs` (`utoipa::IntoParams`, camelCase via `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`). Picked `offset` over a cursor token because the issue left the cursor anchor open and `offset` keeps the change minimal without locking in an opaque token format. A cursor variant can layer on later without breaking this one.

Slicing happens at the route layer over the `Conversation` returned by `SessionManager::get_session`, via a pure `paginate_messages` helper, so no core-crate changes. The helper clamps oversized `limit`/`offset` and preserves chronological order.

`ui/desktop/openapi.json` regenerated via `just generate-openapi`; the only delta is the two new query params on this route.

### Testing

- `cargo test -p goose-server --lib session::tests`: 4/4 pass (full history, limit-only, offset paging, oversized clamp).
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p goose-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

### Related Issues

Closes #9358

This PR addresses an issue where the minimize button and double-click-to-minimize gesture were missing from the `layout-handler` path in `chrome_layout.go`. The scaffolder only patched `storeName`/`storeSlug`. Everything else kept the upstream template's Teloz identity:

author: kidiatoliny
body:
## Summary
- The `keyring` crate (3.x) reaches the macOS keychain via the Security framework FFI. Under macOS hardened runtime, that path reports successful writes but the entry does not persist across launches. Every boot generates a fresh AES key, the previously encrypted token can no longer be decrypted, and the host app loses login state on every restart.
- Replaces the dependency with a per-platform shell-out that mirrors the strategy `onyx-rs` and `zalando/go-keyring` already use successfully in `Spectra` and other Foundation apps.

## Backends
- macOS: `security add-generic-password -U` / `find-generic-password -w` / `delete-generic-password`
- Linux: `secret-tool store --label=<svc>` / `lookup` / `clear`
- Windows: `cmdkey /generic` for write/delete, `Get-StoredCredential` (CredentialManager PowerShell module) for read

`TokenKeyring`'s public API is unchanged, so consumers only bump the SDK version.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --features desktop -- --test-threads=1` (all green, including a round-trip test that writes/reads/deletes a unique service entry against the real backend on the current OS)
- [ ] Tag v1.5.1, bump in unified-dev, ship v0.12.3, verify the keychain entry written by the signed bundle survives a relaunch and sync errors stop.

author: jeancarlosmolossi
body:
## Summary

Implements `vkc uninstall <package>` to fully reverse a previous installation.

## What this does

- Removes files that were **created** during install (tracked via `created_files` in `.ai-setup/installed.yaml`)
- Restores **backup files** if a backup was made during install with `--conflict-action backup-and-overwrite`
- Removes managed VKC blocks from `AGENTS.md` files (by agent name, not package name)
- Removes the installation record from `.ai-setup/installed.yaml`
- Supports `--dry-run` to preview without applying

## Key design decisions

- **`AgentBlocks` struct** stores `{Path, AgentName}` — the block removal key (agent name like `kalika-reviewer`) differs from the package name (like `basic-kalika-pack`)
- **`AGENTS.md` excluded from `CreatedFiles`** — shared config files are handled via `RemoveManagedBlock`, never via `os.Remove`
- **Uninstall order**: block removal → backup restore → file deletion → state write (state written last for retryability)
- **`RemoveManagedBlock` is idempotent** — returns nil for absent file or absent block

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/state/installed.go` | Add `CreatedFiles`, `AgentBlock` struct, `AgentBlocks` fields |
| `internal/app/install.go` | Populate `CreatedFiles` and `AgentBlocks` during install |
| `internal/installer/merge.go` | Add `RemoveManagedBlock(targetPath, agentName)` |
| `internal/installer/merge_test.go` | 4 sub-tests for `RemoveManagedBlock` |
| `internal/app/uninstall.go` | New: `Uninstall()` function |
| `internal/app/uninstall_test.go` | New: 7 integration sub-tests |
| `internal/cli/uninstall_cmd.go` | New: Cobra command with `--dry-run` |
| `internal/cli/root.go` | Register `newUninstallCmd()` |
| `README.md` | Document `vkc uninstall`, remove stale limitation note |
| `.github/skills/go-reversible-install-state/SKILL.md` | New reusable skill |

## Tests

- `TestRemoveManagedBlock`: 4/4 PASS (existing, idempotent, preserve other content, file absent)
- `TestUninstall`: 7/7 PASS (created files, backup, managed block, agent name, state record, not found, idempotent)
- `go test ./...`: all 15 packages pass

author: comwanga
body:
… for Miri compat

x509-cert, der, p256, ecdsa, serde_json, and base64 were unconditional dependencies compiled even under --no-default-features. Under Miri with -Zmiri-strict-provenance these trigger UB/leak false-positives (p256 uses subtle constant-time arithmetic; serde_json initialises global state).

All code using these deps is already gated behind #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]. Making them optional and tying them to the alloc feature keeps them out of the no-default-features Miri run while preserving full functionality under std / alloc builds.

author: lukasingemarsson
body:
## Problem

The test suite was non-hermetic and order-dependent on macOS — `go test ./...` failures shifted with test order, and a contributor's local config/cwd state could flip any run red. Three independent causes:

1. **HOME/config reads** — keybinding tests (`Ctrl+P`/`O`/`Z`) read the developer's real `~/.config/ask/ask.json` via `currentKeyMap`, so custom or unbound shortcuts failed them.
2. **macOS temp-dir symlinks** — `t.TempDir()` lives under `/var` (a symlink to `/private/var`), but production resolves cwd via `filepath.EvalSymlinks` (`memoryProjectRoot`). The mismatch keyed seeded vs. read project config under different roots, failing the `workflow_*` MCP tests (and an `index out of range` panic that was masking later failures).
3. **cwd leakage** — production `os.Chdir` (`closeTab`, the `cd` handler, shell mode) left the process in a temp dir, breaking later relative-path tests (e.g. the usage-plugin file reads).

## Fix (test-only, all in `testhelpers_test.go`)

- A package `TestMain` points `$HOME`/`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` at a throwaway dir, so config reads fall back to compiled defaults; it also invalidates the keymap cache and restores cwd at the suite boundary.
- `isolateHome` resolves the temp dir through `filepath.EvalSymlinks` so seeded and read project-config keys agree.
- `newTestModel` captures cwd and restores it via `t.Cleanup`.

## Verification

`go test ./...` is green in default order and under `-shuffle` (seeds 1/42/9999 + random), 1729 passed.

body:
## Summary

Reduce la latencia de `/api/clientes/:cod/historial-compras` para cargas repetidas, sin tocar la lógica de agregación.

- **Backend** (`server-lib/historialCompras.ts`): cache RAM del response ya armado, key = `cod_cliente`, TTL 5 min (alineado con el TTL del mes actual de `snapshotCache`). El permiso se valida SIEMPRE antes de tocar el cache, así que servir cacheado no filtra datos. Primera carga igual (~400ms), segunda en adelante (cualquier vendedor, mismo cliente) ~0ms de cómputo.
- **Frontend** (`VendorShell.tsx`): cache compartido por `cod_cliente` a nivel de módulo. Hoy cada `ClienteObjetivoCard` tenía su propio state y volver a un cliente refetcheaba. Ahora una reapertura del mismo cliente (dentro de 5 min) arranca con la data ya cargada, sin spinner y sin pegarle al server.

Nota: el cold-start post-deploy (cache de `snapshotCache` vacío) sigue igual — eso lo mitiga el prewarm existente (`server.ts`, boot warm + cron horario). Este PR ataca la latencia de uso repetido, que es el caso real del vendedor moviéndose entre clientes.

author: supremecommanderhedgehog
body:
## Summary

Fourth of the five initial ADR 0002 transforms. Prepends an 8-byte big-endian u64 timestamp to the payload so downstream consumers see `[timestamp][original payload]` and don't need their own clock.

Closes #82. Built on the pipeline scaffolding from #79.

## Config

```toml
[[destinations.transforms]]
type  = "prepend_timestamp"
clock = "epoch_ns"        # or "monotonic_ns"
```

## Clock semantics

| Clock          | Source                  | Drift behavior | Cross-destination correlation |
|----------------|-------------------------|----------------|-------------------------------|
| `epoch_ns`     | `SystemTime::now()`     | Subject to NTP slews; drops if clock is pre-1970 | OK — same wall clock everywhere |
| `monotonic_ns` | `Instant::now()` minus per-transform first-use anchor | Stable across wall-clock changes | Not comparable across transforms — each anchors independently |

## Byte order

Big-endian (network byte order), so the prefix is portable across architectures without extra annotation.

## Allocation

`PrependTimestamp` always allocates an `8 + payload.len()` BytesMut. No way around it since the payload is growing.

## Tests

- Four unit tests: epoch prefix matches current system time within a tight before/after window; monotonic prefix is non-decreasing across two back-to-back calls; monotonic first-use anchor is sub-second; `build_pipeline` construction round-trips.

## Docs

- `MANUAL.md` Transforms section gains a `prepend_timestamp` subsection covering clock semantics, drift, and allocation.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green.
- [ ] Local: `cargo test --no-default-features --lib transforms` shows 19 passing tests (verified).

The MCP tools accept simple `LocalDate startDate` / `LocalDate endDate` parameters; a private helper translates them into the React Admin `filter` JSON shape (`{"startDate":"...","endDate":"..."}`) that the existing services consume. This keeps the MCP surface clean while reusing the production services unchanged.

Ports the secrets-scan **preflight** hook to the runtime-neutral `.agent0/` surface (`git mv .claude/hooks/secrets-scan.sh → .agent0/hooks/secrets-preflight.sh`) so Claude Code and Codex CLI run the same `PreToolUse(Bash)` commit-shape gate — continuing the multi-runtime hook migration (106 delegation, 107 governance). The preflight gates commit *shape* and bridges the `# OVERRIDE:` marker to the native `.githooks/pre-commit` gitleaks scanner via `CLAUDE_SECRETS_OVERRIDE_REASON`; it runs no gitleaks itself. Renamed because "scan" was materially false for this layer.

Key design (from a converged cross-model debate, `docs/specs/108-*/debate.md`): **runtime-aware override output** — Codex requires `permissionDecision:"allow"` alongside `updatedInput`, Claude keeps `updatedInput`-only (so it doesn't bypass the permission prompt) — branched via `memory_runtime()`; project root via `memory_project_dir()`; non-commit Bash now silent (no `skip-not-commit` flood under the broad matcher); audit → `.agent0/secrets-audit.jsonl` + `runtime` provenance field (hard cutover).

## The headline finding (V8 live dogfood)

The original Claude registration narrowed with `if: "Bash(git commit *|git commit|...)"`. **Pipe-alternation inside a single `Bash(...)` is not valid Claude Code permission-rule syntax** — `|` is a shell command separator there, not an alternation operator (verified vs the official permissions docs). The pattern matched nothing, so the Claude preflight was **dormant** — zero `claude-code` rows ever — even though 11/11 harness scenario tests + direct invocation all passed (none of them exercise CC's real `if`-filter evaluation). A live PreToolUse dogfood through the Bash tool is what surfaced it.

**Fix:** drop the `if`, use a bare `"matcher": "Bash"` (mirrors governance-gate and the Codex `^Bash$` registration; the script already self-filters on non-commit).

## Verification (live, both runtimes, 2026-05-28)

- **Codex:** block + override rewrite reached Bash/native git.
- **Claude (cold-started, post-fix):** compound `git add && git commit` blocked (`reject-shape`/`compound-and`/`claude-code`); override commit of a fake-key fixture landed end-to-end (preflight `override-pass-through` + native `override`/`finding_count:1`), proving the env-var bridge reaches gitleaks on Claude.
- 11/11 secrets-scan scenario tests, latency baseline, harness-sync suites green; `grep -rn` clean of stale `.claude/hooks/secrets-scan.sh` refs.

## Follow-up flagged

The **supply-chain** registration (`if: "Bash(npm *|pnpm *|...)"`, settings.json) carries the **same latent `if`-pipe bug** → it's firing on nothing today. Must be fixed (drop `if` → bare matcher) during the spec-109 supply-chain port. The two `hook-chain-*` memory files are reconciled accordingly (the "~70ms if-narrowing saving" was illusory — a dormant hook, not narrowing).

## Summary

Your `ck worktree rebuild-image` was failing at step 3/11 with `sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match` on the uv installer. Both pinned installer SHAs in the Dockerfile had drifted upstream since 2026-04-30, and while we're in here, swap the Claude Code install to the `@latest` channel so containers track the same release stream as the Homebrew `claude-code@latest` cask.

## Three changes

1. **`UV_INSTALLER_SHA256`** refreshed `facbed3...` → `d79d834...`. `astral.sh/uv/install.sh` drifted; this is what made the build fail.
2. **`CLAUDE_INSTALLER_SHA256`** refreshed `b315b46...` → `005ec1a...`. The Anthropic bootstrap also drifted in the same window.
3. **`bash /tmp/install.sh`** → **`bash /tmp/install.sh latest`**. The bootstrap script accepts a positional channel argument (`stable` | `latest` | a specific semver) that gets forwarded to `claude install <target>`. Passing `latest` mirrors the host install when CLI users have done `brew install --cask claude-code@latest` (stable cask lags @latest by ~a week).

From-scratch build with `--build-arg CACHEBUST=$(date +%s)`:
- All 11/11 steps succeeded

author: tomsilver
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `robot_id` parameter to `SingleArmPyBulletRobot.__init__` that lets an instance **bind to an already-loaded PyBullet body** instead of loading its own URDF.

This is foundational infrastructure for the upcoming bimanual Dexmate Vega robot: a multi-arm robot will load a single shared body once, then expose each arm as a `SingleArmPyBulletRobot` (with its own `arm_joints` / end effector) over that shared `robot_id`. Exposing arms this way lets existing consumers — `inverse_kinematics(robot.left_arm, ...)`, `run_motion_planning(robot.left_arm, ...)` — work unchanged.

## Behavior

When `robot_id` is provided:
- skips `p.loadURDF` (and the self-collision flag computation, which is a body-level decision owned by whoever loads the body);
- skips applying `base_pose` and skips the initial `set_joints(home)` reset — the owner of the shared body controls the initial posture;
- skips the IKFast-with-custom-URDF warning.

The home-limits assertion is preserved: it validates each view's home against its own `joint_lower_limits` (derived from its `arm_joints`).

Default behavior (`robot_id=None`) is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `./run_ci_checks.sh` passes locally (77 tests; +1).
- [x] New `test_single_arm_robot_bind_to_existing_body`: binds a second Panda to an existing body and asserts no new body is loaded, `robot_id`/`arm_joints` match, the bound instance leaves a pre-set non-home configuration untouched, and FK agrees with the original.

# Phase 7 Final Test Report

Generated: 2026-05-28T21:45:07.153388+00:00

## Scope

This report covers the Phase 7 staging validation for:

- Category wizard and simplified prompt manager
- One prompt per category/language output
- Gemini structured AI output
- Gemini fallback model behavior
- Telegram review and publish flow
- Social media processing for X/Twitter and Instagram
- Multi-photo handling
- Telegram-safe video preparation

## Branch

`test/dashboard-phase7-category-wizard-prompts`

## Environment

Staging Worker:

`https://ai-curation-publisher-agent-staging.mpourebadi.workers.dev`

## Key fixes validated

### 1. AI output validation

Problem found:

`sourceAttributionText` was required to be a non-empty string, but the product requirement allows it to be empty when the source URL should not be shown in the caption.

Fix:

`sourceAttributionText` is now allowed to be an empty string.

Result:

AI outputs now persist as valid generated outputs instead of falling back to:

`تولید کپشن این پست کامل نشد...`

### 2. Gemini fallback model

Problem found:

`gemini-2.5-flash` may intermittently return 503/high-demand errors.

Fix:

Gemini provider can fall back to:

`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`

Result:

Recent staging outputs show successful generation with both:

- `gemini-2.5-flash`
- `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`

### 3. X/Twitter multi-photo handling

Problem found:

Some X multi-photo posts were downloaded as short still video wrappers and then uploaded to Telegram as video/document-like files.

Fixes:

- Detect still-video wrappers
- Extract first frame as JPEG
- Upload converted stills as Telegram `photo`, not document
- Preserve multi-asset media group metadata

Result:

X multi-photo test now stores assets as:

- `kind: photo`
- `telegramFileType: photo`
- Telegram file IDs beginning with photo-style IDs

### 4. Instagram video playback

Problem found:

Some Instagram reels uploaded to Telegram played with audio while the image stayed frozen.

Fix:

Added Telegram-safe video compatibility checks and transcode path for incompatible video characteristics.

Result:

Instagram 60fps reels are detected as requiring safe transcode.

### 5. fps=30 enforcement for Telegram-safe transcode

Problem found:

The pipeline could mark a video as Telegram-safe-transcoded while still reporting `preparedFrameRate: 60`.

Fix in this patch:

When `transcode_video(..., reason="telegram_safe")` runs, the ffmpeg filter now includes:

`fps=30`

Result expected:

New Telegram-safe transcodes should report:

- `preparedFrameRate <= 30`
- `preparedPixelFormat: yuv420p`
- `preparedVideoCodec: h264`

## Regression test set

### Text-only post

Input:

`برای تست: بیت‌کوین امروز دوباره بالای محدوده مهم بازار معامله می‌شود و معامله‌گران منتظر شکست مقاومت بعدی هستند.`

Expected:

- Persian output
- No fallback
- No media job required

### X video

URL:

`https://x.com/i/status/2057120818551734589`

Expected:

- `telegramFileType: video`
- No aspect drift
- Playable in Telegram

### X multi-photo

URL:

`https://x.com/i/status/2055414662116585612`

Expected:

- `assetCount: 3`
- all assets `telegramFileType: photo`
- no document upload
- no black video wrappers

### Instagram 60fps reel

URL:

`https://www.instagram.com/reel/DVZtZunjev9/?igsh=MW05ZjFnc2FrbTlrbQ==`

Expected after this patch:

- `telegramSafeVideoTranscodeRequired: true`
- `transcoded: true`
- `preparedFrameRate <= 30`

### Instagram 30fps reel

URL:

`https://www.instagram.com/reel/DYFSaPnxFQq/?igsh=YzMyeGw2aWg2bGg5`

Expected:

- `telegramSafeVideoTranscodeRequired: false`
- avoid unnecessary heavy transcode
- playable in Telegram

## Debug policy

Raw AI/debug capture should remain available in code paths because it was critical for identifying the validation issue quickly.

Do not remove debug capability.

Future cleanup should move raw AI diagnostics into `provider_logs` / `prompt_runs` rather than user-facing caption fields.

- Move AI raw debug payloads from generated output fields into dedicated observability tables.
- Add dashboard-only debug inspection for AI validation failures.
- Consider staging cron override for faster publish testing.
- Prepare PR and merge after final publish verification.

body:
## Summary

Proof-of-concept that wraps the existing 100% client-side app as a native desktop app, producing a Windows `.exe` installer. The app needs no backend and has no native modules, so this is just a thin Electron shell around the static build.

- **`electron/main.cjs`** — Electron main process. Loads the built bundle over `file://` (or the live Vite dev server when `ELECTRON_START_URL` is set), opens external links (e.g. the UNI SIM navbar) in the system browser, and runs the renderer sandboxed (`contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`).
- **New `desktop` Vite mode** — builds with a relative `base` (`./`) and skips the PWA service worker, so assets resolve under `file://`. The hosted web build is unchanged (`/pdf/` base + service worker still emitted).
- **electron-builder config** in `package.json` — emits an NSIS Windows installer to `release/`.

### New scripts

```sh
npm run build:desktop   # build the web bundle for Electron (relative base, no SW)
npm run electron        # run the packaged-style app against that build
npm run dist:win        # build + produce the Windows installer in release/
```

## What was verified (headless Linux)

- `npm run build:desktop` succeeds; `dist/index.html` references assets relatively (`./assets/...`, `./favicon.svg`).
- The pdf.js worker resolves via `new URL("pdf.worker...", import.meta.url)`, i.e. relative to the script — correct under `file://`.
- `npm run build` (web) still emits `sw.js` + `manifest.webmanifest` with the `/pdf/` base — no regression to the hosted PWA.

## Not verified here / follow-ups

- **The actual window launch and the `.exe` packaging were not run** — this container has no display and the Electron binary download was skipped. `npm run dist:win` must run on **Windows (or Linux/macOS + Wine)** and downloads the Electron binary (~100 MB) on first run.
- Worth confirming on Windows that the module worker loads from `file://` (it normally does in Electron); the fallback is a custom protocol or a tiny embedded HTTP server.
- Optional polish: code signing, a dedicated `.ico` (electron-builder currently auto-converts `public/unisim-icon.png`), and a CI job to build the installer.

## Test plan

- [ ] On Windows: `npm install && npm run dist:win`, run the generated installer from `release/`, open/annotate/sign/export a PDF.
- [ ] Confirm external navbar links open in the default browser.
- [ ] Confirm the hosted web app + PWA install still work (unchanged build path).

author: youtalk
body:
## Description

Lowest-risk first step of a per-package quality campaign on autoware_core. The public API/ABI is unchanged.

- **test**: cover the previously-untested `KalmanFilter` validation FALSE branches (init/predict/update dimension guards), the state/covariance getters, a closed-form numerical-equivalence update check on a correlated covariance, and the `TimeDelayKalmanFilter::updateWithDelay` rejection paths (non-column `y`, non-square `R`, `R`/`C` row mismatch, non-PD → LLT failure), capturing stderr to keep test output clean. Tests: 11 → 24.
- **perf**: mirror the optimization already used in `TimeDelayKalmanFilter::updateWithDelay` in the base `KalmanFilter::update`: compute the Kalman gain with a Cholesky (LLT) solve of the innovation covariance `S = C P Cᵀ + R` instead of an explicit matrix inverse. Use `noalias()` in `predict(x_next, A, Q)` to drop intermediate Eigen temporaries.

## Related links

**Parent Issue:**

- autowarefoundation/autoware_core#1096 (autoware_core refactoring campaign)

## How was this PR tested?

- `colcon test --packages-select autoware_kalman_filter` → 24/24 tests pass (was 11), all package linters green.
- `pre-commit run --files ...` → clang-format and cpplint clean.
- Numerical equivalence vs the previous implementation, measured over 200,000 random systems:
  - `predict()` is **bit-identical** (max `|ΔP|` = 0).
  - `update()` for valid (positive-definite) inputs differs only at round-off: worst-case `|Δx| ≤ 4.7e-15`, `|ΔP| ≤ 2.1e-14` (machine epsilon ≈ 2.2e-16).

## Notes for reviewers

Two commits, each independently green: `test:` adds characterization coverage first, then `perf:` applies the Cholesky solve (a RED test for the new fail-safe guard precedes the implementation). The gain formula `K = P Cᵀ S⁻¹` is unchanged; only the linear-solve method changes.

## Interface changes

None. Public method signatures and the `bool` return contract are unchanged.

## Effects on system behavior

Only the base `KalmanFilter::predict(x_next, A, Q)` and `update(...)` are touched; `TimeDelayKalmanFilter::predictWithDelay`/`updateWithDelay` are unchanged.

- `predict()` is bit-identical to the previous implementation (`noalias()` only avoids a temporary allocation).
- `update()` keeps the same gain formula; for valid positive-definite inputs the result changes only at floating-point round-off (≤ ~2e-14, see above). For a **non-positive-definite** innovation covariance, `update()` now returns `false` (fail-safe) instead of silently applying a meaningless finite gain that could corrupt downstream state.

Consumers:
- `autoware_ekf_localizer` (Core) uses only `predictWithDelay`/`updateWithDelay` → unaffected.
- Universe trackers (`autoware_multi_object_tracker`, `autoware_radar_object_tracker`, `autoware_bytetrack`) call the base `predict`/`update`; the impact is the ~1e-14 round-off above, and all of them already check the `bool` return and skip the update on `false`, so the new fail-safe path is strictly safer for them.

## youtalk fork CI — build-and-test all green

The full `build-test-tidy-pr` workflow runs on the youtalk fork (`ubicloud-standard-16`). All build-and-test gate jobs pass for head commit `7225bd599` ([workflow run](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124)):

- ✅ `build-and-test-diff-humble / build-and-test-diff` — https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124/job/78402763440
- ✅ `build-and-test-diff-jazzy / build-and-test-diff` — https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124/job/78402763447
- ✅ `build-and-test-diff-jazzy-agnocast / build-and-test-diff` — https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124/job/78402763421
- ✅ `build-and-test-diff-humble / clang-tidy-diff` — https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124/job/78403103611
- ✅ `build-and-test-diff-jazzy / clang-tidy-diff` — https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_core/actions/runs/26606488124/job/78403136345

(The `*-above` universe jobs are bonus coverage and excluded from the gate.)

author: forkwright
body:
Closes #4119.

## Background

aletheia#4119 disclosed `crates/koina/src/redact.rs` as containing a live OpenAI API key. Cross-validation by 3 independent reviewers (cross-validate run `20260528T212800Z`) revealed the string is the alphabetically-sequential synthetic fixture `sk-proj-abcdefghij1234567890abcdef` used by the redactor's own self-test, not a real credential. All 5 occurrences across koina + nous are properly annotated with `kanon:ignore SECURITY/hardcoded-openai-api-key` (kanon's own scanner skips them), but third-party scanners (gitleaks, trufflehog, etc.) re-flag the same fixtures because they don't recognize kanon's annotation syntax.

The operator rotated the OpenAI key at the dashboard out of caution before cross-validation; verified no actual leak after.

## Change

Add `gitleaks:allow` + `trufflehog:ignore` directives alongside the existing `kanon:ignore` tag on the 5 fixture lines:

- `crates/koina/src/redact.rs` line 50 (sk-ant-api03 fixture)
- `crates/koina/src/redact.rs` line 57 (sk-proj fixture)
- `crates/koina/src/redacting_layer.rs` line 288 (sk-proj fixture in tracing field)
- `crates/nous/src/training/pii.rs` lines 338, 341 (sk-proj fixture for PII detection test)

Comment-only; zero behavior change. Each fixture remains alphabetically-sequential (low entropy) and is inside `#[cfg(test)]` or test-only code paths.

## Why this is the fix (not history rewrite)

Cross-validate captured the convergent finding: the disclosure was a scanner false positive. A path-scoped `git-filter-repo` would have:
- Targeted the wrong commit (the disclosure cited f1fcff8 which actually touches `.github/workflows/llm-regen.yml`, not redact.rs)
- Missed 4 of the 5 fixture occurrences (path scope only covered redact.rs)
- Cost: 97 tag SHA rewrites, 7 PR rebases, signed-commit chain invalidation, active agent worktree desync
- Achieved: zero security benefit (no real credential to scrub)

Per the standing posture (PHILOSOPHY.md §Presence): the work is true at every level — the comment names what's actually there (synthetic test fixture; multi-scanner ignore directive) rather than performing security theater via history rewrite.

## Verification

author: csturzaker
body:
## Goal

Build the empty state for when filters return zero voices, and write the canonical Playwright E2E suite for the squad page.

Part of **DEV-56** (Epic: The Full Squad page) — the last of the three. Builds on DEV-60/61.

## Empty state

When the active filters match no voices, the grid renders a friendly, actionable empty state instead of a blank grid:
- Amber search-with-x icon, heading, supporting copy, and **two escape routes** — "Reset filters" (primary) and "Browse all voices" (ghost, → clean `/squad`).
- Reset clears **in place**: it dispatches a new `squad:filters-reset` event that the filter bar (the source of truth) listens for and clears against, re-broadcasting so the grid re-fills. No reload.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Empty state renders when filters return zero
- [x] All E2E pass locally (and will in CI)
- [x] Total runtime <60s — the squad suites run in **~30s**
- [x] No flaky tests (deterministic fixture surface; `openFilter` gates on hydration)

E2E cases (`tests/e2e/squad.spec.ts`): page loads + header/count, cold-load skeleton, grid hydration, 24-tile first page, load-more (+24 then retire), load-more focus, theme filter narrows, country intersection, URL updates + reload preserves, reset clears, filtered tile links (`from=squad&theme=…`), empty state renders, empty-state reset CTA, keyboard focusable, axe (desktop + mobile via the 3 projects), and 3/6/8 columns.

## ⚠️ Two deviations from the issue (flagged, consistent with DEV-60/61)

1. **Empty state is React, not `EmptyState.astro`.** It has to mount/unmount on client-side filter state, which an Astro component can't do from inside the grid island — same constraint that made `RotationTile` a React port. Lives at `src/islands/SquadEmptyState.tsx`.
2. **Copy is the issue's, container is the prototype's.** The prototype's empty-state paragraph is a filter-specific illustration ("…Spanish-speaking young people in Argentina writing about belonging…") — not literal copy. I used the issue's generic, shippable heading/paragraph + two CTAs, with the prototype's visual treatment (dashed `rule` border, `paper-2` card, 28px uppercase team-sheet heading, 15px/44ch body). The issue adds the amber icon (no conflict).

## Test-suite consolidation

`squad.spec.ts` is the canonical regression guard. To avoid duplication and keep runtime down, I **folded in and removed** the per-feature `squad-grid.spec.ts` and `squad-load-more.spec.ts` from DEV-60/61 — their unique cases (cold-load skeleton, 3/6/8 columns, load-more focus) are preserved in `squad.spec.ts`. The focused **`squad-filters.spec.ts`** (popover / roving-key / escape mechanics) and **`squad-url.spec.ts`** (serialization, back/forward, invalid params) remain as lower-level suites. The load-more demo was bumped 40 → 56 voices for a clean two-click pagination journey.

## Data note

`/squad` data-shape assertions derive counts from the `#squad-data` block (the live pipeline publishes only a few voices today), so they're robust to upstream content. Pagination/filter intersections run against the deterministic 56-voice `/demo/squad-load-more`.

## Local validation

`pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `pnpm test` (374) · `pnpm test:coverage` (96% lines) · `pnpm build` · squad e2e (87 across 3 browsers, ~30s) — all green.

Closes DEV-62

author: smatey
body:
This pull request implements the main UI for the messaging feature, introducing a complete, responsive chat interface with mock data. It adds all the key components for a sidebar with searchable conversations, an active chat window, message bubbles, and input handling. The changes are focused on building out the frontend structure, using placeholder/mock data for now, and setting up the components for future integration with backend services.

The most important changes are:

**Messaging UI Implementation:**

* Added a new messaging page (`mensajes/page.tsx`) that brings together the sidebar, chat window, and empty state, using mock data and React state to manage active conversations.
* Created the main chat sidebar (`chat-sidebar.tsx`) with search functionality and a scrollable, sorted list of conversations.
* Implemented the active chat window (`active-chat-window.tsx`), showing messages, participant info, and a message input footer.
* Added the chat empty state component for when no conversation is selected.

**Componentization and UI Details:**

* Developed reusable components:
  - `ChatListItem` for each conversation in the sidebar, with unread badges and dropdown actions.
  - `ChatMessageBubble` for displaying individual messages, with sent/received styles and read status.
  - `ChatInputFooter` for sending new messages, handling enter key and form submission.
  - `SearchInput` for searching conversations in the sidebar.

**Constants and Mock Data:**

* Defined `MESSAGES_UI_TEXT` constants for all UI text and placeholders, centralizing copy for easy updates and localization.

**Cleanup:**

* Removed placeholder files for unimplemented message components, as their functionality is now covered by the new components.

These changes lay the groundwork for a full-featured messaging system, with a modular and maintainable component structure, ready for backend integration.

author: proggeramlug
body:
Closes #1475.

## What

Adds `getSafeAreaInsets()` to `perry/system`:

```ts
import { getSafeAreaInsets } from "perry/system";
const { top, right, bottom, left } = getSafeAreaInsets();
```

Returns `{ top, right, bottom, left }` in points so apps building a custom top-of-screen / bottom-of-screen layout can position content correctly on every device class, instead of hardcoding magic numbers (`59` Dynamic Island, `34` home indicator) keyed on `__platform__` — which is wrong on 44pt-notch iPhones, iPad, and Android.

## How

- **Runtime** (`crates/perry-runtime/src/safe_area.rs`, new): `perry_safe_area_insets_make(top, right, bottom, left)` builds the `{top,right,bottom,left}` object and returns it NaN-boxed (modeled on `pointer_event.rs`). Centralizes the object layout in one place; each platform just computes four floats and calls it. The system-table row uses `ReturnKind::F64` since the value is already a NaN-boxed pointer (pass-through).
- **iOS** (real): reads `UIWindow.safeAreaInsets` off the key window; falls back to all-zero before the scene connects / in headless builds.
- **macOS, Windows, GTK4, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS**: report all-zero (no system safe area, or not yet wired) so the symbol links everywhere.
- **Android**: zero stub for now — a real `decorView.getRootWindowInsets().getInsets(WindowInsets.Type.systemBars())` JNI implementation is a tracked follow-up so the host-verifiable iOS path can land first.
- Wires the import into the UI-link trigger list (`collect_modules.rs`), adds the manifest entry + regenerated API docs, and the `.d.ts` `SafeAreaInsets` type.

## Validation

- `cargo build --release` for `perry-runtime`, `perry-dispatch`, `perry-api-manifest`, `perry-ui-macos`, `perry-stdlib`, `perry` — clean.
- `cargo build --release -p perry-ui-ios --target aarch64-apple-ios` — the real iOS implementation compiles.
- New unit test `safe_area_insets_layout_matches_documented_order` passes.
- End-to-end on the macOS host: `getSafeAreaInsets()` returns a real object; destructuring and `.top`/`.right`/`.bottom`/`.left` property access work (zeros on macOS, as expected).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; API docs regenerated (`api-docs-drift`).

Note: per the maintainer workflow, version bump + CHANGELOG entry are intentionally omitted from this branch to be folded in at merge.

author: margolinilya-create
body:
> Stacked поверх [#15 Phase 1a Next.js 15 upgrade](https://github.com/margolinilya-create/pnhd-studio-clone/pull/15). Сначала merge #14 → #15, потом этот PR.

## Summary

Payload CMS 3.85 scaffold через single-app integration. Старый `/admin` (Supabase + custom Server Actions) **не тронут** — Payload временно сидит на `/admin-payload`. В Phase 2b после миграции каталога делаем atomic swap.

## Что добавлено

**Dependencies:**
- `payload@3.85.0`, `@payloadcms/next@3.85`, `@payloadcms/db-postgres@3.85`, `@payloadcms/storage-s3@3.85`, `@payloadcms/richtext-lexical@3.85`, `@payloadcms/ui@3.85`, `graphql@^16.14`
- `cross-env@^7`, `tsx@^4.22` (dev)

**Payload config + collections:**
- [src/payload.config.ts](src/payload.config.ts) — Users + Media collections, S3 storage plugin, routes на `/admin-payload` + `/api-payload`
- [src/collections/Users.ts](src/collections/Users.ts) — `roles: select-multi[admin | brand_manager | marketing | operations | sales]` (расширим в Phase 2)
- [src/collections/Media.ts](src/collections/Media.ts) — upload-collection, `imageSizes` (thumbnail 400 / card 800 / hero 1920)
- [src/access/{isAdmin,hasRole}.ts](src/access/) — переиспользуемые access-helpers

**Next.js route handlers:**
- `src/app/(payload)/admin-payload/[[...segments]]/{page,not-found}.tsx` — Payload Admin UI через `@payloadcms/next/views`
- `src/app/(payload)/api-payload/{[...slug],graphql,graphql-playground}/route.ts` — REST + GraphQL
- `src/app/(payload)/layout.tsx` — RootLayout + handleServerFunctions
- `src/app/(payload)/admin-payload/importMap.js` — stub (генерится через `payload generate:importmap`)

**Infrastructure:**
- `next.config.mjs` обёрнут `withPayload(withSentryConfig(nextConfig, ...))`
- `tsconfig.json`: alias `@payload-config` + `target: ES2022` (для `import.meta.url` в payload.config)
- `.env.example`: `DATABASE_URI`, `PAYLOAD_SECRET`, `S3_*`, `PAYLOAD_BOOTSTRAP_*` (mib@pnhd.ru)
- `package.json` scripts: `payload`, `payload:seed`, `payload:gen-types`, `payload:gen-importmap`, `payload:migrate`, `payload:migrate:create`
- `scripts/seed-admin-user.ts` — bootstrap admin из ENV (идемпотентен)
- `supabase/migrations/20260529000001_payload_media_bucket.sql` — bucket `payload-media` (public read, write через S3 service-role keys)

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` зелёный
- [x] Payload routes в bundle:
  - `/admin-payload/[[...segments]]` — 642 kB First Load (изолирован в route group `(payload)`)
  - `/api-payload/[...slug]` — REST
  - `/api-payload/graphql` + `/api-payload/graphql-playground`
- [x] Storefront chunks без значимого роста (179 → 180 kB shared)
- [x] `npm test` — 35 passed
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [ ] (после merge на Vercel) выставить ENV: `DATABASE_URI`, `PAYLOAD_SECRET`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (остальные значения из `.env.example`)
- [ ] `npm run payload:gen-importmap` + `npm run payload:gen-types` локально с DB connection
- [ ] `npm run payload:seed` локально для создания admin `mib@pnhd.ru`
- [ ] Smoke `/admin-payload` → login форма → залогиниться → загрузить картинку в Media

## ⚠️ Что НЕ в этом PR (намеренно)

- **Реальный bootstrap admin user** — требует `DATABASE_URI` + `PAYLOAD_SECRET` в Vercel; запустишь `npm run payload:seed` после merge с заполненным `.env.local`
- **Реальная генерация `payload-types.ts` / `importMap.js`** — требует БД connection; файлы сейчас stub'ы (минимальный валидный TS), регенерируется при первом dev
- **DROP старого `/admin`** — это Phase 2b после миграции каталога в Payload

## Следующие шаги после merge

1. Vercel ENV: `DATABASE_URI` (Supabase Pooler session-mode), `PAYLOAD_SECRET` (`openssl rand -hex 32`), `S3_*` (Supabase Storage S3 keys)
2. Локально: `npm run payload:gen-types && npm run payload:gen-importmap && npm run payload:seed` → коммитим сгенерированные файлы
3. Phase 2a: `feat/payload-catalog` — products/variants/prices/categories collections + ETL из Supabase

body:
This pull request enhances the `EIPOH100` dashboard page by adding a new "Activity by Repo" donut chart, improving the recent activity feed's UI, and introducing utility functions for consistent labeling and time formatting. The main changes are grouped below:

**New Features:**

* Added a "Repo distribution donut" section that visualizes the share of PRs checked per repository type using an ECharts donut chart. This uses a derived `typeComparison` data structure and a new `pieOption` configuration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ac0e8f71f63ce172796dbe49579d2b7f191b277e4a02eafe2d2d1684e11770beR383-R434) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ac0e8f71f63ce172796dbe49579d2b7f191b277e4a02eafe2d2d1684e11770beR671-R712)

**UI/UX Improvements:**

* Redesigned the recent activity feed items for better clarity, including a two-line layout with actor, action, timestamp, title, repo tag, PR/proposal number, and a "View" link. The feed now uses more prominent cards and improved spacing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ac0e8f71f63ce172796dbe49579d2b7f191b277e4a02eafe2d2d1684e11770beL626-R771) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ac0e8f71f63ce172796dbe49579d2b7f191b277e4a02eafe2d2d1684e11770beL662-R829)
* Increased the height of skeleton loaders in the activity feed for better visual balance during loading states.

**Utility Functions:**

* Introduced `relativeTime` for human-readable timestamps (e.g., "just now", "2h ago") and `repoTagStyle` for consistent repo labeling and color styling across the UI.

These changes collectively improve the dashboard's data visualization, consistency, and overall user experience.
